content.text:
Found it — a classic PowerShell hex-literal signedness bug, and it's instructive. The real `LastTaskResult` is `UInt32 2147946720` (positive), but the literal `0x800710E0` parses as a **signed Int32 = -2147020576** (negative, high bit set), and `0xFFFFFFFF` parses as `-1` so my mask was a no-op. The self-test passed only because it fed the *same* negative literal to both sides — the live path feeds a positive UInt32 that never equals the negative literal → `unknown`. This is exactly the kind of bug the live-smoke exists to catch.

Fix: mask and compare with **long literals** (`0xFFFFFFFFL`, `0x800710E0L`, `0xFFFD0000L`) so everything normalizes to the positive low-32 value, and make the self-test mirror the real UInt32 representation so it becomes a regression guard:

Built the self-healing layer for the loopctl loop ecosystem (extends [[project_loopify_compiler_2026_06_30]]). Amo asked to "go into detail + implement" self-healing after seeing loops recover untouched.

## The model (6 layers)
Self-healing = a triad — **fail-closed + idempotent cadence-retry + observable heal (RED->GREEN)** — layered: 0 contained work · 1 cadence retry (passive) · 2 active remediators · 3 escalation budget (transient vs permanent) · 4 watchdog revives dead loop/daemon · 5 fleet board. Before this, the fleet had 0/1/5 + daemon-4 (`Jarvis-EngineWatchdog`, `*-Watchdog`, `MasterOverseer`); thin on 2/3 and had NO loop-revival (fleet-health only *reports* stale loops).

input.content:
<#
  loop-medic -- Stage C of the self-healing stack. Detect -> match -> HEAL -> re-verify,
  escalate to Amo ONLY when auto-heal fails or the fault is escalate-class. Closes the
  layer-4 gap: fleet-health only REPORTS stale/failing loops; the medic REVIVES them.

  Companion, not duplicate: the medic HEALS (runs 09:30), fleet-health REPORTS the
  cleaner board (10:00). The medic never posts a routine digest -- it acts, then pings
  only on a heal-failure or an escalate-class fault.

  SAFETY:
    * Default is DRY-RUN. Without -DoApply it mutates NOTHING -- it reports what it WOULD
      heal (Invoke-LoopHeal -WhatIf). Flip -DoApply to let it actually heal.
    * Only safe/idempotent remediators run (battery-gate, hung-runner, dead-loop).
      Destructive/funding faults return Escalate from loop-heal and are never auto-acted.
    * Claims the scheduled-tasks resource lock before any mutation (peer-safe).
    * Thrash guard: a target healed >= ThrashBudget times is escalated, not re-healed --
      a fault that won't stay fixed is a human problem, not a loop to paper over.
    * MaxHealsPerRun caps mutations per fire. Runtime cap + fail-closed + heartbeat.

  Exit: 0 OK | 1 ERROR (RED + notify).  ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $MedicId = 'loop-medic',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 240,
    [switch] $DoApply,                 # OFF (default) = dry-run; ON = actually heal
    [int]    $MaxHealsPerRun = 6,
    [int]    $ThrashBudget = 3
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl    = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal   = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'
$lockScript = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\claude-resource-lock.ps1'
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

function Send-MedicNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$MedicId] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

# Pure decision helper -- returns a bucket + message; caller owns the state.
function Get-HealAction {
    param(
        [string] $Sig, [string] $Target, [string] $Label,
        [bool] $Apply, [int] $HealCount, [int] $MaxHeals, [int] $Thrash, [hashtable] $Log
    )
    $count = 0
    if ($Log.ContainsKey($Target)) { $count = [int]$Log[$Target] }
    if ($count -ge $Thrash) {
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='escalate'; msg="$Label ($Sig): auto-healed $count times already -- WON'T STAY HEALED, needs a human"; target=$Target }
    }
    if ($Apply -and $HealCount -lt $MaxHeals) {
        $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target
        if ($r.decision -eq 'Healed') { return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='healed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): $($r.action)"; target=$Target } }
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='failed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): heal FAILED -- $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
    }
    $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target -WhatIf
    return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='would'; msg="$Label ($Sig): would $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
}

# --- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not (Test-Path $loopHeal)) {
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: preflight -- loop-heal.ps1 missing"
    Write-Error "preflight: $loopHeal missing"
    exit 1
}
. $loopHeal   # defines ConvertTo-LoopFault / Invoke-LoopHeal / etc. (also sets StrictMode)

$medicDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$MedicId"
if (-not (Test-Path $medicDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $medicDir -Force | Out-Null }
$healLogPath = Join-Path $medicDir 'heal-log.json'
$healLog = @{}
if (Test-Path $healLogPath) {
    try { $j = Get-Content $healLogPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          foreach ($p in $j.PSObject.Properties) { $healLog[$p.Name] = [int]$p.Value } } catch { }
}

$onBattery = $false
try { $bat = Get-CimInstance Win32_Battery -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
      if ($bat -and $bat.BatteryStatus -eq 1) { $onBattery = $true } } catch { }

$healed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$would  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$escal  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$failed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$healCount = 0
$lockHeld = $false
$autoHeal  = @('battery-gate','hung-runner','dead-loop')
$escalSigs = @('night-wakefail','wake-fail','worker-error','unknown')

try {
    if ($DoApply -and (Test-Path $lockScript)) {
        try { & $lockScript -Claim scheduled-tasks -Reason "loop-medic auto-heal" | Out-Null; $lockHeld = $true }
        catch { $DoApply = $false; $escal.Add("could not claim scheduled-tasks lock -- ran DRY this fire") }
    }

    # --- 1) failing scheduled tasks -----------------------------------------
    $tasks = Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -match '^(Jarvis|JARVIS|Hermes|DP600|Loopify)-' }
    foreach ($t in $tasks) {
        if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded" }
        if ($t.TaskName -eq "Loopify-$MedicId") { continue }
        $info = $null
        try { $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $t.TaskName -ErrorAction Stop } catch { }
        if (-not $info) { continue }
        $isNight = $false
        foreach ($tr in $t.Triggers) { if ("$($tr.StartBoundary)" -match 'T0[0-5]:') { $isNight = $true } }
        $sig = ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult ([long]$info.LastTaskResult) -TaskState "$($t.State)" -IsNight $isNight -OnBattery $onBattery
        if ($sig -eq 'none' -or $sig -eq 'dependency-down') { continue }   # dep-down self-heals on cadence
        if ($autoHeal -contains $sig) {
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig $sig -Target $t.TaskName -Label $t.TaskName -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
        elseif ($escalSigs -contains $sig) {
            $escal.Add("$($t.TaskName) ($sig): escalate-class -- needs a human")
        }
    }

    # --- 2) dead / red loops in the loopctl registry ------------------------
    $regPath = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops\registry.json'
    if (Test-Path $regPath) {
        $reg = Get-Content $regPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
        foreach ($l in @($reg.loops)) {
            if ($null -eq $l) { continue }
            if (-not ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'id')) { continue }
            if ($l.id -eq $MedicId) { continue }
            $status = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'status') { "$($l.status)" } else { '' }
            if ($status -ne 'deployed') { continue }
            $hb = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'last_heartbeat') { "$($l.last_heartbeat)" } else { '' }
            if ($hb -match 'RED|ERROR') { $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): heartbeat $hb -- failing its own work, needs a human"); continue }
            $stale = $false
            if ($hb) {
                $stamp = ($hb -split ' ')[0]; $dt = $null
                if ([datetime]::TryParse($stamp, [ref]$dt)) {
                    if (((Get-Date).ToUniversalTime() - $dt.ToUniversalTime()).TotalHours -gt 26) { $stale = $true }
                }
            } else { $stale = $true }
            if (-not $stale) { continue }
            $target = "Loopify-$($l.id)"
            if (-not (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $target -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): stale hb '$hb' and no task $target to re-run -- needs a human"); continue
            }
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig 'dead-loop' -Target $target -Label "loop $($l.id)" -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
    }

    # --- persist heal-log + write report ------------------------------------
    try { ($healLog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3) | Set-Content -Path $healLogPath -Encoding UTF8 } catch { }
    $mode = if ($DoApply) { 'APPLY' } else { 'DRY-RUN' }
    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
    $reportPath = Join-Path $medicDir ("report-{0}.md" -f (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))
    $lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines.Add("# loop-medic -- $stamp  [$mode]")
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Healed -- $($healed.Count)")
    if ($healed.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $healed | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Would heal (dry / over-cap) -- $($would.Count)")
    if ($would.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $would | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Escalate to human -- $($escal.Count)")
    if ($escal.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $escal | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    ($lines -join "`r`n") | Set-Content -Path $reportPath -Encoding UTF8

    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }

    if ($failed.Count -gt 0 -or $escal.Count -gt 0) {
        Send-MedicNote ("[$mode] healed $($healed.Count), would $($would.Count), ESCALATE $($escal.Count). See $reportPath")
    }
    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State GREEN
    Write-Output ("loop-medic [$mode] OK: healed=$($healed.Count) would=$($would.Count) escalate=$($escal.Count) report=$reportPath")
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: $msg"
    Write-Error "loop-medic FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='escalate'; msg="$Label ($Sig): auto-healed $count times already -- WON'T STAY HEALED, needs a human"; target=$Target }
    }
    if ($Apply -and $HealCount -lt $MaxHeals) {
        $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target
        if ($r.decision -eq 'Healed') { return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='healed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): $($r.action)"; target=$Target } }
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='failed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): heal FAILED -- $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
    }
    $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target -WhatIf
    return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='would'; msg="$Label ($Sig): would $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
}

# --- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not (Test-Path $loopHeal)) {
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: preflight -- loop-heal.ps1 missing"
    Write-Error "preflight: $loopHeal missing"
    exit 1
}
. $loopHeal   # defines ConvertTo-LoopFault / Invoke-LoopHeal / etc. (also sets StrictMode)

$medicDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$MedicId"
if (-not (Test-Path $medicDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $medicDir -Force | Out-Null }
$healLogPath = Join-Path $medicDir 'heal-log.json'
$healLog = @{}
if (Test-Path $healLogPath) {
    try { $j = Get-Content $healLogPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          foreach ($p in $j.PSObject.Properties) { $healLog[$p.Name] = [int]$p.Value } } catch { }
}

$onBattery = $false
try { $bat = Get-CimInstance Win32_Battery -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
      if ($bat -and $bat.BatteryStatus -eq 1) { $onBattery = $true } } catch { }

$healed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$would  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$escal  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$failed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$healCount = 0
$lockHeld = $false
$autoHeal  = @('battery-gate','hung-runner','dead-loop')
$escalSigs = @('night-wakefail','wake-fail','worker-error','unknown')

try {
    if ($DoApply -and (Test-Path $lockScript)) {
        try { & $lockScript -Claim scheduled-tasks -Reason "loop-medic auto-heal" | Out-Null; $lockHeld = $true }
        catch { $DoApply = $false; $escal.Add("could not claim scheduled-tasks lock -- ran DRY this fire") }
    }

    # --- 1) failing scheduled tasks -----------------------------------------
    $tasks = Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -match '^(Jarvis|JARVIS|Hermes|DP600|Loopify)-' }
    foreach ($t in $tasks) {
        if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded" }
        if ($t.TaskName -eq "Loopify-$MedicId") { continue }
        $info = $null
        try { $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $t.TaskName -ErrorAction Stop } catch { }
        if (-not $info) { continue }
        $isNight = $false
        foreach ($tr in $t.Triggers) { if ("$($tr.StartBoundary)" -match 'T0[0-5]:') { $isNight = $true } }
        $sig = ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult ([long]$info.LastTaskResult) -TaskState "$($t.State)" -IsNight $isNight -OnBattery $onBattery
        if ($sig -eq 'none' -or $sig -eq 'dependency-down') { continue }   # dep-down self-heals on cadence
        if ($autoHeal -contains $sig) {
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig $sig -Target $t.TaskName -Label $t.TaskName -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
        elseif ($escalSigs -contains $sig) {
            $escal.Add("$($t.TaskName) ($sig): escalate-class -- needs a human")
        }
    }

    # --- 2) dead / red loops in the loopctl registry ------------------------
    $regPath = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops\registry.json'
    if (Test-Path $regPath) {
        $reg = Get-Content $regPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
        foreach ($l in @($reg.loops)) {
            if ($null -eq $l) { continue }
            if (-not ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'id')) { continue }
            if ($l.id -eq $MedicId) { continue }
            $status = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'status') { "$($l.status)" } else { '' }
            if ($status -ne 'deployed') { continue }
            $hb = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'last_heartbeat') { "$($l.last_heartbeat)" } else { '' }
            if ($hb -match 'RED|ERROR') { $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): heartbeat $hb -- failing its own work, needs a human"); continue }
            $stale = $false
            if ($hb) {
                $stamp = ($hb -split ' ')[0]; $dt = $null
                if ([datetime]::TryParse($stamp, [ref]$dt)) {
                    if (((Get-Date).ToUniversalTime() - $dt.ToUniversalTime()).TotalHours -gt 26) { $stale = $true }
                }
            } else { $stale = $true }
            if (-not $stale) { continue }
            $target = "Loopify-$($l.id)"
            if (-not (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $target -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): stale hb '$hb' and no task $target to re-run -- needs a human"); continue
            }
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig 'dead-loop' -Target $target -Label "loop $($l.id)" -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
    }

    # --- persist heal-log + write report ------------------------------------
    try { ($healLog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3) | Set-Content -Path $healLogPath -Encoding UTF8 } catch { }
    $mode = if ($DoApply) { 'APPLY' } else { 'DRY-RUN' }
    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
    $reportPath = Join-Path $medicDir ("report-{0}.md" -f (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))
    $lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines.Add("# loop-medic -- $stamp  [$mode]")
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Healed -- $($healed.Count)")
    if ($healed.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $healed | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Would heal (dry / over-cap) -- $($would.Count)")
    if ($would.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $would | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Escalate to human -- $($escal.Count)")
    if ($escal.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $escal | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    ($lines -join "`r`n") | Set-Content -Path $reportPath -Encoding UTF8

    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }

    if ($failed.Count -gt 0 -or $escal.Count -gt 0) {
        Send-MedicNote ("[$mode] healed $($healed.Count), would $($would.Count), ESCALATE $($escal.Count). See $reportPath")
    }
    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State GREEN
    Write-Output ("loop-medic [$mode] OK: healed=$($healed.Count) would=$($would.Count) escalate=$($escal.Count) report=$reportPath")
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: $msg"
    Write-Error "loop-medic FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

content.text:
Good — the medic **failed closed correctly** (RED + exit 1, brakes working), and it surfaced a real bug: `[datetime]::TryParse($stamp, [ref]$dt)` fails with an overload error. Root cause is subtle and important: **dot-sourcing `loop-heal.ps1` leaked its `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` into the medic's scope**, and under StrictMode the `TryParse` + `[ref]`-to-untyped-null overload resolution breaks. fleet-health uses the identical pattern and works precisely because it *isn't* under StrictMode.

That's a latent footgun I just shipped into the template (every future loop dot-sourcing loop-heal would inherit StrictMode and could break). Two fixes: (1) stop loop-heal leaking StrictMode to dot-source callers — only enforce it in CLI mode; (2) make the medic's date-parse robust regardless. Fix 1:

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$script:LoopRoot = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops'

# ---- Self-test (verification) --------------------------------------------------
function Invoke-LoopHealSelfTest {
    $script:__stFail = 0
    function _assert { param([string]$Name,[bool]$Cond)
        if ($Cond) { Write-Host "  PASS  $Name" } else { Write-Host "  FAIL  $Name"; $script:__stFail++ }
    }

    Write-Host 'ConvertTo-LoopFault:'
    _assert 'battery gate (0x800710E0 on battery)' ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x800710E0L -OnBattery $true) -eq 'battery-gate')
    _assert 'hung runner (0x800710E0 on AC)'       ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x800710E0L -OnBattery $false) -eq 'hung-runner')
    _assert 'REGRESSION positive UInt32 2147946720 -> hung-runner' ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 2147946720 -OnBattery $false) -eq 'hung-runner')
    _assert 'night wake-fail (0xFFFD0000 night)'   ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0xFFFD0000L -IsNight $true) -eq 'night-wakefail')
    _assert 'REGRESSION positive UInt32 4294770688 night -> night-wakefail' ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 4294770688 -IsNight $true) -eq 'night-wakefail')
    _assert 'wake-fail off-night (0xFFFD0000)'     ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0xFFFD0000L -IsNight $false) -eq 'wake-fail')
    _assert 'worker error (0x1)'                   ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x1) -eq 'worker-error')
    _assert 'dependency down (0x3)'                ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x3) -eq 'dependency-down')
    _assert 'running state -> hung-runner'         ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -TaskState 'Running') -eq 'hung-runner')
    _assert 'benign 0 -> none'                     ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0) -eq 'none')
    _assert 'stale heartbeat -> dead-loop'         ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -HeartbeatStale $true) -eq 'dead-loop')
    _assert 'garbage code -> unknown'              ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x12345) -eq 'unknown')

    Write-Host 'Invoke-LoopHeal (WhatIf / decision routing):'
    _assert 'battery-gate + target -> Skipped(WhatIf)' ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'battery-gate' -Target 'X' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Skipped')
    _assert 'battery-gate no target -> NoOp'           ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'battery-gate' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'NoOp')
    _assert 'dead-loop + target -> Skipped(WhatIf)'    ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'dead-loop' -Target 'X' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Skipped')
    _assert 'dependency-down -> Retry'                 ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'dependency-down' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Retry')
    _assert 'night-wakefail -> Escalate'               ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'night-wakefail' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Escalate')
    _assert 'engine-down -> Escalate (guarded)'        ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'engine-down' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Escalate')
    _assert 'provider-exhausted -> Escalate'           ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'provider-exhausted' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Escalate')
    _assert 'none -> NoOp'                              ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'none' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'NoOp')

    Write-Host 'Register-LoopResult (escalation budget, id=_healtest, budget=3):'
    $tid = '_healtest'
    $tdir = Join-Path $script:LoopRoot $tid
    if (Test-Path $tdir) { Remove-Item $tdir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
    $r1 = Register-LoopResult -Id $tid -State RED -Fault 'worker-error' -Budget 3
    _assert 'RED #1 -> Retry, fails=1'   ($r1.decision -eq 'Retry' -and $r1.consecutive_fails -eq 1 -and -not $r1.escalate)
    $r2 = Register-LoopResult -Id $tid -State RED -Fault 'worker-error' -Budget 3
    _assert 'RED #2 -> Retry, fails=2'   ($r2.decision -eq 'Retry' -and $r2.consecutive_fails -eq 2 -and -not $r2.escalate)

**Stage C shipped and verified.** The self-healing stack is now A→B→C complete.

## What `loop-medic` does
Deployed `Loopify-loop-medic`, `DAILY@09:30` (heals *before* fleet-health reports at 10:00), heartbeat **GREEN**. Each run it scans failing tasks + the loop registry, and:
- **auto-heals** the safe faults (battery-gate with the flag actually set; dead loop → re-run),
- **escalates** everything else (worker-errors, wake-fails, unknowns, heal-failures),
- **thrash guard**: a target it's healed ≥3 times gets escalated instead ("won't stay healed → human problem"), so it can't mask a chronic fault,
- **claims the scheduled-tasks lock** before any mutation, caps heals/run, fails closed.

This closes the last gap in the stack — **nothing previously auto-revived a dead loop**; fleet-health only reported them.

## The dry-run gate earned its keep
Deploying it **dry-run by default** (per your own doctrine) immediately paid off. The first dry-run against your live fleet flagged **15 "would-heal" + 4 escalations** — almost all wrong. Running it *live* would have **stopped 11 legitimately-running watchdogs** and cleared already-clear battery flags. The gate caught four real classifier bugs:
1. `State='Running'` mis-read as "hung" (a task mid-run is normal).
2. `0x800710E0` mis-read as battery-gate whenever on battery — even when the task's flag was already clear (→ now `stale-refusal`, self-clears).
3. Codes `267014`/`267010` (terminated/disabled) false-escalating as `unknown`.
4. (bonus) dot-sourcing loop-heal was leaking `StrictMode` into runners, and a non-ASCII ellipsis had crept into a comment.

After fixes: **0 bogus would-heals, 1 true escalation** (VaultIngest's real `0x1`, which self-clears at 07:00). All committed (`5983226`); 29/29 self-test PASS under PS 5.1 + pwsh 7. **Lesson worth keeping: always live-smoke a classifier against the real fleet, not just unit tests.**

## To make it actually heal — your call

`PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP`: flipping `loop-medic` live means an autonomous agent will mutate scheduled tasks unattended (clear battery flags, re-run stalled loops) on a daily cadence.

It's deployed **dry-run** right now — it writes `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/report-<date>.md` daily but touches nothing. My recommendation: **let it run dry for a few days**, read a couple of reports, and once you trust the classifications, flip it by adding `-DoApply` to the task's Arguments (reversible; the thrash-guard + lock + heal-caps bound the blast radius). I won't flip it without your explicit go.

## Where the stack stands
| Stage | Status |
|---|---|
| A — fault catalog | ✅ committed |
| B — escalation budget | ✅ committed + wired into template |
| C — medic (detect→heal→escalate) | ✅ deployed **dry-run**, gated |
| D — `loopctl -Action Heal\|Restart` verb | not built (optional — unifies the control-plane API) |

Built the self-healing layer for the loopctl loop ecosystem (extends [[project_loopify_compiler_2026_06_30]]). Amo asked to "go into detail + implement" self-healing after seeing loops recover untouched.

## The model (6 layers)
Self-healing = a triad — **fail-closed + idempotent cadence-retry + observable heal (RED->GREEN)** — layered: 0 contained work · 1 cadence retry (passive) · 2 active remediators · 3 escalation budget (transient vs permanent) · 4 watchdog revives dead loop/daemon · 5 fleet board. Before this, the fleet had 0/1/5 + daemon-4 (`Jarvis-EngineWatchdog`, `*-Watchdog`, `MasterOverseer`); thin on 2/3 and had NO loop-revival (fleet-health only *reports* stale loops).

## Built + shipped (Stage A + B) — commit `20bcb41` in ~/scripts
`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1` (dot-source OR `-Action Classify|Heal|Result|State|SelfTest`):
- **Stage A** `Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault <sig> -Target <task> [-WhatIf]` -> `Healed|Retry|Escalate|NoOp|Skipped`. Catalog: battery-gate/hung-runner/dead-loop = auto-heal (safe/idempotent); night-wakefail/worker-error/engine-down/dead-daemon/provider-exhausted = **Escalate, no action** (inherits the destructive-op gate — never auto-restarts engine/Hermes or touches billing).
- `ConvertTo-LoopFault` (pure classifier) + `Get-LoopFaultSignature` (live-task wrapper).
- **Stage B** `Register-LoopResult -Id -State GREEN|RED -Budget K` over `~/.claude/loops/<id>/heal-state.json`: GREEN resets counter; RED increments; at K consecutive fails returns `Escalate` (no infinite retry). Default K=3.
- 25/25 built-in SelfTest PASS under PS 5.1 AND pwsh 7; live Classify verified (DP600->battery-gate, morning-brief->dependency-down, VaultIngest->worker-error).
- Wired into the loopify runner template `~/.claude/skills/loopify/templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (dot-sources loop-heal best-effort; GREEN resets, RED escalates after K). Template edit on disk only — the whole loopify skill is untracked in ~/.claude (0 tracked files), left to match that convention.

## GOTCHA (reusable) — PowerShell hex-literal signedness
A bare `0x800710E0` literal parses as a **negative Int32** (-2147020576) and `0xFFFFFFFF` as **-1** (so `-band 0xFFFFFFFF` is a no-op). But `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo.LastTaskResult` is a **positive UInt32** (2147946720). Comparing the two silently fails -> classifier returned `unknown` for a real 0x800710E0. FIX: use LONG literals `...L` (`0xFFFFFFFFL`, `0x800710E0L`) so everything normalizes to the positive low-32 value. The SelfTest passed at first because it fed the same negative literal to both sides — the LIVE smoke caught it. Two regression asserts now pin the positive-UInt32 path. See [[rules-windows-pitfalls]].

## Stage C — BUILT + deployed DRY-RUN (gated)
`~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/run.ps1`, registered+deployed `Loopify-loop-medic` DAILY@09:30 (before fleet-health 10:00), heartbeat GREEN. # loop-medic -- 2026-07-01 01:48  [DRY-RUN]

<#
  Loopify scheduled-runner template  -- ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
  Copy to ~/.claude/loops/<id>/run.ps1 and fill the two marked blocks.
  All six brakes are pre-wired: preflight gate, heartbeat, fail-closed,
  stop/runtime cap, budget cap, notify. Do not remove them.

  Deploy:  loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id <id> -Goal "..." -Archetype scheduled-cadence `
             -Runner local-scheduled -RunnerPath <this file> -Schedule "DAILY@10:00" -Deploy
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'CHANGE-ME',              # must match the registered loop id
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 600            # brake 4/5: hard wall-clock cap for one fire
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'   # self-healing layer (Stage A/B)
$FailBudget = 3                                       # consecutive REDs before escalating
if (Test-Path $loopHeal) { . $loopHeal }             # best-effort; template still works if absent
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    # Brake 6: best-effort notify. No-op if webhook unset. NEVER throws.
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

function Test-Preflight {
    # Brake 1: verify dependencies. Return $true to proceed, $false to abort clean (no-op).
    # ---- FILL: check whatever this loop depends on (engine /health, a file, a port). ----
    # Example:
    #   try { (Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:8010/health' -TimeoutSec 5).status -eq 'ok' }
    #   catch { $false }
    return $true
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Preflight)) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN     # dep down is not an error; abort clean
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: dependency not ready -- skipping this fire (no-op)."
        exit 0
    }

    # ================= WORK BLOCK (fill this) =================
    # Do the loop's actual work. Write any report to
    #   Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$Id\report-<date>.md"
    # Enforce the runtime cap inside any inner loop:
    #   if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded" }
    $result = "TODO: implement work"
    Write-Output $result
    # =========================================================

    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
    if (Get-Command Register-LoopResult -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State GREEN | Out-Null    # Stage B: reset the fail counter
    }
    exit 0
}
catch {
    # Brake 3: fail-closed. Stamp RED, notify, exit non-zero. Never green-on-error.
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State RED } catch { }
    # Stage B: escalation budget -- transient REDs retry on cadence; after $FailBudget
    # consecutive fails, escalate louder (a chronic fault a human must look at).
    $note = "RED: $msg"
    if (Get-Command Register-LoopResult -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $d = Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State RED -Fault 'runner-exception' -Budget $FailBudget
        if ($d.escalate) { $note = "ESCALATE ($($d.consecutive_fails)/$FailBudget consecutive REDs): $msg" }
    }
    Send-LoopNote $note
    Write-Error "LOOP FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\mattm\.claude\skills\loopify # Loopify — the prompt-to-loop compiler > A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes. > Loopify's job: take a goal Amo states once, and leave behind a **running loop** that pursues it — safely, observably, and killably. **Autonomy: FULL AUTO-DEPLOY** (Amo's standing choice, 2026-06-30). Safe loops register, deploy, and start themselves. The brakes below plus the machine's existing hooks (credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the safety net. Only genuinely destructive / outward-facing steady-state actions stop at a human gate (see §Safety). --- ## The one-screen model ``` GOAL (English) ──▶ [1 CLASSIFY] ──▶ [2 LEDGER] ──▶ [3 RUNNER] ──▶ [4 BRAKES] ──▶ [5 FEEDBACK] ──▶ [6 REGISTER+DEPLOY] ──▶ running loop what shape? what's "done" where runs? how it stops how it learns loopctl + verify + report ``` Every stage is mandatory. Create a todo per stage and work them in order. Do not skip to deploy. --- ## Control plane All loops share one registry and one CLI: **`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1`** → `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`. ```powershell loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id -Goal "" -Archetype -Runner [-RunnerPath

] [-Schedule ] [-StopCondition ] [-BudgetCap ] [-Deploy] loopctl.ps1 -Action Deploy -Id # (re)create the scheduled task for a local-scheduled loop loopctl.ps1 -Action List # fleet board loopctl.ps1 -Action Status [-Id ] # full JSON loopctl.ps1 -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR # runners call this every iteration loopctl.ps1 -Action Remove -Id [-Purge] # -Purge also deletes the scheduled task ``` `-Deploy` on a `local-scheduled` loop creates a `Loopify-` Windows task (shim pwsh, battery-gate cleared, LIMITED, daytime). For every other runner, deploy is done by *you* (the agent) with the right tool, then recorded via `-Action Register`. --- ## Stage 1 — CLASSIFY (what shape is this loop?) Walk the decision tree top-down; first match wins. | If the goal… | Archetype | Canonical runner | |---|---|---| | watches **external state** and acts when it changes (CI, a queue, a price, a file landing) | **dynamic** | in-session `/loop` + `ScheduleWakeup`, OR local-scheduled poller | | drains a **known, finite backlog** (a task list, a set of files) to empty | **backlog-drain** | in-session `/ralph` | | drains a backlog that **regenerates itself** — you must re-discover work each pass | **discovery-drain** | in-session `/jarvis-loop` | | must **push a quality metric to a bar** (score ≥ X, tests green, latency < Y) by generate→judge→improve | **evaluator-optimizer** | in-session loop or Workflow | | fires on a **clock** to read/compute/report (digest, audit, briefing) | **scheduled-cadence** | local-scheduled (fs/tooling) OR cloud routine (Gmail/Cal/pure-cognition) | | is **one big parallelizable pass** with a verify step (review N files, migrate N sites) | **fan-out-verify** | `Workflow` | | **proposes** a change, a second pass **checks** it, then commit | **maker-checker** | in-session loop or Workflow | Write down: `archetype = ` and one sentence why. If two fit, prefer the *simplest runner* that satisfies the stop condition. **Runner picker (hard constraints):** - Touches `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local fs → **local-scheduled** or **in-session**. NEVER a cloud routine (the sandbox can't see the local disk — it fails silently). - Pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar / Drive / web → **cloud routine** (`/schedule` or CCR `create_trigger`). - Needs many agents at once → **Workflow** (fan-out-verify). - Needs to run while no Claude session is open → **local-scheduled** or **cloud** (never in-session). --- ## Stage 2 — LEDGER (what is "done", and where does state live?) A loop without a written ledger is an infinite loop. Define both: 1. **Done predicate** — the exact, checkable condition that ends the loop or a run: - drain: `prd.json` all `passes:true` AND discovery finds 0 new (discovery-drain) / backlog empty (backlog-drain) - evaluator-optimizer: `metric >= threshold` OR `no improvement for K rounds` - scheduled-cadence: never "done" — it's a heartbeat; the run is done when the report is emitted - dynamic: the watched condition resolved (merge landed, queue empty) 2. **State store** — where the loop remembers across iterations: - drain → a `prd.json` / queue file (reuse the ralph/jarvis-loop layout) - evaluator-optimizer → a metrics JSONL (`~/.claude/loops//metrics.jsonl`), one row per round - scheduled-cadence → last-run marker + the report file under `~/.claude/loops//` - dynamic → the external state itself is the store; record last-seen in `~/.claude/loops//state.json` No state store you can point at → you have not finished Stage 2. --- ## Stage 3 — RUNNER (scaffold the execution substrate) Create `~/.claude/loops//` (or, for a repo-scoped loop, `/scripts/loops/`). Put the runner there. - **local-scheduled** → copy `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (next to this SKILL), fill the WORK block. It already wires preflight, heartbeat, fail-closed, notify, and the loopctl heartbeat call. ASCII-only (PS 5.1 will run it). Use `127.0.0.1`, shim paths, battery-safe (loopctl handles the last one at deploy). - **in-session** (`/loop`, `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`) → no script; the runner is the skill. Register the loop so it's on the board, and use `ScheduleWakeup`/the skill's own loop for iteration. - **cloud** → the runner is the routine prompt. Write it as a *complete standalone instruction* (fresh session each fire sees no history). - **workflow** → the runner is the Workflow script (pipeline/parallel + verify stage). - **evaluator-optimizer** (in-session or workflow) → copy `templates/evaluator-optimizer.md` — generate → *independent* judge panel → improve, with stop-at-bar / converge / cap / budget brakes already wired. --- ## Stage 4 — BRAKES (mandatory — no loop deploys without all six) Every deployed loop MUST carry all six. This is what makes it an *engineered* loop, not a runaway. 1. **Preflight gate** — verify dependencies before doing work; abort (no-op, exit 0) if a dep is down. (Don't trade if the engine's down; don't digest if the data source is unreachable.) 2. **Heartbeat** — call `loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR` every iteration. A dead loop stops stamping → the fleet board shows it stale. 3. **Fail-closed** — on any error: stamp RED, notify, exit **non-zero**. Never swallow an error into a green "success". (Anti-pattern: "no error in the log so it worked.") 4. **Stop condition** — the Stage-2 done predicate, checked every iteration. Even cadence loops need a max-runtime guard. 5. **Budget / iteration cap** — a hard ceiling (max iterations, max tokens, max wall-clock). The backstop when the stop condition never trips. 6. **Notification** — on RED / stop / budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` Discord, or Telegram). No-op silently if unset — never throw, never block. For PowerShell runners, brakes 1-3 and 6 come pre-wired in `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. For in-session/cloud/workflow, wire the equivalents (a Workflow gets brakes from `budget.total`, a stop-count loop, and a verify stage). --- ## Stage 5 — FEEDBACK (how the loop learns / self-corrects) Match the archetype: - **discovery-drain** → the discovery phase IS the feedback (re-scan signals each pass). - **evaluator-optimizer** → a judge/verify step scores each attempt; the next attempt reads the score. Use an *independent* judge (separate agent/criteria), not self-grading. - **maker-checker / fan-out-verify** → a second pass adversarially checks the first before commit. Default the checker to skeptical. - **scheduled-cadence** → the report's own deltas vs last run (flag regressions). - **dynamic** → re-read external state each wake; act only on genuine change. A loop with no feedback is a cron job. That's fine *if* the goal is truly stateless cadence — but say so explicitly. --- ## Stage 6 — REGISTER + DEPLOY + OBSERVE 1. **Register** via `loopctl -Action Register …` with the archetype, runner, stop condition, and budget cap filled in. 2. **Deploy** (full auto): - `local-scheduled` → add `-Deploy` (loopctl creates + battery-clears the task). Then **verify it exists**: `schtasks /Query /TN Loopify- /V /FO LIST` shows `Ready` + a plausible Next Run. - `cloud` → create the trigger with CCR `create_trigger` (fresh-session mode for standalone) or `/schedule`, then `Register` (record `task_name`=trigger id). - `in-session` → start the loop now (invoke `/ralph` / `/jarvis-loop` / `/loop`), Register it so it's on the board. - `workflow` → run the `Workflow`; Register a one-shot entry for the audit trail. 3. **Smoke-run once** if safe (a scheduled runner: `Start-ScheduledTask` then read the heartbeat / report). Confirm GREEN. Per verification.md — never claim it runs from the absence of an error; hit the actual heartbeat/report. 4. **Report to Amo** in the format below. ### Report format (always end a /loopify run with this) ``` LOOP COMPILED: goal : archetype : runner: ledger : done = state = brakes : preflight | cap | stop | notify deployed : status= observe : loopctl -Action List (and: ) kill : gated? : ``` --- ## Safety — what full auto-deploy does NOT cover Full auto-deploy means: read-only, report, local-fs-analysis, and in-repo maker-checker loops **deploy and start themselves**. It does **not** authorize a loop whose *steady-state action* is destructive or outward-facing. If the compiled loop would, on its own, repeatedly: - place **live** trades, or flip a paper/live flag - `git push` to a shared branch (main/master/develop/release/*), or force-push - mutate secrets / `.env` / 1Password - delete or mass-move files (always archive, never delete) - restart a prod service (engine, Hermes gateway) unguarded - send messages to **third parties** (email/DM to people who aren't Amo) then **do not auto-deploy it live**. Instead: compile it fully, register it with `status=blocked`, deploy it in **report-only / dry-run** mode (or gate the mutating step behind a flag defaulting OFF), and surface the gate to Amo with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The loop's dangerous step still hits the machine's PreToolUse hooks as a second line of defense — but the design-time gate is yours to hold. Everything else deploys. When in doubt between "useful cadence report" and "outward action", ship the report and let Amo pull the trigger on the action. --- ## Anti-patterns | Anti-pattern | Why it's wrong | Do instead | |---|---|---| | Deploy without a stop condition | infinite loop / runaway spend | Stage 2 done predicate is mandatory | | Green on error (swallow exceptions) | silent failure looks healthy | fail-closed: RED + notify + non-zero exit | | Cloud routine that reads `C:\Users\mattm\` | sandbox can't see local fs — fails silently | local-scheduled for anything local | | Self-grading evaluator loop | grades its own homework, never converges | independent judge / adversarial checker | | Night-time scheduled task (00:00-05:59) | machine asleep → 0xFFFD0000 | schedule 09:00-11:00 (Stage 6) | | One loop per file / per finding | fleet noise | group related work into one loop | | `git add -A` inside a runner | sweeps the 1,450-file backlog | stage per-file, pathspec commit | | Skipping Register | loop invisible + unkillable from the board | always Register, even in-session/workflow | --- ## Dogfood examples (shapes, not prescriptions) - "keep an eye on the self-healing scheduled tasks and ping me if one stays red" → **scheduled-cadence**, local-scheduled, daily 10:00, report-only, notify on red. Safe → auto-deploy. - "get the MES VWAP strategy's paper Sharpe above 0.5" → **evaluator-optimizer**, in-session/Workflow, metric ledger, independent gate-v2 judge, cap 20 rounds. Backtest-only → auto-deploy; any live wiring is Amo-gated. - "review every open PR for the exec-path stack and verify findings" → **fan-out-verify**, Workflow, adversarial verify stage. Read-only → auto-deploy. - "watch for the Vertex quota grant and flip the engine to Vertex-primary" → **dynamic**, poller; but the flip mutates engine config → deploy the *watch* live, **gate the flip** (notify Amo when granted). --- ## Cross-references - Brakes library + heartbeat: `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1` - Loop archetypes in the wild: `/ralph` (backlog), `/jarvis-loop` (discovery), `/loop` (dynamic) - Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `~/.claude/rules/windows-pitfalls.md` - Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `~/.claude/rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling - Verify-before-claiming: `~/.claude/rules/verification.md` - Destructive-op gate: `~/.claude/rules/destructive-op-gates.md` ARGUMENTS: Run the full JARVIS maintenance discovery-execute cycle on a recurring cadence: sweep all discovery signals (A untracked files in ~/scripts, B modified tracked files in ~/scripts, C failing scheduled tasks, D MEMORY.md size >20KB, E broken memory refs, F large untracked collections, G night-scheduled tasks 00:00-05:59), generate stories, auto-execute the safe/non-gated fixes (commit clean untracked scripts, clear battery gates, reschedule night tasks, archive oversized MEMORY sections), and surface Amo-gated items. This is the discovery-drain archetype currently run manually as /jarvis-loop.

# Jarvis Loop — Continuous Discovery-Execute Cycle

> Never stop because a prd.json is empty. Stop only when discovery finds nothing left to do.

---

## What Makes This Different From /ralph

`/ralph` executes a fixed backlog and outputs `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>` when empty.

`/jarvis-loop` wraps ralph's execute step inside an outer loop:

```
while (true) {
    execute all stories in prd.json  ← ralph logic
    run discovery phase              ← NEW
    if (discovery finds 0 new stories) break
    append new stories to prd.json
}
```

---

## The Loop

### Step 1 — Execute Current Stories (Ralph Phase)

Follow the Ralph skill exactly for each story:
1. Pick highest-priority story where `passes: false`
2. Implement it following acceptance criteria
3. Commit changes (conventional commits, per-file staging)
4. Mark `passes: true` in prd.json
5. Append learnings to progress.txt

### Step 2 — Discovery Phase (when prd.json is empty or all pass)

Run ALL of the following checks. Each produces a list of candidate stories.

**Signal A: Untracked files in ~/scripts**
```powershell
Set-Location C:\Users\mattm\scripts
git status --short | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\?\?' }
```
Story if: any `.ps1`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.yaml`, `.md` file is untracked and not in a worktree or temp dir.
Action: "Scan `<file>` for secrets and commit if clean."

**Signal B: Modified tracked files in ~/scripts**
```powershell
git status --short | Where-Object { $_ -match '^ M' }
```
Story if: any tracked file has unstaged changes.
Action: "Review diff of `<file>` and commit clean changes."

**Signal C: Failing scheduled tasks**
```powershell
Set-Location C:\Users\mattm\scripts
.\verify-jarvis-tasks.ps1 -FailOnly
```
Story for each failing task:
- `0x800710E0` → clear battery gate
- `0xFFFD0000` → task runs at night; reschedule to daytime
- `0x1` → investigate worker script, fix and rerun
- `0x41306` → task was manually stopped; check if expected or needs restart
- `0x8007042B` → service died; check if task should be re-enabled
- `Disabled` state → investigate whether disabling was deliberate

**Signal D: MEMORY.md size**
```powershell
(Get-Item C:\Users\mattm\.claude\projects\C--Users-mattm\memory\MEMORY.md).Length
```
Story if: size > 20480 bytes (20 KB).
Action: "Run ensure-memory-under-cap.ps1 to archive oldest section."

**Signal E: Broken memory refs**
Run `memory-hygiene.ps1` and check `brokenRefs` count in `.memory-hygiene-state.json`.
Story if: any broken refs found.
Action: "Fix broken link `<file>` in MEMORY.md."

**Signal F: Large untracked collections**
```powershell
Set-Location C:\Users\mattm\scripts
git status --short | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\?\?' } | Measure-Object
```
Story if: more than 15 untracked items remain after Signal A stories are generated.
Action: "Batch-scan and commit remaining untracked files in `<dir>/`."

**Signal G: Scheduled task time-of-day risk**
Check tasks that run between midnight and 6 AM:
```powershell
Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -match '^(Jarvis|JARVIS|Hermes|DP600)-' } | ForEach-Object {
    $triggers = $_.Triggers
    foreach ($t in $triggers) {
        if ($t.StartBoundary -match 'T0[0-5]:') {
            Write-Host "$($_.TaskName): $($t.StartBoundary)"
        }
    }
}
```
Story if: any task runs 00:00–05:59 (machine likely asleep → 0xFFFD0000 risk).
Action: "Reschedule `<task>` from `<time>` to 09:00–11:00 AM."

---

## Story Generation Rules

When discovery finds signals, convert them to stories:

1. **Group related findings** — don't create one story per file if they're the same operation. "Commit 8 untracked archive scripts" is one story, not eight.
2. **Priority order:**
   - P1: Security gaps (secrets in untracked files, broken gitignore)
   - P2: Failing tasks (operational breakage)
   - P3: Modified tracked files (potential regressions)
   - P4: Untracked files (version control gap)
   - P5: Housekeeping (reschedule, rename, doc updates)
3. **Max 10 stories per discovery round** — prevents runaway batches.
4. **Minimum actionable threshold** — skip a story if the fix would take longer than the value delivered. A 1-line diff with no risk = commit it. A 300-line rewrite with unknown deps = skip and note why.

---

## Stop Conditions

Stop the loop when **ALL** of the following are true:
- All signals A–G return zero actionable findings
- `prd.json` has all stories `passes: true`
- No new stories were generated by the last discovery round

Also stop if:
- Discovery finds something that requires Amo's manual action (rotation, push authorization, env flip, PR merge) — enumerate the blocked items and stop
- A story has been attempted twice and keeps failing — surface the blocker and stop

---

## Progress Tracking

After each discovery round, append to progress.txt:

```markdown
## [Date] - Discovery Round N
- Signals checked: A, B, C, D, E, F, G
- New stories generated: N
- Signals that fired: [list]
- Signals that were clean: [list]
---
```

---

## Workflow Variant (ultracode / parallel)

When invoked with the `ultracode` flag or when `budget.total` is set, use the Workflow tool for the discovery phase instead of sequential checks:

```javascript
// Phase: Discovery (all signals in parallel)
const [gitStatus, taskHealth, memSize, memRefs] = await parallel([
    () => agent("Run git status in ~/scripts, list untracked and modified files. Return JSON array of {file, status}.", {schema: GIT_SCHEMA}),
    () => agent("Run verify-jarvis-tasks.ps1 -FailOnly in ~/scripts, return list of failing tasks with error codes.", {schema: TASK_SCHEMA}),
    () => agent("Check MEMORY.md byte size at C:\\Users\\mattm\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-mattm\\memory\\MEMORY.md. Return {bytes, over_cap}.", {schema: SIZE_SCHEMA}),
    () => agent("Run memory-hygiene.ps1, return {brokenRefs count, issues}.", {schema: HYGIENE_SCHEMA}),
])

// Phase: Story generation (synthesize findings into prd.json)
const stories = await agent(`Given these discovery results: ${JSON.stringify({gitStatus, taskHealth, memSize, memRefs})}, generate up to 10 new user stories for the JARVIS maintenance prd.json. Prioritize: security > operational failures > version control gaps > housekeeping.`, {schema: STORIES_SCHEMA})
```

---

## Key Rules Inherited From Ralph

- ONE story per response — don't try to do everything at once
- Commit frequently — each story = one commit
- Keep CI green — never commit failing code
- Read patterns first — check progress.txt before starting
- Update learnings — help future iterations succeed
- Never `git add -A` — stage per-file always
- ASCII-only PS scripts — no em-dashes, no UTF-8 BOM

---

## Example Discovery Output

```
=== DISCOVERY ROUND 2 ===

Signal A (untracked files): 4 files → 1 story
  - register-inject-hook.py, contribution-log.py, scan_transcripts.py, set-inject-floor.py
  → US-016: "Scan and commit untracked Python scripts in ~/scripts"

Signal B (modified files): 0 files → clean

Signal C (failing tasks): 1 task → 1 story
  - DP600-Baseline-Mock: 0x1 (exit code 1)
  → US-017: "Investigate and fix DP600-Baseline-Mock 0x1 failure"

Signal D (MEMORY.md size): 16,674 bytes → clean (under 20,480)

Signal E (broken refs): 0 → clean

Signal F (large untracked): 0 remaining → clean

Signal G (night-time tasks): 0 → clean

Generated 2 new stories. Continuing...
```

---

## Where prd.json Lives

For Jarvis maintenance sessions:
```
C:\Users\mattm\.claude\skills\ralph\projects\jarvis-maintenance-<YYYY-MM-DD>\prd.json
```

Create a new dated directory for each invocation date. The discovery loop appends to the same prd.json until truly empty.

skills.content:
Amo asked: **X bookmarks ingestion into Obsidian/second-brain vault and how jarvis-trader utilizes them (discord-jarvis MCP search_bookmarks, gbrain semantic search, obsidian MCP)**

Answer it grounded in his gbrain knowledge vault, using the graph-aware recall layer so you
pull in not just the most-similar notes but **the documents they connect to**.

**Step 1 — Graph recall.** Run (Bash or PowerShell):

```
pwsh -File ~/scripts/recall-graph.ps1 "X bookmarks ingestion into Obsidian/second-brain vault and how jarvis-trader utilizes them (discord-jarvis MCP search_bookmarks, gbrain semantic search, obsidian MCP)" -Top 6 -Hops 1
```

This returns SEEDS (semantic matches) plus CONNECTED DOCUMENTS reached via their `[[links]]`,
each tagged with which seed linked it. If the question is broad or the seeds look thin, widen
with `-Hops 2` or raise `-Top`. For full bodies of the most relevant hits, re-run with `-Full`
or pull a single page with `pwsh -File ~/scripts/recall.ps1 "<slug or topic>" -Full`.

**Step 2 — Read the cluster, not just the top hit.** The whole point is the connections —
weigh the connected documents, not only the #1 seed. Note contradictions or supersessions
(memories carry dates; newer wins).

**Step 3 — Answer.** Respond to Amo's question directly, grounded in what you retrieved. Cite
the slugs you used so he can trace the chain. If the vault genuinely doesn't cover it, say so
plainly rather than guessing — and if a relevant memory looks STALE/contradicted, flag it.

**Notes.**
- The brain daemon must be up on `http://127.0.0.1:8077` (it normally is). If recall-graph
  reports it unreachable, tell Amo rather than answering from nothing.
- Retrieval is only as current as the last ingest. If a very recent memory you know exists
  doesn't surface, the brain may need a re-index (`POST :8077/ingest`) — mention it, don't
  silently miss it.
- Read-only: this never writes to the brain.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---

---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) — highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** — override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** — lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**Never read skill files manually with file tools** — always use your platform's skill-loading mechanism so the skill is properly activated.

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you — follow it directly.

**In Codex:** Skills load natively. Follow the instructions presented when a skill activates.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills speak in actions ("dispatch a subagent", "create a todo", "read a file") rather than naming any one runtime's tools. For per-platform tool equivalents and instructions-file conventions, see [claude-code-tools.md](references/claude-code-tools.md), [codex-tools.md](references/codex-tools.md), [copilot-tools.md](references/copilot-tools.md), [gemini-tools.md](references/gemini-tools.md), [pi-tools.md](references/pi-tools.md), and [antigravity-tools.md](references/antigravity-tools.md). Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

```dot
digraph skill_flow {
    "User message received" [shape=doublecircle];
    "About to enter plan mode?" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Already brainstormed?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" [shape=box];
    "Might any skill apply?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke the skill" [shape=box];
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" [shape=box];
    "Has checklist?" [shape=diamond];
    "Create a todo per item" [shape=box];
    "Follow skill exactly" [shape=box];
    "Respond (including clarifications)" [shape=doublecircle];

    "About to enter plan mode?" -> "Already brainstormed?";
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Invoke brainstorming skill" [label="no"];
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Might any skill apply?" [label="yes"];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" -> "Might any skill apply?";

    "User message received" -> "Might any skill apply?";
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Invoke the skill" [label="yes, even 1%"];
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Respond (including clarifications)" [label="definitely not"];
    "Invoke the skill" -> "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'";
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";
    "Has checklist?" -> "Create a todo per item" [label="yes"];
    "Has checklist?" -> "Follow skill exactly" [label="no"];
    "Create a todo per item" -> "Follow skill exactly";
}
```

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills could apply, use this order:

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, systematic-debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task
2. **Implementation skills second** (frontend-design, mcp-builder) - these guide execution

"Let's build X" → brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
"Fix this bug" → systematic-debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, systematic-debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

The skill itself tells you which.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.
