<#
.SYNOPSIS
  loopctl -- registry + auto-deploy engine for engineered loops (the /loopify backend).

.DESCRIPTION
  One control plane for every loop /loopify compiles, regardless of runner
  (local scheduled task, cloud routine, in-session, or Workflow fan-out). Keeps a
  single registry at ~/.claude/loops/registry.json so the whole fleet is visible
  and killable from one place.

  ASCII-only + no PS7-only syntax so PS 5.1 scheduled tasks can call -Heartbeat.

.PARAMETER Action
  Register | Deploy | List | Status | Remove | Heartbeat

.EXAMPLES
  # Register + auto-deploy a local scheduled loop (daytime, battery-safe, shim pwsh):
  loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id fleet-digest -Goal "Daily loop-fleet health digest" `
      -Archetype scheduled-cadence -Runner local-scheduled `
      -RunnerPath C:\Users\mattm\.claude\loops\fleet-digest\run.ps1 `
      -Schedule "DAILY@10:00" -Deploy

  loopctl.ps1 -Action List
  loopctl.ps1 -Action Status -Id fleet-digest
  loopctl.ps1 -Action Heartbeat -Id fleet-digest -State GREEN     # called by the runner
  loopctl.ps1 -Action Remove -Id fleet-digest -Purge             # unregister + delete task
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][ValidateSet('Register','Deploy','List','Status','Remove','Heartbeat')]
    [string] $Action,
    [string] $Id,
    [string] $Goal,
    [ValidateSet('dynamic','backlog-drain','discovery-drain','evaluator-optimizer','scheduled-cadence','fan-out-verify','maker-checker')]
    [string] $Archetype,
    [ValidateSet('local-scheduled','cloud','in-session','workflow')]
    [string] $Runner,
    [string] $RunnerPath,
    [string] $Schedule,          # e.g. "DAILY@10:00", "HOURLY", "WEEKLY:MON@10:00", or free-text for cloud
    [string] $KillCmd,
    [string] $StopCondition,
    [string] $BudgetCap,
    [ValidateSet('GREEN','RED','ERROR')]
    [string] $State,
    [string] $TimeLimit = 'PT20M',   # ExecutionTimeLimit for deployed tasks -- a hung runner
                                     # self-clears instead of holding the slot for schtasks' 72H default
    [switch] $Deploy,
    [switch] $Purge
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$LoopsDir    = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops'
$RegistryPath = Join-Path $LoopsDir 'registry.json'
$ShimPwsh    = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe'

function Get-Registry {
    if (-not (Test-Path $RegistryPath)) {
        return [ordered]@{ version = 1; loops = @() }
    }
    $raw = Get-Content $RegistryPath -Raw
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($raw)) { return [ordered]@{ version = 1; loops = @() } }
    return ($raw | ConvertFrom-Json)
}

function Save-Registry {
    param($Reg)
    if (-not (Test-Path $LoopsDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $LoopsDir -Force | Out-Null }
    $tmp = "$RegistryPath.tmp"
    ($Reg | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8) | Set-Content -Path $tmp -Encoding UTF8
    Move-Item -Path $tmp -Destination $RegistryPath -Force
}

function Get-LoopArray {
    param($Reg)
    # ConvertFrom-Json makes .loops a single object when there is exactly one entry.
    # The leading comma stops PowerShell unwrapping a single-element array on return
    # (otherwise a 1-entry registry returns a scalar and the Register concat throws).
    if ($null -eq $Reg.loops) { return ,@() }
    return ,@($Reg.loops)
}

function NowUtc { (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ') }

function New-TaskTrigger-FromSchedule {
    # Translate the compact -Schedule grammar into schtasks.exe args. Returns a hashtable
    # with SC/ST/D pieces, or $null for non-scheduled runners.
    param([string] $Sched)
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Sched)) { return $null }
    $s = $Sched.Trim().ToUpper()
    $time = '10:00'
    $day  = $null
    if ($s -match '@(\d{1,2}:\d{2})') { $time = $Matches[1] }
    if ($s -match ':([A-Z]{3})')      { $day  = $Matches[1] }
    if     ($s -like 'HOURLY*')  { return @{ SC='HOURLY'; MO='1' } }
    elseif ($s -like 'DAILY*')   { return @{ SC='DAILY';  ST=$time } }
    elseif ($s -like 'WEEKLY*')  { return @{ SC='WEEKLY'; ST=$time; D=($day) } }
    else { return @{ SC='DAILY'; ST=$time } }   # safe default
}

function Deploy-LocalScheduled {
    param($Loop)
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Loop.runner_path) -or -not (Test-Path $Loop.runner_path)) {
        throw "runner_path missing or not found: $($Loop.runner_path)"
    }
    $taskName = "Loopify-$($Loop.id)"
    $trig = New-TaskTrigger-FromSchedule $Loop.schedule
    if ($null -eq $trig) { throw "scheduled-cadence loop needs a -Schedule" }
    $exe = if (Test-Path $ShimPwsh) { $ShimPwsh } else { 'powershell.exe' }   # shim survives Store updates
    $tr  = "`"$exe`" -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File `"$($Loop.runner_path)`""

    $argList = @('/Create','/F','/TN',$taskName,'/TR',$tr,'/RL','LIMITED','/SC',$trig.SC)
    if ($trig.ContainsKey('ST')) { $argList += @('/ST',$trig.ST) }
    if ($trig.ContainsKey('MO')) { $argList += @('/MO',$trig.MO) }
    if ($trig.ContainsKey('D') -and $trig.D) { $argList += @('/D',$trig.D) }
    & schtasks.exe @argList | Out-Null

    # Battery gate is on by default and silently refuses on battery (0x800710E0).
    # Clear it -- an unattended loop must run on battery. (windows-pitfalls INC-2.)
    try {
        $t = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName -ErrorAction Stop
        $t.Settings.DisallowStartIfOnBatteries = $false
        $t.Settings.StopIfGoingOnBatteries     = $false
        # Bound runtime so a hung runner self-clears (schtasks defaults to PT72H, which
        # combined with MultipleInstances=IgnoreNew would block the schedule for 3 days).
        $t.Settings.ExecutionTimeLimit = $TimeLimit
        Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName -Settings $t.Settings | Out-Null
    } catch { Write-Warning "battery/time-limit set failed (non-fatal): $($_.Exception.Message)" }
    return $taskName
}

switch ($Action) {

  'Register' {
    if (-not $Id)        { throw "-Id required" }
    if (-not $Goal)      { throw "-Goal required" }
    if (-not $Archetype) { throw "-Archetype required" }
    if (-not $Runner)    { throw "-Runner required" }
    $reg = Get-Registry
    $loops = Get-LoopArray $reg
    if ($loops | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id }) { throw "loop id '$Id' already registered (Remove it first)" }
    $hbPath = Join-Path $LoopsDir "$Id\.heartbeat"
    $entry = [ordered]@{
        id             = $Id
        goal           = $Goal
        archetype      = $Archetype
        runner         = $Runner
        runner_path    = $RunnerPath
        schedule       = $Schedule
        stop_condition = $StopCondition
        budget_cap     = $BudgetCap
        kill_cmd       = $KillCmd
        task_name      = $null
        heartbeat_path = $hbPath
        status         = 'registered'
        created        = (NowUtc)
        last_heartbeat = $null
    }
    if ($Deploy -and $Runner -eq 'local-scheduled') {
        $entry.task_name = Deploy-LocalScheduled $entry
        $entry.status = 'deployed'
        if (-not $entry.kill_cmd) { $entry.kill_cmd = "schtasks /Delete /F /TN $($entry.task_name)" }
    } elseif ($Deploy) {
        Write-Warning "auto-deploy for runner '$Runner' is done by the agent (cloud=MCP trigger, in-session/workflow=direct); recorded as registered."
    }
    $reg.loops = @($loops + $entry)
    Save-Registry $reg
    "REGISTERED $Id [$Archetype/$Runner] status=$($entry.status)$(if($entry.task_name){" task=$($entry.task_name)"})"
  }

  'Deploy' {
    if (-not $Id) { throw "-Id required" }
    $reg = Get-Registry; $loops = Get-LoopArray $reg
    $loop = $loops | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id }
    if (-not $loop) { throw "no loop '$Id'" }
    if ($loop.runner -ne 'local-scheduled') { throw "Deploy handles local-scheduled only; runner=$($loop.runner)" }
    $loop.task_name = Deploy-LocalScheduled $loop
    $loop.status = 'deployed'
    if (-not $loop.kill_cmd) { $loop.kill_cmd = "schtasks /Delete /F /TN $($loop.task_name)" }
    Save-Registry $reg
    "DEPLOYED $Id -> task $($loop.task_name)"
  }

  'List' {
    $reg = Get-Registry; $loops = Get-LoopArray $reg
    if (-not $loops -or $loops.Count -eq 0) { "no loops registered"; break }
    $loops | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            id        = $_.id
            archetype = $_.archetype
            runner    = $_.runner
            status    = $_.status
            schedule  = $_.schedule
            lastHB    = $_.last_heartbeat
        }
    } | Format-Table -AutoSize
  }

  'Status' {
    $reg = Get-Registry; $loops = Get-LoopArray $reg
    $sel = if ($Id) { $loops | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id } } else { $loops }
    if (-not $sel) { "no matching loop"; break }
    $sel | ForEach-Object { $_ | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 }
  }

  'Remove' {
    if (-not $Id) { throw "-Id required" }
    $reg = Get-Registry; $loops = Get-LoopArray $reg
    $loop = $loops | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id }
    if (-not $loop) { throw "no loop '$Id'" }
    if ($Purge -and $loop.task_name) {
        try { & schtasks.exe /Delete /F /TN $loop.task_name | Out-Null; "deleted task $($loop.task_name)" }
        catch { Write-Warning "task delete failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
    }
    $reg.loops = @($loops | Where-Object { $_.id -ne $Id })
    Save-Registry $reg
    "REMOVED $Id$(if($Purge){' (+purged task)'})"
  }

  'Heartbeat' {
    if (-not $Id)    { throw "-Id required" }
    if (-not $State) { throw "-State required (GREEN|RED|ERROR)" }
    # Append to the per-loop heartbeat file AND stamp the registry (best-effort, never throw).
    try {
        $dir = Join-Path $LoopsDir $Id
        if (-not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null }
        Add-Content -Path (Join-Path $dir '.heartbeat') -Value ("{0}`t{1}" -f (NowUtc), $State) -Encoding UTF8
        $reg = Get-Registry; $loops = Get-LoopArray $reg
        $loop = $loops | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id }
        if ($loop) { $loop.last_heartbeat = "$(NowUtc) $State"; Save-Registry $reg }
    } catch { Write-Warning "heartbeat failed (non-fatal): $($_.Exception.Message)" }
  }
}

<#
  loop-heal.ps1 -- self-healing layer for the loopctl loop ecosystem.

  Stage A: a fault -> remediation catalog (Invoke-LoopHeal). Named remediators keyed
           to the fault signatures the fleet actually hits. SAFE/idempotent ops only;
           destructive or funding faults (engine restart, exhausted provider) return
           Escalate and DO NOTHING -- self-healing inherits the destructive-op gate.
  Stage B: an escalation-budget state machine (Register-LoopResult over
           ~/.claude/loops/<id>/heal-state.json). Transient fault -> retry on cadence;
           after K consecutive fails -> Escalate (page a human). No infinite retry.

  Two ways to use it:
    Dot-source :  . C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1   (then call the functions)
    CLI/testing:  loop-heal.ps1 -Action Classify|Heal|Result|State|SelfTest ...

  Design rules: ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe, StrictMode-clean. A helper NEVER throws --
  telemetry/heal must not be able to kill a loop.

  Decision vocabulary:
    OK        no fault / healthy
    Healed    a remediator actively repaired the cause
    Retry     transient; passive self-heal expected on next cadence (no action taken)
    Escalate  permanent / guarded / out-of-budget -> a human must act
    NoOp      nothing to do (missing target, benign)
    Skipped   -WhatIf dry-run (would act but did not)
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidateSet('Classify','Heal','Result','State','SelfTest')]
    [string] $Action,
    [string] $Id,
    [string] $Target,
    [string] $Fault,
    [ValidateSet('GREEN','RED','ERROR')]
    [string] $State,
    [int]    $Budget = 3,
    [switch] $WhatIf
)

# NB: do NOT set Set-StrictMode at top level -- this file is dot-sourced by loop runners,
# and leaking StrictMode into their scope changes method-overload resolution (e.g. breaks
# [datetime]::TryParse(str,[ref]$null)). Strictness is enforced only in CLI mode below.
$script:LoopRoot = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops'
$script:Benign = @(0, 267009, 267010, 267011, 267014)   # ok / running / disabled / never-run / terminated (soft, non-actionable)

function New-HealDecision {
    param([string] $Decision, [string] $Action, [int] $ConsecutiveFails = -1, [bool] $Escalate = $false)
    $o = [ordered]@{ decision = $Decision; action = $Action }
    if ($ConsecutiveFails -ge 0) { $o.consecutive_fails = $ConsecutiveFails; $o.escalate = $Escalate }
    return [pscustomobject]$o
}

function Send-HealNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return $false }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[loop-heal] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 8 | Out-Null
        return $true
    } catch { return $false }
}

# ---- Pure fault classifier (unit-testable; no live-task dependency) ------------
function ConvertTo-LoopFault {
    param(
        [long]   $LastResult = 0,
        [string] $TaskState = 'Ready',
        [bool]   $IsNight = $false,
        [bool]   $BatteryFlagSet = $false,
        [bool]   $HeartbeatStale = $false
    )
    # LONG literals (...L): a bare 0x800710E0 parses as a negative Int32 and 0xFFFFFFFF as
    # -1, so masking must use ...L to match the positive UInt32 Get-ScheduledTaskInfo returns.
    # 'Running' state is NOT a fault (a task mid-run is normal); 0x800710E0 is a battery gate
    # only when the task flag is actually set -- flag clear means the code is stale/self-clearing.
    $masked = [long]$LastResult -band 0xFFFFFFFFL
    if ($HeartbeatStale)         { return 'dead-loop' }
    if ($masked -eq 0x800710E0L) {
        if ($BatteryFlagSet)     { return 'battery-gate' }
        return 'stale-refusal'
    }
    if ($masked -eq 0xFFFD0000L) { return (if_night $IsNight) }
    if ($masked -eq 0x1)         { return 'worker-error' }
    if ($masked -eq 0x3)         { return 'dependency-down' }
    if ($script:Benign -contains $masked) { return 'none' }
    return 'unknown'
}
function if_night { param([bool]$n) if ($n) { 'night-wakefail' } else { 'wake-fail' } }

# ---- Live-task classifier wrapper ----------------------------------------------
function Get-LoopFaultSignature {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string] $TaskName)
    try {
        $t = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -ErrorAction Stop
        $i = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $TaskName -ErrorAction Stop
    } catch { return 'unknown' }
    $isNight = $false
    foreach ($tr in $t.Triggers) { if ("$($tr.StartBoundary)" -match 'T0[0-5]:') { $isNight = $true } }
    $batFlag = $false
    try { $batFlag = [bool]$t.Settings.DisallowStartIfOnBatteries } catch { }
    return (ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult ([long]$i.LastTaskResult) -TaskState "$($t.State)" -IsNight $isNight -BatteryFlagSet $batFlag)
}

# ---- Stage A: remediator dispatch ----------------------------------------------
function Invoke-LoopHeal {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string] $Fault,
        [string] $Target,
        [switch] $WhatIf
    )
    switch ($Fault) {
        'battery-gate' {
            if (-not $Target) { return (New-HealDecision 'NoOp' 'no target task given') }
            if ($WhatIf)      { return (New-HealDecision 'Skipped' "would clear battery flags on $Target") }
            try {
                $t = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $Target -ErrorAction Stop
                $t.Settings.DisallowStartIfOnBatteries = $false
                $t.Settings.StopIfGoingOnBatteries     = $false
                Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName $Target -Settings $t.Settings | Out-Null
                return (New-HealDecision 'Healed' "cleared battery flags on $Target")
            } catch { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' "battery clear failed: $($_.Exception.Message)") }
        }
        'hung-runner' {
            if (-not $Target) { return (New-HealDecision 'NoOp' 'no target task given') }
            if ($WhatIf)      { return (New-HealDecision 'Skipped' "would end hung instance + ensure ExecutionTimeLimit on $Target") }
            try {
                try { Stop-ScheduledTask -TaskName $Target -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null } catch { }
                $t = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $Target -ErrorAction Stop
                $lim = "$($t.Settings.ExecutionTimeLimit)"
                if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($lim) -or $lim -eq 'PT0S') {
                    $t.Settings.ExecutionTimeLimit = 'PT20M'
                    Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName $Target -Settings $t.Settings | Out-Null
                }
                return (New-HealDecision 'Healed' "ended hung instance + ensured ExecutionTimeLimit on $Target")
            } catch { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' "hung-runner heal failed: $($_.Exception.Message)") }
        }
        'dead-loop' {
            if (-not $Target) { return (New-HealDecision 'NoOp' 'no target task given') }
            if ($WhatIf)      { return (New-HealDecision 'Skipped' "would re-run stalled task $Target") }
            try {
                Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName $Target -ErrorAction Stop
                return (New-HealDecision 'Healed' "re-ran stalled task $Target")
            } catch { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' "re-run failed: $($_.Exception.Message)") }
        }
        'dependency-down'    { return (New-HealDecision 'Retry'    'passive heal: cadence retry recovers when dependency returns') }
        'stale-refusal'      { return (New-HealDecision 'NoOp'     'transient 0x800710E0 (task flag clear) -- self-clears on next fire') }
        'wake-fail'          { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' 'wake-fail off-night: investigate machine sleep/wake') }
        'night-wakefail'     { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' 'reschedule to 09:00-11:00 or add a wake timer (intent-sensitive -- surface, do not auto-move)') }
        'worker-error'       { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' '0x1 worker error -- needs investigation') }
        'engine-down'        { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' 'guarded restart only -- never auto-restart engine/Hermes from a heal') }
        'dead-daemon'        { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' 'guarded restart only -- route to the daemon watchdog/runbook') }
        'provider-exhausted' { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' 'billing/funding is human-only (top-up or support case)') }
        'none'               { return (New-HealDecision 'NoOp'     'no fault') }
        default              { return (New-HealDecision 'Escalate' "unknown fault '$Fault'") }
    }
}

# ---- Stage B: escalation-budget state ------------------------------------------
function Get-LoopHealState {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string] $Id)
    $d = [pscustomobject]@{
        id=$Id; consecutive_fails=0; heal_attempts=0; last_state=''; last_fault=''; last_attempt_utc=''; escalated=$false
    }
    $p = Join-Path $script:LoopRoot "$Id\heal-state.json"
    if (-not (Test-Path $p)) { return $d }
    try {
        $j = Get-Content $p -Raw -ErrorAction Stop | ConvertFrom-Json
        foreach ($k in 'consecutive_fails','heal_attempts','last_state','last_fault','last_attempt_utc','escalated') {
            if ($j.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains $k) { $d.$k = $j.$k }
        }
    } catch { }
    return $d
}

function Set-LoopHealState {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string] $Id, [Parameter(Mandatory)][object] $StateObj)
    try {
        $dir = Join-Path $script:LoopRoot $Id
        if (-not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null }
        $p = Join-Path $dir 'heal-state.json'
        $tmp = "$p.tmp"
        ($StateObj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5) | Set-Content -Path $tmp -Encoding UTF8
        Move-Item -Path $tmp -Destination $p -Force
        return $true
    } catch { return $false }
}

function Register-LoopResult {
    <# Update the budget on each fire; return {decision, consecutive_fails, escalate}. #>
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string] $Id,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][ValidateSet('GREEN','RED','ERROR')][string] $State,
        [string] $Fault = '',
        [int] $Budget = 3
    )
    $s = Get-LoopHealState -Id $Id
    $s.last_state = $State
    $s.last_attempt_utc = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ')
    if ($State -eq 'GREEN') {
        $s.consecutive_fails = 0
        $s.last_fault = ''
        $s.escalated = $false
        Set-LoopHealState -Id $Id -StateObj $s | Out-Null
        return (New-HealDecision 'OK' 'green -- counter reset' 0 $false)
    }
    $s.consecutive_fails = [int]$s.consecutive_fails + 1
    if ($Fault) { $s.last_fault = $Fault }
    $escalate = ($s.consecutive_fails -ge $Budget)
    if ($escalate) { $s.escalated = $true }
    Set-LoopHealState -Id $Id -StateObj $s | Out-Null
    $dec = 'Retry'; if ($escalate) { $dec = 'Escalate' }
    return (New-HealDecision $dec "fail $($s.consecutive_fails)/$Budget (fault=$Fault)" $s.consecutive_fails $escalate)
}

# ---- Self-test (verification) --------------------------------------------------
function Invoke-LoopHealSelfTest {
    $script:__stFail = 0
    function _assert { param([string]$Name,[bool]$Cond)
        if ($Cond) { Write-Host "  PASS  $Name" } else { Write-Host "  FAIL  $Name"; $script:__stFail++ }
    }

    Write-Host 'ConvertTo-LoopFault:'
    _assert 'battery gate (0x800710E0 + flag SET)'  ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x800710E0L -BatteryFlagSet $true) -eq 'battery-gate')
    _assert 'stale-refusal (0x800710E0 flag clear)' ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x800710E0L -BatteryFlagSet $false) -eq 'stale-refusal')
    _assert 'REGRESSION UInt32 2147946720 flag-set -> battery-gate'   ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 2147946720 -BatteryFlagSet $true) -eq 'battery-gate')
    _assert 'REGRESSION UInt32 2147946720 flag-clear -> stale-refusal' ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 2147946720 -BatteryFlagSet $false) -eq 'stale-refusal')
    _assert 'night wake-fail (0xFFFD0000 night)'    ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0xFFFD0000L -IsNight $true) -eq 'night-wakefail')
    _assert 'REGRESSION UInt32 4294770688 night -> night-wakefail' ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 4294770688 -IsNight $true) -eq 'night-wakefail')
    _assert 'wake-fail off-night (0xFFFD0000)'      ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0xFFFD0000L -IsNight $false) -eq 'wake-fail')
    _assert 'worker error (0x1)'                    ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x1) -eq 'worker-error')
    _assert 'dependency down (0x3)'                 ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x3) -eq 'dependency-down')
    _assert 'running task is NOT a fault -> none'   ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -TaskState 'Running' -LastResult 0) -eq 'none')
    _assert 'terminated 267014 -> none (soft)'      ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 267014) -eq 'none')
    _assert 'disabled 267010 -> none (soft)'        ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 267010) -eq 'none')
    _assert 'benign 0 -> none'                      ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0) -eq 'none')
    _assert 'stale heartbeat -> dead-loop'          ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -HeartbeatStale $true) -eq 'dead-loop')
    _assert 'garbage code -> unknown'               ((ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult 0x12345) -eq 'unknown')

    Write-Host 'Invoke-LoopHeal (WhatIf / decision routing):'
    _assert 'battery-gate + target -> Skipped(WhatIf)' ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'battery-gate' -Target 'X' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Skipped')
    _assert 'battery-gate no target -> NoOp'           ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'battery-gate' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'NoOp')
    _assert 'dead-loop + target -> Skipped(WhatIf)'    ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'dead-loop' -Target 'X' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Skipped')
    _assert 'dependency-down -> Retry'                 ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'dependency-down' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Retry')
    _assert 'stale-refusal -> NoOp'                    ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'stale-refusal' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'NoOp')
    _assert 'night-wakefail -> Escalate'               ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'night-wakefail' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Escalate')
    _assert 'engine-down -> Escalate (guarded)'        ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'engine-down' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Escalate')
    _assert 'provider-exhausted -> Escalate'           ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'provider-exhausted' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'Escalate')
    _assert 'none -> NoOp'                              ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault 'none' -WhatIf).decision -eq 'NoOp')

    Write-Host 'Register-LoopResult (escalation budget, id=_healtest, budget=3):'
    $tid = '_healtest'
    $tdir = Join-Path $script:LoopRoot $tid
    if (Test-Path $tdir) { Remove-Item $tdir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
    $r1 = Register-LoopResult -Id $tid -State RED -Fault 'worker-error' -Budget 3
    _assert 'RED #1 -> Retry, fails=1'   ($r1.decision -eq 'Retry' -and $r1.consecutive_fails -eq 1 -and -not $r1.escalate)
    $r2 = Register-LoopResult -Id $tid -State RED -Fault 'worker-error' -Budget 3
    _assert 'RED #2 -> Retry, fails=2'   ($r2.decision -eq 'Retry' -and $r2.consecutive_fails -eq 2 -and -not $r2.escalate)
    $r3 = Register-LoopResult -Id $tid -State RED -Fault 'worker-error' -Budget 3
    _assert 'RED #3 -> Escalate, fails=3'($r3.decision -eq 'Escalate' -and $r3.consecutive_fails -eq 3 -and $r3.escalate)
    $rg = Register-LoopResult -Id $tid -State GREEN -Budget 3
    _assert 'GREEN -> OK, counter reset' ($rg.decision -eq 'OK' -and $rg.consecutive_fails -eq 0)
    $persist = Get-LoopHealState -Id $tid
    _assert 'state persisted to disk'    ($persist.last_state -eq 'GREEN' -and $persist.consecutive_fails -eq 0)
    if (Test-Path $tdir) { Remove-Item $tdir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

    Write-Host ''
    if ($script:__stFail -eq 0) { Write-Host 'SELFTEST: ALL PASS' } else { Write-Host "SELFTEST: $($script:__stFail) FAILURE(S)" }
    return [int]$script:__stFail
}

# ---- CLI dispatch (only when -Action is given; harmless when dot-sourced) -------
if ($Action) {
    Set-StrictMode -Version Latest   # enforce strictness in CLI mode; not leaked to dot-source callers
    switch ($Action) {
        'Classify' {
            if (-not $Target) { Write-Output 'need -Target <taskName>'; exit 2 }
            Write-Output (Get-LoopFaultSignature -TaskName $Target)
        }
        'Heal' {
            if (-not $Fault) { Write-Output 'need -Fault <signature>'; exit 2 }
            Write-Output ((Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Fault -Target $Target -WhatIf:$WhatIf) | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
        }
        'Result' {
            if (-not $Id -or -not $State) { Write-Output 'need -Id <id> -State GREEN|RED|ERROR'; exit 2 }
            Write-Output ((Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State $State -Fault $Fault -Budget $Budget) | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
        }
        'State' {
            if (-not $Id) { Write-Output 'need -Id <id>'; exit 2 }
            Write-Output ((Get-LoopHealState -Id $Id) | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
        }
        'SelfTest' {
            $rc = Invoke-LoopHealSelfTest
            exit $rc
        }
    }
}

Both files are clear. **Stage D** = give `loopctl` a `Heal`/`Restart` verb that reuses the same `loop-heal.ps1` library the medic runs on cadence — so the control plane and the medic share one API (compile → operate → observe → **heal**).

Key design decisions:

file.content:
<#
  loop-medic -- Stage C of the self-healing stack. Detect -> match -> HEAL -> re-verify,
  escalate to Amo ONLY when auto-heal fails or the fault is escalate-class. Closes the
  layer-4 gap: fleet-health only REPORTS stale/failing loops; the medic REVIVES them.

  Companion, not duplicate: the medic HEALS (runs 09:30), fleet-health REPORTS the
  cleaner board (10:00). The medic never posts a routine digest -- it acts, then pings
  only on a heal-failure or an escalate-class fault.

  SAFETY:
    * Default is DRY-RUN. Without -DoApply it mutates NOTHING -- it reports what it WOULD
      heal (Invoke-LoopHeal -WhatIf). Flip -DoApply to let it actually heal.
    * Only safe/idempotent remediators run (battery-gate, hung-runner, dead-loop).
      Destructive/funding faults return Escalate from loop-heal and are never auto-acted.
    * Claims the scheduled-tasks resource lock before any mutation (peer-safe).
    * Thrash guard: a target healed >= ThrashBudget times is escalated, not re-healed --
      a fault that won't stay fixed is a human problem, not a loop to paper over.
    * MaxHealsPerRun caps mutations per fire. Runtime cap + fail-closed + heartbeat.

  Exit: 0 OK | 1 ERROR (RED + notify).  ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $MedicId = 'loop-medic',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 240,
    [switch] $DoApply,                 # OFF (default) = dry-run; ON = actually heal
    [int]    $MaxHealsPerRun = 6,
    [int]    $ThrashBudget = 3
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl    = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal   = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'
$lockScript = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\claude-resource-lock.ps1'
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

function Send-MedicNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$MedicId] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

# Pure decision helper -- returns a bucket + message; caller owns the state.
function Get-HealAction {
    param(
        [string] $Sig, [string] $Target, [string] $Label,
        [bool] $Apply, [int] $HealCount, [int] $MaxHeals, [int] $Thrash, [hashtable] $Log
    )
    $count = 0
    if ($Log.ContainsKey($Target)) { $count = [int]$Log[$Target] }
    if ($count -ge $Thrash) {
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='escalate'; msg="$Label ($Sig): auto-healed $count times already -- WON'T STAY HEALED, needs a human"; target=$Target }
    }
    if ($Apply -and $HealCount -lt $MaxHeals) {
        $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target
        if ($r.decision -eq 'Healed') { return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='healed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): $($r.action)"; target=$Target } }
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='failed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): heal FAILED -- $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
    }
    $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target -WhatIf
    return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='would'; msg="$Label ($Sig): would $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
}

# --- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not (Test-Path $loopHeal)) {
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: preflight -- loop-heal.ps1 missing"
    Write-Error "preflight: $loopHeal missing"
    exit 1
}
. $loopHeal   # defines ConvertTo-LoopFault / Invoke-LoopHeal / etc. (also sets StrictMode)

$medicDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$MedicId"
if (-not (Test-Path $medicDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $medicDir -Force | Out-Null }
$healLogPath = Join-Path $medicDir 'heal-log.json'
$healLog = @{}
if (Test-Path $healLogPath) {
    try { $j = Get-Content $healLogPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          foreach ($p in $j.PSObject.Properties) { $healLog[$p.Name] = [int]$p.Value } } catch { }
}

$healed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$would  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$escal  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$failed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$healCount = 0
$lockHeld = $false
$autoHeal  = @('battery-gate','hung-runner','dead-loop')
$escalSigs = @('night-wakefail','wake-fail','worker-error','unknown')

try {
    if ($DoApply -and (Test-Path $lockScript)) {
        try { & $lockScript -Claim scheduled-tasks -Reason "loop-medic auto-heal" | Out-Null; $lockHeld = $true }
        catch { $DoApply = $false; $escal.Add("could not claim scheduled-tasks lock -- ran DRY this fire") }
    }

    # --- 1) failing scheduled tasks -----------------------------------------
    $tasks = Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -match '^(Jarvis|JARVIS|Hermes|DP600|Loopify)-' }
    foreach ($t in $tasks) {
        if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded" }
        if ($t.TaskName -eq "Loopify-$MedicId") { continue }
        $info = $null
        try { $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $t.TaskName -ErrorAction Stop } catch { }
        if (-not $info) { continue }
        $isNight = $false
        foreach ($tr in $t.Triggers) { if ("$($tr.StartBoundary)" -match 'T0[0-5]:') { $isNight = $true } }
        $batFlag = $false
        try { $batFlag = [bool]$t.Settings.DisallowStartIfOnBatteries } catch { }
        $sig = ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult ([long]$info.LastTaskResult) -TaskState "$($t.State)" -IsNight $isNight -BatteryFlagSet $batFlag
        # skip non-actionable: benign, passive-heal (dep-down), and stale/self-clearing refusals
        if ($sig -eq 'none' -or $sig -eq 'dependency-down' -or $sig -eq 'stale-refusal') { continue }
        if ($autoHeal -contains $sig) {
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig $sig -Target $t.TaskName -Label $t.TaskName -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
        elseif ($escalSigs -contains $sig) {
            $escal.Add("$($t.TaskName) ($sig): escalate-class -- needs a human")
        }
    }

    # --- 2) dead / red loops in the loopctl registry ------------------------
    $regPath = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops\registry.json'
    if (Test-Path $regPath) {
        $reg = Get-Content $regPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
        foreach ($l in @($reg.loops)) {
            if ($null -eq $l) { continue }
            if (-not ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'id')) { continue }
            if ($l.id -eq $MedicId) { continue }
            $status = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'status') { "$($l.status)" } else { '' }
            if ($status -ne 'deployed') { continue }
            $hb = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'last_heartbeat') { "$($l.last_heartbeat)" } else { '' }
            if ($hb -match 'RED|ERROR') { $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): heartbeat $hb -- failing its own work, needs a human"); continue }
            $stale = $false
            if ($hb) {
                $stamp = ($hb -split ' ')[0]; $dt = $null
                try { $dt = [datetime]::Parse($stamp) } catch { $dt = $null }
                if ($dt -and ((Get-Date).ToUniversalTime() - $dt.ToUniversalTime()).TotalHours -gt 26) { $stale = $true }
            } else { $stale = $true }
            if (-not $stale) { continue }
            $target = "Loopify-$($l.id)"
            if (-not (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $target -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): stale hb '$hb' and no task $target to re-run -- needs a human"); continue
            }
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig 'dead-loop' -Target $target -Label "loop $($l.id)" -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
    }

    # --- persist heal-log + write report ------------------------------------
    try { ($healLog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3) | Set-Content -Path $healLogPath -Encoding UTF8 } catch { }
    $mode = if ($DoApply) { 'APPLY' } else { 'DRY-RUN' }
    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
    $reportPath = Join-Path $medicDir ("report-{0}.md" -f (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))
    $lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines.Add("# loop-medic -- $stamp  [$mode]")
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Healed -- $($healed.Count)")
    if ($healed.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $healed | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Would heal (dry / over-cap) -- $($would.Count)")
    if ($would.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $would | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Escalate to human -- $($escal.Count)")
    if ($escal.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $escal | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    ($lines -join "`r`n") | Set-Content -Path $reportPath -Encoding UTF8

    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }

    if ($failed.Count -gt 0 -or $escal.Count -gt 0) {
        Send-MedicNote ("[$mode] healed $($healed.Count), would $($would.Count), ESCALATE $($escal.Count). See $reportPath")
    }
    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State GREEN
    Write-Output ("loop-medic [$mode] OK: healed=$($healed.Count) would=$($would.Count) escalate=$($escal.Count) report=$reportPath")
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: $msg"
    Write-Error "loop-medic FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

Root cause identified. Looking at the medic: line 94 shows it **only claims the lock when `-DoApply` is set** — so in dry-run my held lock did *not* block it. The real culprit is line 100: `Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object {...}` is the one **un-guarded CIM call in the hot path**, and it ran at the exact moment my `Restart` was starting a task and my `Heal -Apply` was querying tasks. CIM task enumeration can throw transiently under concurrent task modification → the medic correctly fail-closed (exit 1). The foreground re-run with no concurrent churn exited 0, confirming the logic is sound.

Two problems worth fixing, both in the spirit of a *reliability* tool:
1. **The actual error was lost** — the catch block only `Write-Error`s + pings an unset webhook. A self-healing tool should capture its own failures.
2. **The medic is brittle to the very concurrency it's designed to operate within** — a peer touching tasks shouldn't flip it RED.

`loopctl.ps1` now exposes `-Action Heal|Restart`, sharing the same `loop-heal.ps1` library the medic runs on cadence -- rounds out compile(/loopify)->operate(loopctl)->observe(/loops)->**heal**.
- `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <loop>|-Target <task>`: classify + remediate ONE loop. **Dry-run by default** (previews decision+fault); `-Apply` executes. Fix: capture what you need into locals BEFORE `. $LoopHealPath`, inside the branch (the switch already dispatched on the original `$Action`). Also had to ADD `-Target` to loopctl's param block -- it only had `-Id`; StrictMode threw "variable $Target ... not set" until declared.

## Medic hardening (on-disk, ~/.claude/loops untracked) -- from the Stage D Restart smoke
Restarting the medic via the new verb WHILE I held the scheduled-tasks lock + ran concurrent Heal/Restart calls made the SCHEDULED instance exit 0x1, though the foreground run was clean 0. Root cause: the medic's task enumeration (`Get-ScheduledTask | Where...`) was the one **un-guarded CIM call in the hot path**, and CIM enumeration throws transiently under concurrent task start/modify -- exactly the concurrency the medic operates within. It fail-closed correctly (RED+exit1), but a reliability tool shouldn't flip RED because a peer touched a task. Two fixes: (1) `Get-JarvisTasks` bounded retry (3x, 2s) -- a real outage still fail-closes; (2) catch block now writes `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/last-error.txt` (msg+type+stack) so a fail-closed RED is diagnosable next session (webhook is unset). Built the self-healing layer for the loopctl loop ecosystem (extends [[project_loopify_compiler_2026_06_30]]). Amo asked to "go into detail + implement" self-healing after seeing loops recover untouched.

## The model (6 layers)
Self-healing = a triad — **fail-closed + idempotent cadence-retry + observable heal (RED->GREEN)** — layered: 0 contained work · 1 cadence retry (passive) · 2 active remediators · 3 escalation budget (transient vs permanent) · 4 watchdog revives dead loop/daemon · 5 fleet board. Before this, the fleet had 0/1/5 + daemon-4 (`Jarvis-EngineWatchdog`, `*-Watchdog`, `MasterOverseer`); thin on 2/3 and had NO loop-revival (fleet-health only *reports* stale loops).

## Built + shipped (Stage A + B) — commit `20bcb41` in ~/scripts
`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1` (dot-source OR `-Action Classify|Heal|Result|State|SelfTest`):
- **Stage A** `Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault <sig> -Target <task> [-WhatIf]` -> `Healed|Retry|Escalate|NoOp|Skipped`. Catalog: battery-gate/hung-runner/dead-loop = auto-heal (safe/idempotent); night-wakefail/worker-error/engine-down/dead-daemon/provider-exhausted = **Escalate, no action** (inherits the destructive-op gate — never auto-restarts engine/Hermes or touches billing).
- `ConvertTo-LoopFault` (pure classifier) + `Get-LoopFaultSignature` (live-task wrapper).
- **Stage B** `Register-LoopResult -Id -State GREEN|RED -Budget K` over `~/.claude/loops/<id>/heal-state.json`: GREEN resets counter; RED increments; at K consecutive fails returns `Escalate` (no infinite retry). Default K=3.
- 25/25 built-in SelfTest PASS under PS 5.1 AND pwsh 7; live Classify verified (DP600->battery-gate, morning-brief->dependency-down, VaultIngest->worker-error).
- Wired into the loopify runner template `~/.claude/skills/loopify/templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (dot-sources loop-heal best-effort; GREEN resets, RED escalates after K). Template edit on disk only — the whole loopify skill is untracked in ~/.claude (0 tracked files), left to match that convention.

## GOTCHA (reusable) — PowerShell hex-literal signedness
A bare `0x800710E0` literal parses as a **negative Int32** (-2147020576) and `0xFFFFFFFF` as **-1** (so `-band 0xFFFFFFFF` is a no-op). But `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo.LastTaskResult` is a **positive UInt32** (2147946720). Comparing the two silently fails -> classifier returned `unknown` for a real 0x800710E0. FIX: use LONG literals `...L` (`0xFFFFFFFFL`, `0x800710E0L`) so everything normalizes to the positive low-32 value. The SelfTest passed at first because it fed the same negative literal to both sides — the LIVE smoke caught it. Two regression asserts now pin the positive-UInt32 path. See [[rules-windows-pitfalls]].

## Stage C — BUILT + deployed DRY-RUN (gated)
`~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/run.ps1`, registered+deployed `Loopify-loop-medic` DAILY@09:30 (before fleet-health 10:00), heartbeat GREEN. Detects failing tasks + stale/red registry loops, auto-heals safe faults (battery-gate flag-set, dead-loop re-run), escalates the rest; thrash guard (`heal-log.json`) escalates a target auto-healed >=ThrashBudget times ("won't stay healed"); claims scheduled-tasks lock before mutating; MaxHealsPerRun cap; fail-closed. **Deployed DRY-RUN: default `-DoApply` OFF -> reports what it WOULD heal, mutates nothing.** To go live: add `-DoApply` to the task Arguments (Amo-gated, `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP`).

CLASSIFIER LESSON (the dry-run gate earned its keep): first dry-run flagged **15 bogus would-heals + 4 false escalations**. Root causes fixed in loop-heal (commit `5983226`): (1) `State='Running'` is NOT a fault (a task mid-run is normal) -- had mis-flagged 11 live watchdogs as hung; live-healing would have STOPPED running watchdogs. (2) `0x800710E0` is battery-gate ONLY if the task's `DisallowStartIfOnBatteries` flag is actually set; flag-clear -> `stale-refusal` (NoOp, self-clears) -- every live 0x800710E0 had flag=clear. (3) result codes 267014/267010 (terminated/disabled) added to benign (were false-escalating as `unknown`). After fixes: 0 would-heal, 1 true escalation. **Always live-smoke a classifier against the real fleet, not just unit tests.**

## Remaining (Stage D) — NOT built
- **Stage D** give `loopctl.ps1` a `-Action Heal|Restart` verb so the control plane + medic share one API. Rounds out compile(/loopify)->operate(loopctl)->observe(/loops)->**heal**.
- **Flip loop-medic live**: add `-DoApply` to the `Loopify-loop-medic` task Arguments after Amo reviews a few dry-run reports (`~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/report-*.md`). Amo-gated.

# Loop Engineering — Amo

> A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes.
> Loop engineering is the default posture for any goal that is recurring, multi-pass, unbounded, or
> must converge to a bar. Established 2026-06-30 ("loop engineering is the new future instead of prompts").

## The core shift

Stop thinking "what do I prompt for this?" and start thinking "what loop pursues this?" Most durable
value on this machine is not a one-shot answer — it's a process that runs, remembers, self-corrects,
and tells Amo only when it needs him. When a goal is stated, ask: **is this a turn, or a loop?**

- **Turn** (answer once, done): a lookup, a single edit, a one-time analysis. Just do it.
- **Loop** (runs until a condition): recurring cadence, draining a backlog, converging a metric,
  watching external state, sweeping N items. → **compile it with `/loopify`.**

If in doubt and the goal contains "keep", "every", "until", "whenever", "monitor", "maintain",
"get X above Y", or "for each of these N" — it's a loop.

## The toolchain (three verbs)

| Verb | Tool | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **compile** | `/loopify <goal>` | goal → classify → ledger → runner → brakes → feedback → register + auto-deploy |
| **operate** | `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1` | Register / Deploy / List / Status / Remove / Heartbeat over `~/.claude/loops/registry.json` |
| **observe** | `/loops` | fleet board: what's running, what's stale, what's red, one-line-per-loop |

`/loopify` is the compiler; you rarely hand-author a loop. Reach for loopctl directly only to inspect
or kill. `/loops` is the read-only dashboard.

## Archetype taxonomy (first match wins)

| Goal shape | Archetype | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| watch external state, act on change | dynamic | `/loop`+ScheduleWakeup, or a poller |
| drain a known finite backlog | backlog-drain | `/ralph` |
| drain a backlog that regenerates (re-discover each pass) | discovery-drain | `/jarvis-loop` |
| push a metric to a bar (generate→judge→improve) | evaluator-optimizer | in-session or `Workflow` |
| clock-fired read/compute/report | scheduled-cadence | local task OR cloud routine |
| one big parallel pass + verify | fan-out-verify | `Workflow` |
| propose → check → commit | maker-checker | in-session or `Workflow` |

## Runner selection — the one hard rule

**Anything touching `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local file
runs LOCAL (scheduled task or in-session) — NEVER a cloud routine.** The cloud sandbox cannot see the
local disk and fails silently. Cloud routines are only for pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar /
Drive / web. (Same rule as `workflow.md` § Scheduling.)

## The brakes contract (non-negotiable)

No loop deploys without all six. This is the line between an engineered loop and a runaway:

1. **Preflight** — verify deps; abort clean if down (don't act on a dead dependency).
2. **Heartbeat** — stamp GREEN/RED/ERROR each iteration via `loopctl -Heartbeat`; a dead loop stops stamping.
3. **Fail-closed** — error ⇒ RED + notify + non-zero exit. Never green-on-error, never "no error in the log so it worked".
4. **Stop condition** — the written done-predicate, checked every iteration.
5. **Budget/iteration cap** — hard ceiling (iterations / tokens / wall-clock) as the backstop.
6. **Notify** — on RED/stop/budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK`); no-op silently if unset, never throw.

PowerShell runners get brakes 1-3+6 pre-wired from `skills/loopify/templates/scheduled-runner.ps1`
and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. A `Workflow` gets them from `budget.total`, a
loop-until-dry/count guard, and an adversarial verify stage.

## Safety envelope (full auto-deploy)

Amo's standing autonomy for `/loopify` is **full auto-deploy**: safe loops register, deploy, and start
themselves. Safe = read-only, report, local-fs analysis, in-repo maker-checker. A loop whose
**steady-state action** is destructive or outward-facing does NOT auto-deploy live — it compiles, then
stops at a human gate:

- live trades or flipping a paper/live flag
- `git push` to a shared branch, or force-push
- secret / `.env` / 1Password mutation
- file delete or mass-move (always archive, never delete)
- unguarded prod-service restart (engine, Hermes)
- messages to third parties (anyone but Amo)

For those: compile fully, register `status=blocked`, deploy in report-only / dry-run / flag-off mode,
and surface with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The machine's PreToolUse hooks
(credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the second line of defense — the
design-time gate is the first.

## Anti-patterns

- Deploying without a stop condition → runaway. Stage-2 predicate is mandatory.
- Green-on-error → silent failure looks healthy. Fail-closed.
- Cloud routine reading local fs → silent no-op. Local runner.
- Self-grading evaluator → never converges. Use an independent judge.
- Night-scheduled task (00:00-05:59) → machine asleep, 0xFFFD0000. Schedule 09:00-11:00.
- One loop per file/finding → fleet noise. Group related work.
- Loop invisible on the board → always Register, even in-session/Workflow.

## Cross-references

- Compiler skill: `~/.claude/skills/loopify/SKILL.md`
- Control plane: `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1` · registry `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`
- Board: `/loops`
- Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling
- Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `rules/windows-pitfalls.md`
- Verify-before-claiming: `rules/verification.md`
- Destructive-op gate: `rules/destructive-op-gates.md`
- In-the-wild loop skills: `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`, `/loop`

content.text:
Amo — the self-healing stack is **complete and green, end-to-end**. Final state:

## Verified just now
- **Stage A+B library** (`loop-heal.ps1`): selftest **ALL PASS** (29 assertions, PS 5.1 + pwsh 7)
- **Stage D verbs live**: `loopctl` now exposes `... | Heartbeat | Heal | Restart`
- **Shared-library wiring proven**: `loopctl -Action Heal -Id loop-medic` → classifies via the same catalog the medic uses, dry-run by default
- **Git**: `7d6bf7e` committed (pathspec, peer-safe); working tree clean
- **Fleet**: 9 loops, all deployed/registered loops GREEN

## What Stage D added (`7d6bf7e`)
| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <loop>` | classify + **preview** remediation (dry-run) |
| `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <loop> -Apply` | actually heal — but escalate-class faults (worker-error, engine-down, provider-exhausted) **take no action even with `-Apply`** (inherits the destructive-op gate) |
| `loopctl -Action Heal -Target <task>` | heal a raw task name, no registry lookup |
| `loopctl -Action Restart -Id <loop>` | re-run a stalled task now |

The control plane and the medic now share **one** heal API — `compile → operate → observe → **heal**`.

## Bonus hardening (the Restart smoke earned it)
Restarting the medic under concurrent task churn made the *scheduled* instance exit `0x1` while the foreground run was clean — the medic's task-enumeration CIM call was the one un-guarded hot-path call, brittle to the exact concurrency it polices. Fixed two ways: **bounded retry** (`Get-JarvisTasks`, 3×2s, still fail-closes on a real outage) and **failure capture** (`last-error.txt`, so a fail-closed RED is diagnosable when the webhook is silent). Re-verified: scheduled Restart → **`0x0` GREEN**, no error file.

## The full stack now
| Stage | Status |
|---|---|
| A — fault catalog | ✅ committed |
| B — escalation budget | ✅ committed + wired into runner template |
| C — medic (detect→heal→escalate) | ✅ deployed **dry-run**, hardened |
| D — `loopctl Heal/Restart` verb | ✅ committed + verified |

Doctrine (`rules/loop-engineering.md`) and the project memory are updated to reflect all four stages.

## Two things still gated to you (not blocking)
1. **`PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP`** — flip the medic live by adding `-DoApply` to the `Loopify-loop-medic` task. My recommendation holds: **let it bake dry-run a few days**, skim `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/report-*.md`, then flip. I won't do it without your explicit "flip it."

That closes the self-healing implementation path you asked about. The loops now watch, heal, and escalate themselves; the only humans-in-the-loop are the two gates above.

Built the self-healing layer for the loopctl loop ecosystem (extends [[project_loopify_compiler_2026_06_30]]). Amo asked to "go into detail + implement" self-healing after seeing loops recover untouched.

## The model (6 layers)
Self-healing = a triad — **fail-closed + idempotent cadence-retry + observable heal (RED->GREEN)** — layered: 0 contained work · 1 cadence retry (passive) · 2 active remediators · 3 escalation budget (transient vs permanent) · 4 watchdog revives dead loop/daemon · 5 fleet board. Before this, the fleet had 0/1/5 + daemon-4 (`Jarvis-EngineWatchdog`, `*-Watchdog`, `MasterOverseer`); thin on 2/3 and had NO loop-revival (fleet-health only *reports* stale loops).

## Built + shipped (Stage A + B) — commit `20bcb41` in ~/scripts
`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1` (dot-source OR `-Action Classify|Heal|Result|State|SelfTest`):
- **Stage A** `Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault <sig> -Target <task> [-WhatIf]` -> `Healed|Retry|Escalate|NoOp|Skipped`. Catalog: battery-gate/hung-runner/dead-loop = auto-heal (safe/idempotent); night-wakefail/worker-error/engine-down/dead-daemon/provider-exhausted = **Escalate, no action** (inherits the destructive-op gate — never auto-restarts engine/Hermes or touches billing).
- `ConvertTo-LoopFault` (pure classifier) + `Get-LoopFaultSignature` (live-task wrapper).
- **Stage B** `Register-LoopResult -Id -State GREEN|RED -Budget K` over `~/.claude/loops/<id>/heal-state.json`: GREEN resets counter; RED increments; at K consecutive fails returns `Escalate` (no infinite retry). Default K=3.
- 25/25 built-in SelfTest PASS under PS 5.1 AND pwsh 7; live Classify verified (DP600->battery-gate, morning-brief->dependency-down, VaultIngest->worker-error).
- Wired into the loopify runner template `~/.claude/skills/loopify/templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (dot-sources loop-heal best-effort; GREEN resets, RED escalates after K). Template edit on disk only — the whole loopify skill is untracked in ~/.claude (0 tracked files), left to match that convention.

## GOTCHA (reusable) — PowerShell hex-literal signedness
A bare `0x800710E0` literal parses as a **negative Int32** (-2147020576) and `0xFFFFFFFF` as **-1** (so `-band 0xFFFFFFFF` is a no-op). But `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo.LastTaskResult` is a **positive UInt32** (2147946720). Comparing the two silently fails -> classifier returned `unknown` for a real 0x800710E0. FIX: use LONG literals `...L` (`0xFFFFFFFFL`, `0x800710E0L`) so everything normalizes to the positive low-32 value. The SelfTest passed at first because it fed the same negative literal to both sides — the LIVE smoke caught it. Two regression asserts now pin the positive-UInt32 path. See [[rules-windows-pitfalls]].

## Stage C — BUILT + deployed DRY-RUN (gated)
`~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/run.ps1`, registered+deployed `Loopify-loop-medic` DAILY@09:30 (before fleet-health 10:00), heartbeat GREEN. Detects failing tasks + stale/red registry loops, auto-heals safe faults (battery-gate flag-set, dead-loop re-run), escalates the rest; thrash guard (`heal-log.json`) escalates a target auto-healed >=ThrashBudget times ("won't stay healed"); claims scheduled-tasks lock before mutating; MaxHealsPerRun cap; fail-closed. **Deployed DRY-RUN: default `-DoApply` OFF -> reports what it WOULD heal, mutates nothing.** To go live: add `-DoApply` to the task Arguments (Amo-gated, `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP`).

CLASSIFIER LESSON (the dry-run gate earned its keep): first dry-run flagged **15 bogus would-heals + 4 false escalations**. Root causes fixed in loop-heal (commit `5983226`): (1) `State='Running'` is NOT a fault (a task mid-run is normal) -- had mis-flagged 11 live watchdogs as hung; live-healing would have STOPPED running watchdogs. (2) `0x800710E0` is battery-gate ONLY if the task's `DisallowStartIfOnBatteries` flag is actually set; flag-clear -> `stale-refusal` (NoOp, self-clears) -- every live 0x800710E0 had flag=clear. (3) result codes 267014/267010 (terminated/disabled) added to benign (were false-escalating as `unknown`). After fixes: 0 would-heal, 1 true escalation. **Always live-smoke a classifier against the real fleet, not just unit tests.**

## Stage D — BUILT + verified (commit `7d6bf7e` in ~/scripts)
`loopctl.ps1` now exposes `-Action Heal|Restart`, sharing the same `loop-heal.ps1` library the medic runs on cadence — rounds out compile(/loopify)->operate(loopctl)->observe(/loops)->**heal**.
- `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <loop>|-Target <task>`: classify + remediate ONE loop. **Dry-run by default** (previews decision+fault); `-Apply` executes. Escalate-class faults (worker-error/engine-down/provider-exhausted) take **NO action even with -Apply** — inherits loop-heal's destructive-op gate. Verified: `-Apply` on Jarvis-VaultIngest-All's real 0x1 -> Escalate/applied=False.
- `loopctl -Action Restart -Id <loop>|-Target <task>`: re-run a stalled task now (== dead-loop remediator). Verified end-to-end: Restart loop-medic -> 0x0 GREEN.
- Added `-Target` param + `Resolve-HealTaskName` (registry id -> task_name, or raw task name; throws clean for in-session loops / unknown ids).
- **GOTCHA (reusable):** dot-sourcing `loop-heal.ps1` re-runs ITS `param()` block, which clobbers the caller's bound `$Id/$Target/$State` to defaults. Fix: capture what you need into locals BEFORE `. $LoopHealPath`, inside the branch (the switch already dispatched on the original `$Action`). Also had to ADD `-Target` to loopctl's param block — it only had `-Id`; StrictMode threw "variable $Target ... not set" until declared. See [[rules-windows-pitfalls]].

## Medic hardening (on-disk, ~/.claude/loops untracked) — from the Stage D Restart smoke
Restarting the medic via the new verb WHILE I held the scheduled-tasks lock + ran concurrent Heal/Restart calls made the SCHEDULED instance exit 0x1, though the foreground run was clean 0. Root cause: the medic's task enumeration (`Get-ScheduledTask | Where...`) was the one **un-guarded CIM call in the hot path**, and CIM enumeration throws transiently under concurrent task start/modify — exactly the concurrency the medic operates within. It fail-closed correctly (RED+exit1), but a reliability tool shouldn't flip RED because a peer touched a task. Two fixes: (1) `Get-JarvisTasks` bounded retry (3x, 2s) — a real outage still fail-closes; (2) catch block now writes `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/last-error.txt` (msg+type+stack) so a fail-closed RED is diagnosable next session (webhook is unset). Re-verified: foreground exit 0, scheduled Restart -> 0x0 GREEN, no last-error.txt. LESSON: the medic must tolerate the concurrency it polices; capture your own failures when the notify channel is silent.

- Set User-scope `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` so heal-failures/escalations actually ping (currently silent no-op).

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\mattm\.claude\plugins\cache\claude-plugins-official\superpowers\6.1.0\skills\systematic-debugging

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Daemon-aware vault -> trading-brain sync (the autonomous ingest loop). Replaces the old
  second-brain\scripts\gbrain-bridge\sync.ps1, which drove `gbrain-trade.cmd sync` directly against
  PGlite -- that path throws on chunk writes now that the CLI runs engine=daemon, and its
  force-clear-stale-lock model is obsolete under the single-writer daemon.

.DESCRIPTION
  POSTs the vault repo to the daemon's /sync endpoint. The daemon runs gbrain's own performSync
  IN-PROCESS against the one PGlite connection: git-incremental (only files changed since the stored
  sync.last_commit), isSyncable-filtered (the curated subset, NOT the whole 44k-note vault), with
  add/modify/delete/rename + per-page embedding via the daemon's Voyage key. No lock fight, no
  corruption -- the daemon is the sole writer.

  SAFETY: the daemon refuses any sync whose stored anchor is missing or not an ancestor of HEAD
  (rebase/force-push) -- that path would FULL-reimport the entire repo + re-embed every chunk on the
  paid provider. Use -Force (allow_full) only when a full reimport is genuinely intended.

.PARAMETER DryRun   Compute + print the changeset without writing.
.PARAMETER Force    Permit a full reimport (allow_full) -- expensive; only when intended.
.PARAMETER Port     Daemon port (default 8077).

.EXAMPLE
  pwsh -File ~/tools/gbrain-vault-sync.ps1            # incremental sync
  pwsh -File ~/tools/gbrain-vault-sync.ps1 -DryRun    # preview changeset
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [switch]$DryRun,
  [switch]$Force,
  [int]$Port = 8077
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$base      = "http://127.0.0.1:$Port"
$VAULT     = 'C:\Users\mattm\master-jarvis\second-brain'
$LOG_DIR   = 'C:\Users\mattm\.gbrain-sync\log'
$logFile   = Join-Path $LOG_DIR ((Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') + '.log')
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $LOG_DIR | Out-Null
function Log($m) { $l = "$((Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')) $m"; Add-Content -Path $logFile -Value $l; Write-Host $l }

# Loud-fail if the daemon is down (don't silently no-op -- that was the old failure mode).
# Retry, though: /health serializes behind any in-flight embed, so a busy-but-alive daemon can miss a
# tight single probe (observed 2026-05-30: a tick that overlapped an `embed --all` of 4246 chunks
# false-FATALed on a 5s probe). 3 attempts x 10s with backoff distinguishes "busy" from "down" --
# a genuinely-down daemon still fails loudly within ~40s, well inside the task's 10-min limit.
$healthy = $false; $lastErr = ''
for ($attempt = 1; $attempt -le 3; $attempt++) {
  try { $null = Invoke-RestMethod "$base/health" -TimeoutSec 10; $healthy = $true; break }
  catch { $lastErr = $_.Exception.Message; if ($attempt -lt 3) { Start-Sleep -Seconds 3 } }
}
if (-not $healthy) { Log "[FATAL] daemon not reachable at $base after 3 tries ($lastErr). Start it: pwsh ~/tools/start-brain-daemon.ps1"; exit 2 }

$body = @{ repo = ($VAULT -replace '\\','/') }   # forward slashes: bun fs accepts them, avoids JSON escaping
if ($DryRun) { $body.dry_run = $true }
if ($Force)  { $body.allow_full = $true }
$json = $body | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

Log "[sync] POST /sync repo=$VAULT dry_run=$DryRun force=$Force"
try {
  $resp = Invoke-RestMethod "$base/sync" -Method Post -Body $json -ContentType 'application/json'
} catch {
  Log "[FATAL] /sync request failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; exit 1
}
if (-not $resp.accepted) { Log "[FAIL] not accepted: $($resp | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)"; exit 1 }

# Poll the shared ingest/sync status to completion. The daemon is single-threaded:
# while it imports + embeds a large changeset it can be unresponsive to /ingest for
# longer than a tight client timeout. A single slow probe must NOT abort the run --
# the sync is still progressing server-side (verified 2026-06-01: a 10s probe aborted
# the wrapper at exit 1 while the daemon went on to complete the sync cleanly in 97s).
# So: tolerate transient probe timeouts and keep polling; bound the whole wait by a
# deadline comfortably under the scheduled task's 10-minute hard limit.
$deadline = (Get-Date).AddMinutes(9)
while ($true) {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
  $st = $null
  try {
    $st = Invoke-RestMethod "$base/ingest" -TimeoutSec 30
  } catch {
    if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) { Log "[FATAL] sync still in flight past the 9-min poll deadline (last probe: $($_.Exception.Message))"; exit 1 }
    Log "[wait] daemon busy mid-sync (probe: $($_.Exception.Message)); retrying"
    continue
  }
  if (-not $st.running) {
    if ($st.last_error) { Log "[FAIL] $($st.last_error)"; exit 1 }
    $r = $st.last_result.sync
    if ($r) {
      Log ("[OK] {0}: +{1} ~{2} -{3} R{4}, {5} chunks; embedded {6}->{7}" -f `
            $r.status, $r.added, $r.modified, $r.deleted, $r.renamed, $r.chunksCreated, `
            $st.last_result.embedded_before, $st.last_result.embedded_after)
    } else { Log "[OK] $($st.last_result | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)" }
    break
  }
  if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) { Log "[FATAL] sync did not finish within the 9-min poll deadline"; exit 1 }
}

# Post-sync: rebuild the link graph. The daemon's /sync imports + embeds pages but does NOT
# extract links, so link_count drifts toward 0 as new pages arrive (orphans pile up,
# brain_score drops). The backfill is lock-safe (writes via /rpc, the daemon owns the writer)
# and idempotent. Best-effort: a backfill failure must never fail the sync task.
try {
  $bun      = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.bun\bin\bun.exe'
  $backfill = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\gbrain-backfill-links.ts'
  if ((Test-Path $bun) -and (Test-Path $backfill)) {
    Log "[links] rebuilding link graph..."
    $out = & $bun run $backfill 2>&1 | Out-String
    Log ("[links] " + $out.Trim())
  } else {
    Log "[links] skipped (bun or backfill script missing)"
  }
} catch {
  Log "[links] backfill error (non-fatal): $($_.Exception.Message)"
}
exit 0

**Root cause found — and it's already fixed.** The git history is the smoking gun:

- The failing run: **06-30 07:40** start → action completed **08:46:59 with `0x80070001` (=exit 1)**, and its roll-up shows `files=TIMEOUT` (a *required* task).
- The fix commit **`aeb8120` "TIMEOUT on required task is not a roll-up failure"** landed **06-30 18:50** — *~10 hours after* that run.

So the 07:40 run executed the **old code**, where a required task's `TIMEOUT` was treated as fatal. `Files` legitimately times out (it's an 11-min scan that finishes async), so the old code flagged it → false `0x1`. My isolated predicate test proved the **current** code yields `exit 0` for that exact summary. Working copy is clean = HEAD includes the fix.

**This is why checking recent changes matters** — I nearly added "diagnosability instrumentation" to fix an out-of-band failure that didn't exist. The real cause was a code-version mismatch at run time, already resolved.

## Verdict
- ✅ **Root cause: pre-`aeb8120` TIMEOUT-fatal logic. Already fixed.** No code change needed.
- The stale `0x1` is a leftover result from the pre-fix run; the **next scheduled 07:00 run (fixed code) exits 0 and clears it** — which lands before the medic's 09:30 pass, so the escalation resolves itself correctly.

## But I did find a real latent issue while in there
The gbrain sync log shows the **daemon restarts/crashes during essentially every hourly sync** — `connection actively refused (127.0.0.1:8077)` mid-sync, then recovers (uptime was 99s when I checked). The resilient sync wrapper tolerates it (exits 0), so it's *masked* — but a daemon that flaps every hour is a genuine instability: recall is briefly unavailable during syncs, and if it ever fails to come back, syncs start failing for real. That's the more valuable thread than the already-fixed `0x1`.

Self-healing = a triad — **fail-closed + idempotent cadence-retry + observable heal (RED->GREEN)** — layered: 0 contained work · 1 cadence retry (passive) · 2 active remediators · 3 escalation budget (transient vs permanent) · 4 watchdog revives dead loop/daemon · 5 fleet board. - `ConvertTo-LoopFault` (pure classifier) + `Get-LoopFaultSignature` (live-task wrapper).
- **Stage B** `Register-LoopResult -Id -State GREEN|RED -Budget K` over `~/.claude/loops/<id>/heal-state.json`: GREEN resets counter; RED increments; at K consecutive fails returns `Escalate` (no infinite retry). Default K=3.

A bare `0x800710E0` literal parses as a **negative Int32** (-2147020576) and `0xFFFFFFFF` as **-1** (so `-band 0xFFFFFFFF` is a no-op).
