<#
  start-brain-daemon.ps1 -- launch the single-writer gbrain brain daemon (M1 read + M3 write).

  Owns the ONE PGlite connection for the trading brain and the embed key (Voyage), resolved from the
  durable DPAPI secret store -- no 1Password app at runtime. Everything else talks to it over HTTP.

  Idempotent: if a daemon already holds the port it is a no-op success, so the at-logon task AND the
  watchdog (install-brain-daemon-task.ps1) can both re-run it without ever spawning a second opener
  -- the lock-collision this whole daemon exists to delete.

  -Detached : start the daemon hidden + return immediately (used by the scheduled tasks; logs ->
              ~/.gbrain-trading/logs). Without it, runs in the foreground; Ctrl-C releases the lock
              cleanly (daemon traps SIGINT/SIGTERM -> engine.disconnect()).
#>
param([switch]$Detached)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$bun         = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.bun\bin\bun.exe'
$daemon      = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\gbrain-src\src\daemon-server.ts'
$secretStore = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\secret-store.ps1'
$logDir      = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\logs'

$env:GBRAIN_DATABASE_PATH    = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\brain.pglite'
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_BASE_URL   = 'https://api.voyageai.com/v1'
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_MODEL      = 'voyage-finance-2'
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_DIMENSIONS = '1024'
if (-not $env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT) { $env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT = '8077' }

# Idempotent guard: if the port is already served, another daemon owns the lock -> do nothing.
$port = [int]$env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT
if (Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue) {
  Write-Host "[start-brain-daemon] daemon already listening on $port - nothing to do."
  exit 0
}

# Resolve the Voyage key from the durable DPAPI store (no 1Password app dependency at runtime).
$key = & pwsh -NoProfile -File $secretStore -Get VOYAGE_API_KEY 2>$null
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($key)) {
  Write-Error "VOYAGE_API_KEY not in secret store. Seed it once: pwsh $secretStore -Import VOYAGE_API_KEY -FromFile <one-line-key.txt>"
  exit 2
}
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_API_KEY = $key

Write-Host "[start-brain-daemon] port=$env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT  brain=$env:GBRAIN_DATABASE_PATH  model=$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_MODEL/$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_DIMENSIONS  detached=$Detached"

if ($Detached) {
  if (-not (Test-Path $logDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logDir -Force | Out-Null }
  $out = Join-Path $logDir 'daemon.out.log'
  $err = Join-Path $logDir 'daemon.err.log'
  # bun.exe is a native exe (not a .cmd shim), so Start-Process -FilePath works. The detached child
  # inherits the GBRAIN_* env set above and survives this launcher exiting (that is the point).
  # PIN the working directory to a durable dir: WITHOUT this the daemon inherits the launcher's cwd
  # (often a temp/worktree). If that dir is later deleted, the daemon stays up + /health green, but
  # execFileSync('git', ...) in /sync can no longer spawn (Windows CreateProcess can't resolve a dead
  # cwd) -- every git op then fails and is mis-reported as "No commits in repo" (observed 2026-05-30,
  # daemon pid 48728). $USERPROFILE never vanishes, so this deletes that failure class.
  Start-Process -FilePath $bun -ArgumentList @('run', "`"$daemon`"") -WindowStyle Hidden `
    -WorkingDirectory $env:USERPROFILE `
    -RedirectStandardOutput $out -RedirectStandardError $err
  Write-Host "[start-brain-daemon] launched detached; logs -> $logDir"
  exit 0
}
& $bun run $daemon

1	<#
2	.SYNOPSIS
3	  Install (or remove) the at-logon + watchdog scheduled tasks that keep the gbrain brain daemon
4	  running, so it is the always-on SOLE opener of brain.pglite (D4). Mirrors the proven
5	  JARVIS-TV-CDP-AtLogon pattern: pwsh shim path, battery flags (INC-2), MultipleInstances IgnoreNew,
6	  schtasks.exe fallback for HRESULT 0x80070057, and a watchdog that relaunches if the port drops.
7	
8	.DESCRIPTION
9	  AtLogon task : launches start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached at user logon.
10	  Watchdog     : every -WatchdogMinutes, re-runs the (idempotent) launcher -> relaunches if the
11	                 daemon port is down, no-ops if it is up.
12	  Both launchers are idempotent (port-check), so they never spawn a second opener.
13	
14	.PARAMETER Uninstall
15	  Remove both tasks (Unregister). Reversibility for the D4 flip.
16	
17	.PARAMETER DryRun
18	  Print what would be registered without touching the scheduler.
19	
20	.EXAMPLE
21	  pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/tools/install-brain-daemon-task.ps1
22	  pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/tools/install-brain-daemon-task.ps1 -Uninstall
23	#>
24	[CmdletBinding()]
25	param(
26	  [int]$Port = 8077,
27	  [int]$WatchdogMinutes = 5,
28	  [switch]$Uninstall,
29	  [switch]$DryRun
30	)
31	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
32	
33	$AtLogonName  = 'JARVIS-BrainDaemon-AtLogon'
34	$WatchdogName = 'JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog'
35	$launcher     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'   # AtLogon: idempotent start
36	$restarter    = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1' # Watchdog: heal down OR wedged
37	
38	# pwsh 7 shim (survives Store auto-updates per windows-pitfalls); fall back to system 5.1.
39	$pwsh = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe'
40	if (-not (Test-Path $pwsh)) { $pwsh = Join-Path $env:WINDIR 'System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe' }
41	
42	if ($Uninstall) {
43	  foreach ($n in @($AtLogonName, $WatchdogName)) {
44	    $t = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $n -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
45	    if ($t) {
46	      if ($DryRun) { Write-Host "[DryRun] would Unregister $n" }
47	      else { Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $n -Confirm:$false; Write-Host "Removed $n" }
48	    } else { Write-Host "$n not present" }
49	  }
50	  return

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Install (or remove) the at-logon + watchdog scheduled tasks that keep the gbrain brain daemon
  running, so it is the always-on SOLE opener of brain.pglite (D4). Mirrors the proven
  JARVIS-TV-CDP-AtLogon pattern: pwsh shim path, battery flags (INC-2), MultipleInstances IgnoreNew,
  schtasks.exe fallback for HRESULT 0x80070057, and a watchdog that relaunches if the port drops.

.DESCRIPTION
  AtLogon task : launches start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached at user logon.
  Watchdog     : every -WatchdogMinutes, re-runs the (idempotent) launcher -> relaunches if the
                 daemon port is down, no-ops if it is up.
  Both launchers are idempotent (port-check), so they never spawn a second opener.

.PARAMETER Uninstall
  Remove both tasks (Unregister). Reversibility for the D4 flip.

.PARAMETER DryRun
  Print what would be registered without touching the scheduler.

.EXAMPLE
  pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/tools/install-brain-daemon-task.ps1
  pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/tools/install-brain-daemon-task.ps1 -Uninstall
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [int]$Port = 8077,
  [int]$WatchdogMinutes = 5,
  [switch]$Uninstall,
  [switch]$DryRun
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$AtLogonName  = 'JARVIS-BrainDaemon-AtLogon'
$WatchdogName = 'JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog'
$launcher     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'   # AtLogon: idempotent start
$restarter    = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1' # Watchdog: heal down OR wedged

# pwsh 7 shim (survives Store auto-updates per windows-pitfalls); fall back to system 5.1.
$pwsh = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path $pwsh)) { $pwsh = Join-Path $env:WINDIR 'System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe' }

if ($Uninstall) {
  foreach ($n in @($AtLogonName, $WatchdogName)) {
    $t = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $n -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($t) {
      if ($DryRun) { Write-Host "[DryRun] would Unregister $n" }
      else { Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $n -Confirm:$false; Write-Host "Removed $n" }
    } else { Write-Host "$n not present" }
  }
  return
}

if (-not (Test-Path $launcher))  { Write-Error "launcher not found: $launcher"; exit 2 }
if (-not (Test-Path $restarter)) { Write-Error "restarter not found: $restarter"; exit 2 }

# AtLogon: idempotent detached start at boot. Watchdog: restart-brain-daemon -IfUnhealthy, which
# probes /health (not just the port) and heals a DOWN or WEDGED daemon — a bare port check can't tell
# a healthy daemon from a wedged one (port bound, /health dead), so it would never heal a wedge.
$atLogonArg   = "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$launcher`" -Detached"
$watchdogArg  = "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$restarter`" -IfUnhealthy"
$atLogonAction  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument $atLogonArg
$watchdogAction = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument $watchdogArg
# Battery flags are non-negotiable on this machine (INC-2: 0x800710E0). Both actions are detached and
# return fast, so a short ExecutionTimeLimit is fine. IgnoreNew: never stack runs.
$settings  = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `
               -StartWhenAvailable -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew -ExecutionTimeLimit (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 10)
$atLogonTrig  = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn -User "$env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME"
$watchdogTrig = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date).Date.AddMinutes(1) `
                  -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes $WatchdogMinutes) `
                  -RepetitionDuration ([TimeSpan]::FromDays(3650))

function Register-OrFallback($name, $trigger, $desc, $actionObj, $argStr) {
  if ($DryRun) { Write-Host "[DryRun] would register $name ($desc) -> $pwsh $argStr"; return }
  try {
    Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $name -Action $actionObj -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings `
      -RunLevel Limited -Description $desc -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
    Write-Host "Registered $name"
  } catch {
    # HRESULT 0x80070057 etc. -> schtasks.exe fallback, then clear the battery gate it sets by default.
    Write-Warning "Register-ScheduledTask failed for $name ($($_.Exception.Message)); trying schtasks.exe"
    $tr = "`"$pwsh`" $argStr"
    if ($name -eq $AtLogonName) {
      & schtasks.exe /Create /TN $name /TR $tr /SC ONLOGON /RL LIMITED /F | Out-Null
    } else {
      & schtasks.exe /Create /TN $name /TR $tr /SC MINUTE /MO $WatchdogMinutes /RL LIMITED /F | Out-Null
    }
    try {
      $s = (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $name).Settings
      $s.DisallowStartIfOnBatteries = $false
      $s.StopIfGoingOnBatteries     = $false
      Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName $name -Settings $s -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
      Write-Host "Registered $name via schtasks (battery gate cleared)"
    } catch { Write-Warning "Could not clear battery gate on ${name}: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
  }
}

Register-OrFallback $AtLogonName  $atLogonTrig  'gbrain brain daemon - launch at logon (single-writer sole opener)' $atLogonAction  $atLogonArg
Register-OrFallback $WatchdogName $watchdogTrig "gbrain brain daemon - watchdog (heal down/wedged daemon via /health probe, every $WatchdogMinutes min)" $watchdogAction $watchdogArg

if (-not $DryRun) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "Done. Verify: schtasks /Query /TN $AtLogonName /V /FO LIST"
  Write-Host "Daemon comes up at next logon, or run now: pwsh -File $launcher -Detached"
}

  relaunch DETACHED (session-independent, survives the shell that ran this). Use this instead of an
  ad-hoc Stop-Process -- the daemon owns the one PGlite connection, so an uncoordinated kill mid-ingest
  is the exact failure class this daemon exists to delete.

  Safe to kill when ingest is idle: PGlite transactions are atomic (a dropped connection rolls back,
  the heap stays intact). This script refuses to stop while an ingest is RUNNING unless -Force is given.

  -Force : stop even if an ingest is in progress (rolls back the in-flight embed batch; brain stays sound).

  -IfUnhealthy : no-op if the daemon already answers /health OK; otherwise stop + relaunch. This is the
  WATCHDOG entry point — a bare port check (start-brain-daemon's idempotency) can't tell a healthy
  daemon from a wedged one (port bound, /health dead), so the watchdog would never heal a wedge. With
  -IfUnhealthy the watchdog heals BOTH down and wedged daemons.

  Run it yourself (human-in-the-loop) when an agent's destructive-op guard blocks a raw kill:
    ! pwsh -NoProfile -File C:\Users\mattm\tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1
#>
param([int]$Port = 8077, [switch]$Force, [switch]$IfUnhealthy)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$launcher = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'

function Test-Port { Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $Port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue }

# generous timeout avoids killing a healthy-but-busy daemon (/health serializes individually and stays
# responsive even mid-ingest). ?deep=1 adds a child-spawn probe: a spawn-dead daemon (its cwd was
# deleted -> Windows CreateProcess fails) answers /health ok but can't run /sync's git ops -- treat
# spawn.ok=false as unhealthy so the watchdog heals it too. ($null spawn = older daemon w/o the probe;
# fall back to ok alone for backward compat during the upgrade window.) Any failure -> stop + relaunch.
if ($IfUnhealthy) {
  $healthy = $false
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10
    $spawnOk = ($null -eq $h.spawn) -or [bool]$h.spawn.ok
    $healthy = ([bool]$h.ok) -and $spawnOk
    if (([bool]$h.ok) -and -not $spawnOk) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health ok but spawn DEAD ($($h.spawn.error)) - healing spawn-dead daemon."

  } catch { $healthy = $false }

  Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] -IfUnhealthy: daemon down, wedged, or spawn-dead - healing."
}

# Refuse to yank the lock out from under a live embed unless forced.
if (Test-Port) {
  try {
    $st = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 5
    if ($st.ingest.running -and -not $Force) {
      Write-Error "daemon is mid-ingest (phase=$($st.ingest.phase)). Re-run with -Force to stop anyway, or wait for it to finish."

    }
  } catch { Write-Warning "port $Port up but /health unreachable; proceeding to stop." }
}

# Find and stop the daemon's bun process by command line (robust against pid drift).
$procs = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'" |
           Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*' }
foreach ($p in $procs) {
  Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] stopping bun pid $($p.ProcessId)"
  Stop-Process -Id $p.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

# Wait for the port (and thus the PGlite lock) to actually release.
$n = 0
while ((Test-Port) -and $n -lt 20) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500; $n++ }

# take well over 30s, so wait up to 90s before declaring failure (avoids a false "did not come up"
# that alarms the operator / could trigger spurious watchdog churn).
$n = 0
while ($n -lt 90) {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; $n++
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 3
    if ($h.ok) { Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] UP: pid=$($h.pid) model=$($h.embed.model)/$($h.embed.dim) chunks=$($h.stats.chunk_count) embedded=$($h.stats.embedded_count)"; exit 0 }
  } catch { }
}
Write-Error "daemon did not come up on $Port within 90s; check ~/.gbrain-trading/logs/daemon.err.log"

fix(gbrain-daemon): /health answers from memory while ingest.running, never queues behind the shared serialize() chain

Root cause of the gbrain daemon restarting roughly every hour (traced via
systematic-debugging while investigating the medic's Jarvis-VaultIngest-All
escalation): engine.getHealth()/getStats() are proxied through the single-writer
serialize() chain, so /health queues behind whatever ingest/sync step is
CURRENTLY running. /sync is the worst case (runIngest's sync_repo branch
deliberately runs performSync as ONE giant serialize() slot for its whole
duration, to avoid a proxy re-entrant-transaction deadlock), but a plain
/ingest can trip the same failure if a single embed step runs long.

When that queued step outlasts the watchdog's probe timeouts (5-10s),
restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy's client-side call throws; its own
ingest.running safety check queues behind the SAME chain and times out too,
so it falls through to "assume wedged" and force-kills a daemon that was
actually alive and correctly busy.

on essentially every hourly vault-sync AND a mem-ingest, each aligned exactly
to the watchdog's 5-min-past-:01 tick (JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog). The
aborted sync then silently reports "[OK] null" post-restart (a fresh process
has no last_result/last_error), masking the loss.

Fix: while ingest.running, /health answers entirely from in-memory state
(ingestStatus(), pid, uptime, embed config) and never touches engine.getHealth()/
getStats() -- so a busy-but-alive daemon reports honestly instead of looking
wedged, and the watchdog's own safety check succeeds fast enough to correctly
refuse the kill.

## gbrain daemon hourly-restart — root-caused + FIXED (commit `1ab0685` in ~/tools)
The "latent issue found in passing" above turned out to be real and live. Systematic-debugging trace: `~/tools/gbrain-src/src/daemon-server.ts`'s `/health` handler called `engine.getHealth()`/`engine.getStats()`, both proxied through the daemon's single-writer `serialize()` chain (`serializingEngine`). `/sync` deliberately runs `performSync` as ONE giant `serialize()` slot for its whole duration (avoids a proxy re-entrant-transaction deadlock) -- so `/health` queues behind an in-flight sync and can't resolve until it finishes; a plain `/ingest` can trip the same thing if one embed step runs long. `JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` (every 5min, anchor `:01`) runs `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy`, whose probe (5-10s timeout) times out when queued this way; its OWN `ingest.running` safety check ALSO queues behind the same chain and times out, so it falls to "assume wedged" and `Stop-Process -Force`s a daemon that was alive and correctly busy.
**Evidence:** `~/.gbrain-sync/log/2026-06-30.log` shows "connection actively refused" on essentially every hourly vault-sync AND a mem-ingest, each aligned exactly to the watchdog's 5-min-past-`:01` tick. The aborted sync then reports `[OK] null` post-restart (fresh process, no `last_result`/`last_error`) -- masking the loss as success.
**Fix:** while `ingest.running`, `/health` answers entirely from in-memory state (`ingestStatus()`, pid, uptime, embed config) -- never touches `engine.getHealth()`/`getStats()` -- so a busy daemon reports honestly instead of looking wedged, and the watchdog's own safety check now succeeds fast and correctly refuses the kill.
**Verified:** `bun build` clean; `bun test` 776 pass, 0 new failures (108 pre-existing are bare-`bun`-not-on-bash-PATH/unrelated CLI-e2e artifacts, none touch `daemon-server.ts`). Restarted the daemon live (sanctioned `restart-brain-daemon.ps1`, under `service:gbrain-daemon` lock, 6 peers active) -- new pid, brain state intact (chunks=5501 embedded=5493). **Live reproduction, twice:** raced a real (non-dry-run) `/sync` against a concurrent burst of `/health` polls. Run 1: caught the busy window returning `busy:true,ingest.running:true` in single-digit ms across ~20 polls (one early 5s stall, likely a post-restart first-call warm-up artifact). Run 2 (clean re-run): **20/20 fast, 0 slow, 0 errors.** Daemon pid unchanged before/after both runs -- no kill, no restart. ## Root cause found and fixed: gbrain daemon's hourly self-inflicted restarts

**The chain:** `/health` called `engine.getHealth()`/`getStats()`, which are proxied through the daemon's single-writer `serialize()` queue. `/sync` deliberately runs as **one giant unbroken slot** on that same queue (to avoid a transaction deadlock) — so `/health` silently queued behind any in-flight sync, contradicting its own code comment claiming it "stays responsive." The watchdog (`JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog`, every 5 min, anchored at `:01`) polls `/health` with a 5-10s timeout; when that queued, the client-side call timed out, the watchdog's own "is it mid-ingest?" safety check **timed out too** (same queue), so it fell through to "assume wedged" and force-killed a daemon that was actually alive and correctly busy.

**Evidence:** every hourly sync in yesterday's log showed "connection actively refused" precisely at the watchdog's `:01` tick — 12+ consecutive hours, no exceptions. The aborted sync then reported `[OK] null` post-restart, silently masking the loss as success.

**Fix** (commit `1ab0685`): while an ingest/sync is running, `/health` now answers from in-memory state only, never touching the shared queue.

**Verified live, not just by reading code:**
- `bun build` + `bun test` clean (776 pass, 0 regressions)
- Restarted the daemon under the resource lock — brain state intact
- Raced a **real** sync against burst `/health` polling, twice: run 2 was **20/20 fast responses, zero stalls, zero errors**, daemon pid unchanged throughout (no kill)

This was masked for a long time by resilient wrapper scripts logging false "OK" — the fix makes the daemon actually stable instead of silently self-healing around a real bug every hour.

<result>## Root cause found: latency-accounting bug, not an OpenAI problem

**File:** `C:\Users\mattm\ThinkorSwim\jarvis-trader\engine\llm\client.py`

**The mechanism (confirmed by code + `.env` config):**

`call()` sets `start_time = time.time()` **once**, at line 848, before the *original* Anthropic attempt. That timestamp is only ever reset in the RateLimit/APIStatusError retry-and-downgrade loop (lines 939 and 963). In the **credit-exhaustion cascade** (lines 992–1166) — Vertex failover → Gemini fallback → OpenAI fallback — `start_time` is **never reset**. `_handle_success()` (line 560) computes `latency_ms = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000`, so whichever leg finally succeeds gets billed for the wall-clock time of *every prior failed leg too*.

**Confirmed via `.env` (`engine\.env`):** `JARVIS_LLM_VERTEX_FAILOVER=1` (Vertex failover armed, with `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`/`REGION` set — so it makes a real network call, not a fast local-config failure), and both `GOOGLE_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` are present with their fallback flags at default-enabled. Per prior session memory (`project_vertex_quota_filed_llm_restored_2026_06_30`), **Vertex quota is denied** and **Google AI Studio is 429/quota-exhausted** — both confirmed dead. So on every credit-exhausted Anthropic call, the client burns real time trying two guaranteed-to-fail legs (each individually bounded by a 120s hard ceiling via `_bounded()`, and the Vertex leg additionally carries the Anthropic SDK's own internal retry/backoff on top of ours) **before** finally reaching OpenAI. That accumulated dead-leg time then gets misattributed to `gpt-4o-mini` in `/health/llm`'s per-model stats.

Ruled out per your list: max_tokens for debate agents (bull/bear/technical, `debate.py:1018/1241`, `bull_researcher.py:168/255/369`) are small (256–512), so oversized prompts/completions aren't the cause. `_call_openai` is a single httpx POST with no internal retry loop, so OpenAI's own serving latency is likely normal.

**Fixable, in two ways:**
1. **Metric fix (code, cheap):** reset `start_time` before each fallback attempt in the credit-exhaustion cascade, matching the existing pattern at lines 939/963.
2. **Actual latency fix (config, immediate):** since Vertex and Gemini are both confirmed dead right now, temporarily disabling the two known-broken legs (`JARVIS_LLM_VERTEX_FAILOVER=0`, `JARVIS_LLM_GOOGLE_FALLBACK=0`) would let credit-exhausted calls skip straight to OpenAI, eliminating the dead-leg wait entirely.

Not touched (read-only investigation only): no files edited, no restart, `.env` values redacted from this report per secret-hygiene rules.</result>

content.text: That's a real finding: the "85-second gpt-4o-mini latency" isn't OpenAI being slow — it's a **metric-accounting bug** where the timer starts once before the whole Anthropic→Vertex→Gemini→OpenAI cascade and never resets, so failed legs' dead time gets billed to whichever leg finally succeeds. And there's a second discovery that changes the picture further: my live test just now shows **Gemini/Google AI Studio is back up (HTTP 200)** — the prior "dead" verdict is stale. Let me look at the actual code to fix both cleanly.

                            # fall through to OpenAI fallback below

                    # Phase 3.6: both Anthropic and Gemini failed (or Gemini is
                    # disabled) — last-resort OpenAI before declaring the path
                    # unhealthy. Opus/Sonnet → gpt-4o, Haiku → gpt-4o-mini.
                    if self.openai_fallback_enabled:
                        openai_model = self.OPENAI_FAILOVER_MAP.get(
                            current_model, "gpt-4o-mini"
                        )
                        logger.warning(
                            f"[{current_model}] Anthropic+Gemini both failed for {agent_name} -- "
                            f"attempting OpenAI fallback ({openai_model})"
                        )
                        try:
                            openai_result = await self._bounded(
                                self._call_openai(
                                    system=system,
                                    messages=working_messages,
                                    max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                    temperature=temperature,
                                    model=openai_model,
                                ),
                                what="openai fallback call",
                                model=openai_model,
                                agent_name=agent_name,
                            )
                            self.openai_fallback_count += 1
                            _LLM_PATH_STATE["healthy"] = True
                            _LLM_PATH_STATE["last_failure_ts"] = datetime.now(
                                timezone.utc
                            ).isoformat()
                            _LLM_PATH_STATE["last_failure_reason"] = (
                                f"anthropic+gemini failed -> openai fallback ok "
                                f"(count: {self.openai_fallback_count})"
                            )
                            _LLM_PATH_STATE["last_failure_agent"] = agent_name
                            return await self._handle_success(
                                openai_result,
                                openai_model,
                                start_time,
                                retries,
                                agent_name,
                                tier=tier,
                                proxy=proxy,
                                compressed_key=compressed_key,
                                cache_salt=cache_salt,
                            )
                        except Exception as oex:
                            logger.error(
                                f"[{openai_model}] OpenAI fallback also failed for {agent_name}: {oex}"
                            )
                            # fall through to unhealthy-path handling below

                    _LLM_PATH_STATE["healthy"] = False
                    _LLM_PATH_STATE["last_failure_ts"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
                    _LLM_PATH_STATE["last_failure_reason"] = body_str[:500]
                    _LLM_PATH_STATE["last_failure_agent"] = agent_name
                    try:
                        from notifications.openclaw_notifier import notify_credits_exhausted

                        asyncio.create_task(
                            notify_credits_exhausted(reason=body_str[:300], agent=agent_name)
                        )
                    except Exception as notify_err:
                        logger.debug(f"credits-exhausted notifier failed: {notify_err}")
                break

        return await self._handle_failure(
            last_error, current_model, start_time, retries, agent_name, tier=tier
        )

    def _messages_to_ollama_prompt(self, system: str, messages: list[dict]) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        if system:
            parts.append(f"System:\n{system}")
        for message in messages:
            role = message.get("role", "user")
            content = message.get("content", "")

# Loop Engineering — Amo

> A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes.
> Loop engineering is the default posture for any goal that is recurring, multi-pass, unbounded, or
> must converge to a bar. Established 2026-06-30 ("loop engineering is the new future instead of prompts").

## The core shift

Stop thinking "what do I prompt for this?" and start thinking "what loop pursues this?" Most durable
value on this machine is not a one-shot answer — it's a process that runs, remembers, self-corrects,
and tells Amo only when it needs him. When a goal is stated, ask: **is this a turn, or a loop?**

- **Turn** (answer once, done): a lookup, a single edit, a one-time analysis. Just do it.
- **Loop** (runs until a condition): recurring cadence, draining a backlog, converging a metric,
  watching external state, sweeping N items. → **compile it with `/loopify`.**

If in doubt and the goal contains "keep", "every", "until", "whenever", "monitor", "maintain",
"get X above Y", or "for each of these N" — it's a loop.

## The toolchain (three verbs)

| Verb | Tool | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **compile** | `/loopify <goal>` | goal → classify → ledger → runner → brakes → feedback → register + auto-deploy |
| **operate** | `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1` | Register / Deploy / List / Status / Remove / Heartbeat over `~/.claude/loops/registry.json` |
| **observe** | `/loops` | fleet board: what's running, what's stale, what's red, one-line-per-loop |
| **heal** | `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1 -Action Heal\|Restart`, `~/scripts/loop-heal.ps1`, `Loopify-loop-medic` | classify a fault → remediate safe faults / escalate the rest. `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <loop>` previews (dry-run); `-Apply` executes; `-Action Restart` re-runs a stalled task. The `loop-medic` scheduled task does this on cadence (dry-run until Amo flips `-DoApply`). |

`/loopify` is the compiler; you rarely hand-author a loop. Reach for loopctl directly only to inspect,
kill, or **heal** (`-Action Heal`/`Restart` share the `loop-heal.ps1` catalog the medic runs). `/loops`
is the read-only dashboard.

**Self-healing model (the 4th verb).** Layered: 0 contained work · 1 idempotent cadence-retry (passive) ·
2 active remediators (`loop-heal.ps1`: battery-gate / hung-runner / dead-loop auto-heal; escalate-class
faults NEVER auto-act — inherits the destructive-op gate) · 3 escalation budget (K consecutive REDs →
page, no infinite retry) · 4 the `loop-medic` watchdog revives dead loops fleet-health only *reports* ·
5 the `/loops` board. A remediator that mutates must claim the `scheduled-tasks` resource lock and
tolerate the concurrency it polices (bounded retry on CIM enumeration). Detail: [[project_loop_self_healing_2026_07_01]].

## Archetype taxonomy (first match wins)

| Goal shape | Archetype | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| watch external state, act on change | dynamic | `/loop`+ScheduleWakeup, or a poller |
| drain a known finite backlog | backlog-drain | `/ralph` |
| drain a backlog that regenerates (re-discover each pass) | discovery-drain | `/jarvis-loop` |
| push a metric to a bar (generate→judge→improve) | evaluator-optimizer | in-session or `Workflow` |
| clock-fired read/compute/report | scheduled-cadence | local task OR cloud routine |
| one big parallel pass + verify | fan-out-verify | `Workflow` |
| propose → check → commit | maker-checker | in-session or `Workflow` |

## Runner selection — the one hard rule

**Anything touching `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local file
runs LOCAL (scheduled task or in-session) — NEVER a cloud routine.** The cloud sandbox cannot see the
local disk and fails silently. Cloud routines are only for pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar /
Drive / web. (Same rule as `workflow.md` § Scheduling.)

## The brakes contract (non-negotiable)

No loop deploys without all six. This is the line between an engineered loop and a runaway:

1. **Preflight** — verify deps; abort clean if down (don't act on a dead dependency).
2. **Heartbeat** — stamp GREEN/RED/ERROR each iteration via `loopctl -Heartbeat`; a dead loop stops stamping.
3. **Fail-closed** — error ⇒ RED + notify + non-zero exit. Never green-on-error, never "no error in the log so it worked".
4. **Stop condition** — the written done-predicate, checked every iteration.
5. **Budget/iteration cap** — hard ceiling (iterations / tokens / wall-clock) as the backstop.
6. **Notify** — on RED/stop/budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK`); no-op silently if unset, never throw.

PowerShell runners get brakes 1-3+6 pre-wired from `skills/loopify/templates/scheduled-runner.ps1`
and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. A `Workflow` gets them from `budget.total`, a
loop-until-dry/count guard, and an adversarial verify stage.

## Safety envelope (full auto-deploy)

Amo's standing autonomy for `/loopify` is **full auto-deploy**: safe loops register, deploy, and start
themselves. Safe = read-only, report, local-fs analysis, in-repo maker-checker. A loop whose
**steady-state action** is destructive or outward-facing does NOT auto-deploy live — it compiles, then
stops at a human gate:

- live trades or flipping a paper/live flag
- `git push` to a shared branch, or force-push
- secret / `.env` / 1Password mutation
- file delete or mass-move (always archive, never delete)
- unguarded prod-service restart (engine, Hermes)
- messages to third parties (anyone but Amo)

For those: compile fully, register `status=blocked`, deploy in report-only / dry-run / flag-off mode,
and surface with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The machine's PreToolUse hooks
(credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the second line of defense — the
design-time gate is the first.

## Anti-patterns

- Deploying without a stop condition → runaway. Stage-2 predicate is mandatory.
- Green-on-error → silent failure looks healthy. Fail-closed.
- Cloud routine reading local fs → silent no-op. Local runner.
- Self-grading evaluator → never converges. Use an independent judge.
- Night-scheduled task (00:00-05:59) → machine asleep, 0xFFFD0000. Schedule 09:00-11:00.
- One loop per file/finding → fleet noise. Group related work.
- Loop invisible on the board → always Register, even in-session/Workflow.

## Cross-references

- Compiler skill: `~/.claude/skills/loopify/SKILL.md`
- Control plane: `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1` · registry `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`
- Board: `/loops`
- Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling
- Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `rules/windows-pitfalls.md`
- Verify-before-claiming: `rules/verification.md`
- Destructive-op gate: `rules/destructive-op-gates.md`
- In-the-wild loop skills: `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`, `/loop`

# Workflow Rules — Amo

Universal workflow patterns. Project-specific rules live in `rules/<project>.md` (e.g. `rules/jarvis-trader.md`).

## Ground before acting (graph recall) — established 2026-06-24

Before any **substantive** task that touches prior work, a past decision, or a known bug,
**run graph recall FIRST** to ground in what's already known plus the connected context:

```
pwsh -File ~/scripts/recall-graph.ps1 "<topic>"      # or the /vault <question> command
```

This returns semantic seeds **plus the documents they link to** (not isolated chunks), so you
don't re-derive a settled decision or contradict a past call. **Auto-invoke it -- don't wait to
be asked** -- whenever the task is non-trivial and the knowledge base plausibly covers it. Skip
only for genuinely novel work or trivial lookups.

- Curated entry points: [[moc_index]] -> [[moc_trading_campaign]] / [[moc_knowledge_system]] /
  [[moc_ops_business]] / [[moc_build_dev]].
- Recall is current: the memory corpus auto-ingests (`Jarvis-MemoryGbrainIngest` daily; on-demand
  `~/tools/gbrain-memory-ingest.ps1`) and the vault syncs hourly.
- Mechanism + caveats: `reference_graph_aware_recall_2026_06_24`.

## Package Managers

- **Node.js**: `pnpm` always — system `npm` is broken system-wide
- **Python**: per-project venv (e.g. `engine/.venv/Scripts/python` for jarvis-trader). Never system Python 3.14 or Microsoft Store Python.
- **TypeScript check**: `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` (NOT `npx tsc`)

## Model Tiering

- **haiku** → Explore agents (codebase search, file lookups, orientation)
- **sonnet** → Implementation agents (writing/fixing code)
- **opus** → Planning agents, safety review, Tier 3 architecture decisions

## Parallel Agents — Standing Order

- Deploy **10 parallel agents** for any non-trivial task
- Keep 10 running — replace any that stop
- `run_in_background=true` FAILS (ENOTFOUND) on this machine — foreground only
- Background Bash commands work fine; only Agent-tool background mode is broken

## Commit Style (summary)

Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `build:`. Never commit `.env` files, secrets, or credentials. Never `git add -A` blindly. Full guidance in `rules/git-hygiene.md`.

## Session Habits

- `/clear` between unrelated tasks
- `/compact` when approaching context limits — don't fight it
- Save handoffs at milestone boundaries, not every 5 responses (see `rules/handoffs.md`)

## Scheduling — pick the right runner

| Pattern | Tool |
|---|---|
| Local fs / installed-tooling / IB / pm2 / engine state | **Windows Task Scheduler** (`~/scripts/install-regression-tasks.ps1` for the canonical 8; `Register-ScheduledTask` or `schtasks.exe` for ad-hoc) |
| Gmail / Calendar / Drive / cross-account audits / pure cognition | **`/schedule` cloud routines** |
| Bridge | Local task → email/Telegram → cloud routine reads via Gmail MCP |

`/schedule` runs in Anthropic's sandbox and **cannot see `C:\Users\mattm\`**. Never wrap local-fs scans (scan-credentials, tool-health, etc.) as cloud routines — they fail silently in the sandbox.

Phase 7 regression agents (`scan-credentials`, `scan-uncommitted`, `disk-watch`, `tool-health`, `repo-remote-check`, `archive-rotate`, `memory-hygiene`, plus `sweep-orphan-claude-procs`) are local-fs work — installed via `~/scripts/install-regression-tasks.ps1`. Do **not** try to wrap them as `/schedule` routines.

For Windows Scheduled Task pitfalls (HRESULT 0x80070057, shim paths, etc.) → `rules/windows-pitfalls.md`.

## Cross-references

| Topic | File |
|---|---|
| JARVIS TRADER specifics | `rules/jarvis-trader.md` |

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map, list_code_components, get_code_component_info)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
… [truncated]

## claude.ai Gamma
Gamma creates AI-powered presentations, documents, webpages, and social posts. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults - when in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. The read_gamma tool can read the content of an existing Gamma when given its file ID. Existing gammas have a type: "template" or "regular". Only templates can be used with generate_from_template; use get_gammas with type="template" to discover valid templates. Non-template IDs are not valid inputs to generate_from_template. If generate_from_template reports that an ID is inaccessible or not a template, find a valid template with get_gammas(type="template"). If the user's intent is to create a new gamma, but not by using an existing template, then use the generate tool. IMPORTANT: The tools provided by this server cannot edit or modify existing gammas. Do not suggest that you can make changes, adjustments, or refinements to a generated gamma. Instead, let the user know they can customize their gamma directly in the Gamma editor.

## repomix
Repomix MCP Server provides AI-optimized codebase analysis tools. Use pack_codebase or pack_remote_repository to consolidate code into a single XML file, use generate_skill to create Claude Agent Skills from codebases, use attach_packed_output to work with existing packed outputs, then read_repomix_output and grep_repomix_output to analyze it. Perfect for code reviews, documentation generation, bug investigation, GitHub repository analysis, and understanding large codebases. Includes security scanning and supports compression for token efficiency.

1	---
2	name: project_corey_llm_vertex_failover_2026_06_30
3	description: Corey structured-bias extraction died 06-29 because ALL non-Vertex LLM providers are dead; fix = route standalone surfaces through JarvisLLMClient + arm Vertex in engine/.env + /health extraction-lag detector
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 515f51f1-07f3-4232-a609-fd05925ee1a3
8	---
9	
10	# Corey bias-extraction outage → multi-provider LLM death + Vertex-only lifeline (2026-06-30)
11	
12	**Trigger:** Amo asked "does the discord-jarvis MCP actually bridge Corey's #market-updates?"
13	Bridge ingestion + keyword `get_daily_sentiment` + `search_commentary` were all healthy/fresh
14	(last market-updates msg current to the morning). But **structured `get_session_bias` degraded to
15	`data_quality='none'` since 2026-06-29** (was `fresh` through 06-28). Cache `corey_session_bias`
16	had NO rows for 06-29/06-30 (the code skips caching LLM failures — `6d3b22f`).
17	
18	## Root cause (the big finding): every non-Vertex LLM provider is dead
19	Reproduced the exact failover chain via `JarvisLLMClient`:
20	- **Anthropic direct** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, 1P `jarvis-engine/password`): `400` "credit balance too low"
21	- **Google AI Studio / Gemini** (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`): `429` "prepayment credits are depleted"
22	- **OpenAI** (`OPENAI_API_KEY` in engine/.env): `401` invalid key
23	- **Claude-on-Vertex** (SA `jarvis-vertex-sa.json`, GCP billing): **WORKS** (both us-east5 & us-central1)
24	
25	So the engine survives ONLY on Claude-on-Vertex. The **standalone surfaces** (MCP server
26	`mcp_server.py`, `discord.cli --trigger-commentary`, briefing, `corey_compare`) built
27	`CoreyCommentaryProcessor()` with **no llm_client → raw httpx POST to api.anthropic.com** (dead
28	credit), never touching the failover client. The **live engine** is insulated because
29	`main.py:816` builds `CoreyAuctionAnalystAgent(llm_client=llm_client)` → routes through
30	`JarvisLLMClient`.
31	
32	## Two gaps that kept Vertex from working
33	1. **Config:** `engine/.env` was missing `JARVIS_VERTEX_MODEL_MAP` + `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`
34	   (region had drifted to us-central1). Without the model map, `client.py:1504` sends the raw model
35	   name → Vertex `404`. The map lives ONLY in `~/scripts/arm-vertex-failover.ps1` (writes a 5-line
36	   block into engine/.env) — it had never been (re)armed/clobbered.
37	2. **Code:** standalone processor used the raw direct-POST, not the client.
38	
39	## What I did (this session)
40	- **Armed Vertex** in `engine/.env` (backup `.env.bak-20260630-143547`). NOTE: `arm-vertex-failover.ps1`
41	  FAILED here — its `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` mints a token for the wrong
42	  identity (user ADC, no project access) → 404s on every model. The **SA-creds path works** (python
43	  `google-auth` via `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`), so I wrote the block directly. Validated map:
44	  `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001=claude-haiku-4-5@20251001,claude-sonnet-4-6=claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929,claude-opus-4-7=claude-opus-4-1@20250805`.
45	  Region `us-east5`. (A peer flipped `JARVIS_CLAUDE_USE_VERTEX` 1→0 mid-session; failover leg covers it.)
46	- **Code (committed `2a327eb` on branch `fix/corey-standalone-vertex-routing`, stacked on
47	  `fix/corey-cache-stale-nodata`, NOT pushed/merged — neither on master):**
48	  `build_default_llm_client()` in `commentary_processor.py` (anchored cost-DB, returns None never
49	  raises) wired into MCP/CLI/corey_compare; CLI also loads engine/.env. Plus
50	  `get_bias_extraction_health()` (cache-only; flags when bias lags commentary >=2 days — the gap that
51	  hid this from /health) surfaced under `/health futures_sentiment.extraction_quality`. 9 new tests, 29 green.
52	- **Re-extracted** 06-29 (fresh, neutral, conv 0.45) and 06-30 (fresh, bullish, conv 0.75) via Vertex,
53	  zero Anthropic credit.
54	
55	## UPDATE 2026-06-30 PM — engine restarted, /health verified, + response_model strip fixed
56	- **Engine RESTARTED** (twice) and **/health gate GREEN**: status=ok, llm_path_healthy/tv_mcp/
57	  ibkr/ibgateway all true, paper_mode, kill_switch off. Context shifted since the arming: **Amo
58	  topped up Anthropic**, so a peer restarted to **`active_provider=anthropic` / primary_healthy=true /
59	  4 providers / single_leg_warning=false / vertex_failover_count=0** — Anthropic is the live primary
60	  again; **Vertex is the armed-but-inert failover leg** (per peer [[project_vertex_quota_filed_llm_restored_2026_06_30]]
61	  Vertex is actually still 404/global-only & quota-pending, but moot while Anthropic primary is healthy).
62	- **Found + fixed a response_model strip (commit `e65d7c0`, same branch):** the C deliverable's
63	  `futures_sentiment.extraction_quality` detector (and `pending_approvals`) were built in
64	  `_health_inner()` but **`HealthResponse` (engine/api/models.py) didn't declare the fields, so
65	  FastAPI's `response_model` silently stripped them before the wire** — the EXACT bug that hid
66	  `llm_providers` from /health until 2026-06-06 (documented in that field's own docstring). Detector
67	  ran but never reached the client. Added both as `Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` + a regression test
68	  asserting the model round-trips them. After restart, **/health now shows
69	  `futures_sentiment.extraction_quality="ok"`, lag 0, latest_bias_date 2026-06-30** — verified live.
70	- **DURABLE HAZARD (reusable):** any NEW key added to a `_health_inner`/endpoint response dict is
71	  **invisible on the wire unless a matching field is added to the `response_model` Pydantic class**
72	  (FastAPI strips undeclared keys; `SubsystemStatus` dodges this via `extra="allow"`, `HealthResponse`
73	  does NOT). Has now bitten /health twice (llm_providers 06-06, futures_sentiment 06-30).
74	
75	## MERGED 2026-06-30 PM — PR #209 squash-landed on master (`aaee31d`)
76	- The local branch `fix/corey-standalone-vertex-routing` was **76 commits ahead of master** (the whole
77	  cache-stale-nodata stack: x-twitter MCP, ATR-trail backtests, brief Phases A–F, dashboard, etc. —
78	  most already on master via separate squashed PRs). NOT mergeable as-is. The actual deliverable is the
79	  **2 Corey commits** (`2a327eb` + `e65d7c0`) = a clean 7-file / 349-line delta.
80	- **Clean path used:** cherry-picked just those 2 commits onto a fresh branch off **origin/master** (local
81	  master was stale at #180; origin was at #204) in an **isolated worktree** (peers live + main tree dirty
82	  w/ unrelated drift) → tested (14 green vs origin/master base) → pushed → PR #209 → **squash-merged**
83	  (`aaee31d`). Vercel checks were UNSTABLE-not-BLOCKED (dashboard-only, irrelevant to engine Python).
84	- **`corey_compare.py` EXCLUDED:** it's Phase F ("JARVIS vs Corey", dormant) and **not on master**

description: Corey structured-bias extraction died 06-29 because ALL non-Vertex LLM providers are dead; fix = route standalone surfaces through JarvisLLMClient + arm Vertex in engine/.env + /health extraction-lag detector
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 515f51f1-07f3-4232-a609-fd05925ee1a3

# Corey bias-extraction outage → multi-provider LLM death + Vertex-only lifeline (2026-06-30)

**Trigger:** Amo asked "does the discord-jarvis MCP actually bridge Corey's #market-updates?"
Bridge ingestion + keyword `get_daily_sentiment` + `search_commentary` were all healthy/fresh
(last market-updates msg current to the morning). But **structured `get_session_bias` degraded to
`data_quality='none'` since 2026-06-29** (was `fresh` through 06-28). Cache `corey_session_bias`
had NO rows for 06-29/06-30 (the code skips caching LLM failures — `6d3b22f`).

## Root cause (the big finding): every non-Vertex LLM provider is dead
Reproduced the exact failover chain via `JarvisLLMClient`:
- **Anthropic direct** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, 1P `jarvis-engine/password`): `400` "credit balance too low"
- **Google AI Studio / Gemini** (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`): `429` "prepayment credits are depleted"
- **OpenAI** (`OPENAI_API_KEY` in engine/.env): `401` invalid key
- **Claude-on-Vertex** (SA `jarvis-vertex-sa.json`, GCP billing): **WORKS** (both us-east5 & us-central1)

So the engine survives ONLY on Claude-on-Vertex. The **standalone surfaces** (MCP server
`mcp_server.py`, `discord.cli --trigger-commentary`, briefing, `corey_compare`) built
`CoreyCommentaryProcessor()` with **no llm_client → raw httpx POST to api.anthropic.com** (dead
credit), never touching the failover client. The **live engine** is insulated because
`main.py:816` builds `CoreyAuctionAnalystAgent(llm_client=llm_client)` → routes through
`JarvisLLMClient`.

## Two gaps that kept Vertex from working
1. **Config:** `engine/.env` was missing `JARVIS_VERTEX_MODEL_MAP` + `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`
   (region had drifted to us-central1). Without the model map, `client.py:1504` sends the raw model
   name → Vertex `404`. The map lives ONLY in `~/scripts/arm-vertex-failover.ps1` (writes a 5-line
   block into engine/.env) — it had never been (re)armed/clobbered.
2. **Code:** standalone processor used the raw direct-POST, not the client.

## What I did (this session)
- **Armed Vertex** in `engine/.env` (backup `.env.bak-20260630-143547`). NOTE: `arm-vertex-failover.ps1`
  FAILED here — its `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` mints a token for the wrong
  identity (user ADC, no project access) → 404s on every model. The **SA-creds path works** (python
  `google-auth` via `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`), so I wrote the block directly. Validated map:
  `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001=claude-haiku-4-5@20251001,claude-sonnet-4-6=claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929,claude-opus-4-7=claude-opus-4-1@20250805`.
  Region `us-east5`. (A peer flipped `JARVIS_CLAUDE_USE_VERTEX` 1→0 mid-session; failover leg covers it.)
- **Code (committed `2a327eb` on branch `fix/corey-standalone-vertex-routing`, stacked on
  `fix/corey-cache-stale-nodata`, NOT pushed/merged — neither on master):**
  `build_default_llm_client()` in `commentary_processor.py` (anchored cost-DB, returns None never
  raises) wired into MCP/CLI/corey_compare; CLI also loads engine/.env. Plus
  `get_bias_extraction_health()` (cache-only; flags when bias lags commentary >=2 days — the gap that
  hid this from /health) surfaced under `/health futures_sentiment.extraction_quality`. 9 new tests, 29 green.
- **Re-extracted** 06-29 (fresh, neutral, conv 0.45) and 06-30 (fresh, bullish, conv 0.75) via Vertex,
  zero Anthropic credit.

## UPDATE 2026-06-30 PM — engine restarted, /health verified, + response_model strip fixed
- **Engine RESTARTED** (twice) and **/health gate GREEN**: status=ok, llm_path_healthy/tv_mcp/
  ibkr/ibgateway all true, paper_mode, kill_switch off. Context shifted since the arming: **Amo
  topped up Anthropic**, so a peer restarted to **`active_provider=anthropic` / primary_healthy=true /
  4 providers / single_leg_warning=false / vertex_failover_count=0** — Anthropic is the live primary
  again; **Vertex is the armed-but-inert failover leg** (per peer [[project_vertex_quota_filed_llm_restored_2026_06_30]]
  Vertex is actually still 404/global-only & quota-pending, but moot while Anthropic primary is healthy).
- **Found + fixed a response_model strip (commit `e65d7c0`, same branch):** the C deliverable's
  `futures_sentiment.extraction_quality` detector (and `pending_approvals`) were built in
  `_health_inner()` but **`HealthResponse` (engine/api/models.py) didn't declare the fields, so
  FastAPI's `response_model` silently stripped them before the wire** — the EXACT bug that hid
  `llm_providers` from /health until 2026-06-06 (documented in that field's own docstring). Detector
  ran but never reached the client. Added both as `Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` + a regression test
  asserting the model round-trips them. After restart, **/health now shows
  `futures_sentiment.extraction_quality="ok"`, lag 0, latest_bias_date 2026-06-30** — verified live.
- **DURABLE HAZARD (reusable):** any NEW key added to a `_health_inner`/endpoint response dict is
  **invisible on the wire unless a matching field is added to the `response_model` Pydantic class**
  (FastAPI strips undeclared keys; `SubsystemStatus` dodges this via `extra="allow"`, `HealthResponse`
  does NOT). Has now bitten /health twice (llm_providers 06-06, futures_sentiment 06-30).

## MERGED 2026-06-30 PM — PR #209 squash-landed on master (`aaee31d`)
- The local branch `fix/corey-standalone-vertex-routing` was **76 commits ahead of master** (the whole
  cache-stale-nodata stack: x-twitter MCP, ATR-trail backtests, brief Phases A–F, dashboard, etc. —
  most already on master via separate squashed PRs). NOT mergeable as-is. The actual deliverable is the
  **2 Corey commits** (`2a327eb` + `e65d7c0`) = a clean 7-file / 349-line delta.
- **Clean path used:** cherry-picked just those 2 commits onto a fresh branch off **origin/master** (local
  master was stale at #180; origin was at #204) in an **isolated worktree** (peers live + main tree dirty
  w/ unrelated drift) → tested (14 green vs origin/master base) → pushed → PR #209 → **squash-merged**
  (`aaee31d`). Vercel checks were UNSTABLE-not-BLOCKED (dashboard-only, irrelevant to engine Python).
- **`corey_compare.py` EXCLUDED:** it's Phase F ("JARVIS vs Corey", dormant) and **not on master**
  (`git log origin/master -- ...` empty; no master code imports it). The cherry-pick hit a modify/delete
  conflict; resolved by `git rm` (accept master's absence). Phase F's failover wiring travels with the
  Phase F branch (`feat/corey-compare-forecast-journal` worktree). CAVEAT: when Phase F merges, its
  `corey_compare.py` predates `2a327eb` so it'll re-introduce the raw-direct-POST bug unless rewired.

## STILL NEEDED (gated / Amo) — restart + merge now DONE
- ~~Restart engine~~ ✅ done + verified. ~~Merge branch~~ ✅ PR #209 → master `aaee31d`.
- **Relaunch the discord-jarvis MCP** (new Claude session) to activate the standalone code fix +
  armed env — the MCP is a separate process; restarting the engine does NOT reload it.
- **Billing redundancy (Amo chose all):** Anthropic ✅ topped up. Google AI Studio + OpenAI key
  still pending so Vertex isn't the sole backstop.

Observed symptom: `/health/llm` reported 30-85s "gpt-4o-mini latency" that was actually misattributed Vertex/Gemini failure time, not real OpenAI slowness -- skewing every latency/cost dashboard during a credit-exhaustion event.

## Fix

Insert `start_time = time.time()` immediately before each of the three fallback `try:` blocks (Vertex, Gemini, OpenAI) so each leg's `latency_ms` measures only that leg. Three lines, no behavior change beyond metric accuracy.

## Testing

`test_llm_client.py`, `test_llm_client_error_surfacing.py`, `test_corey_llm_client_factory.py` -- **21 passed** against the origin/master base (d15a0b7).

<#
  loop-medic -- Stage C of the self-healing stack. Detect -> match -> HEAL -> re-verify,
  escalate to Amo ONLY when auto-heal fails or the fault is escalate-class. Closes the
  layer-4 gap: fleet-health only REPORTS stale/failing loops; the medic REVIVES them.

  Companion, not duplicate: the medic HEALS (runs 09:30), fleet-health REPORTS the
  cleaner board (10:00). The medic never posts a routine digest -- it acts, then pings
  only on a heal-failure or an escalate-class fault.

  SAFETY:
    * Default is DRY-RUN. Without -DoApply it mutates NOTHING -- it reports what it WOULD
      heal (Invoke-LoopHeal -WhatIf). Flip -DoApply to let it actually heal.
    * Only safe/idempotent remediators run (battery-gate, hung-runner, dead-loop).
      Destructive/funding faults return Escalate from loop-heal and are never auto-acted.
    * Claims the scheduled-tasks resource lock before any mutation (peer-safe).
    * Thrash guard: a target healed >= ThrashBudget times is escalated, not re-healed --
      a fault that won't stay fixed is a human problem, not a loop to paper over.
    * MaxHealsPerRun caps mutations per fire. Runtime cap + fail-closed + heartbeat.

  Exit: 0 OK | 1 ERROR (RED + notify).  ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $MedicId = 'loop-medic',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 240,
    [switch] $DoApply,                 # OFF (default) = dry-run; ON = actually heal
    [int]    $MaxHealsPerRun = 6,
    [int]    $ThrashBudget = 3
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl    = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal   = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'
$lockScript = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\claude-resource-lock.ps1'
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

function Send-MedicNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$MedicId] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

# Pure decision helper -- returns a bucket + message; caller owns the state.
function Get-HealAction {
    param(
        [string] $Sig, [string] $Target, [string] $Label,
        [bool] $Apply, [int] $HealCount, [int] $MaxHeals, [int] $Thrash, [hashtable] $Log
    )
    $count = 0
    if ($Log.ContainsKey($Target)) { $count = [int]$Log[$Target] }
    if ($count -ge $Thrash) {
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='escalate'; msg="$Label ($Sig): auto-healed $count times already -- WON'T STAY HEALED, needs a human"; target=$Target }
    }
    if ($Apply -and $HealCount -lt $MaxHeals) {
        $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target
        if ($r.decision -eq 'Healed') { return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='healed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): $($r.action)"; target=$Target } }
        return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='failed'; msg="$Label ($Sig): heal FAILED -- $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
    }
    $r = Invoke-LoopHeal -Fault $Sig -Target $Target -WhatIf
    return [pscustomobject]@{ bucket='would'; msg="$Label ($Sig): would $($r.action)"; target=$Target }
}

# Enumerating scheduled tasks can throw a transient CIM error when a peer session or another
# loop is starting/modifying a task at the same moment -- exactly the concurrency the medic is
# built to operate within. Retry a few times before giving up (a real outage still fail-closes).
function Get-JarvisTasks {
    $attempt = 0
    while ($true) {
        $attempt++
        try {
            return @(Get-ScheduledTask -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -match '^(Jarvis|JARVIS|Hermes|DP600|Loopify)-' })
        } catch {
            if ($attempt -ge 3) { throw }
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
        }
    }
}

# --- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not (Test-Path $loopHeal)) {
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: preflight -- loop-heal.ps1 missing"
    Write-Error "preflight: $loopHeal missing"
    exit 1
}
. $loopHeal   # defines ConvertTo-LoopFault / Invoke-LoopHeal / etc. (no StrictMode leak by design)

$medicDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$MedicId"
if (-not (Test-Path $medicDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $medicDir -Force | Out-Null }
$healLogPath = Join-Path $medicDir 'heal-log.json'
$healLog = @{}
if (Test-Path $healLogPath) {
    try { $j = Get-Content $healLogPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          foreach ($p in $j.PSObject.Properties) { $healLog[$p.Name] = [int]$p.Value } } catch { }
}

$healed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$would  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$escal  = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$failed = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$healCount = 0
$lockHeld = $false
$autoHeal  = @('battery-gate','hung-runner','dead-loop')
$escalSigs = @('night-wakefail','wake-fail','worker-error','unknown')

try {
    if ($DoApply -and (Test-Path $lockScript)) {
        try { & $lockScript -Claim scheduled-tasks -Reason "loop-medic auto-heal" | Out-Null; $lockHeld = $true }
        catch { $DoApply = $false; $escal.Add("could not claim scheduled-tasks lock -- ran DRY this fire") }
    }

    # --- 1) failing scheduled tasks -----------------------------------------
    $tasks = Get-JarvisTasks
    foreach ($t in $tasks) {
        if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded" }
        if ($t.TaskName -eq "Loopify-$MedicId") { continue }
        $info = $null
        try { $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $t.TaskName -ErrorAction Stop } catch { }
        if (-not $info) { continue }
        $isNight = $false
        foreach ($tr in $t.Triggers) { if ("$($tr.StartBoundary)" -match 'T0[0-5]:') { $isNight = $true } }
        $batFlag = $false
        try { $batFlag = [bool]$t.Settings.DisallowStartIfOnBatteries } catch { }
        $sig = ConvertTo-LoopFault -LastResult ([long]$info.LastTaskResult) -TaskState "$($t.State)" -IsNight $isNight -BatteryFlagSet $batFlag
        # skip non-actionable: benign, passive-heal (dep-down), and stale/self-clearing refusals
        if ($sig -eq 'none' -or $sig -eq 'dependency-down' -or $sig -eq 'stale-refusal') { continue }
        if ($autoHeal -contains $sig) {
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig $sig -Target $t.TaskName -Label $t.TaskName -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
        elseif ($escalSigs -contains $sig) {
            $escal.Add("$($t.TaskName) ($sig): escalate-class -- needs a human")
        }
    }

    # --- 2) dead / red loops in the loopctl registry ------------------------
    $regPath = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops\registry.json'
    if (Test-Path $regPath) {
        $reg = Get-Content $regPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
        foreach ($l in @($reg.loops)) {
            if ($null -eq $l) { continue }
            if (-not ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'id')) { continue }
            if ($l.id -eq $MedicId) { continue }
            $status = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'status') { "$($l.status)" } else { '' }
            if ($status -ne 'deployed') { continue }
            $hb = if ($l.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'last_heartbeat') { "$($l.last_heartbeat)" } else { '' }
            if ($hb -match 'RED|ERROR') { $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): heartbeat $hb -- failing its own work, needs a human"); continue }
            $stale = $false
            if ($hb) {
                $stamp = ($hb -split ' ')[0]; $dt = $null
                try { $dt = [datetime]::Parse($stamp) } catch { $dt = $null }
                if ($dt -and ((Get-Date).ToUniversalTime() - $dt.ToUniversalTime()).TotalHours -gt 26) { $stale = $true }
            } else { $stale = $true }
            if (-not $stale) { continue }
            $target = "Loopify-$($l.id)"
            if (-not (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $target -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                $escal.Add("loop $($l.id): stale hb '$hb' and no task $target to re-run -- needs a human"); continue
            }
            $res = Get-HealAction -Sig 'dead-loop' -Target $target -Label "loop $($l.id)" -Apply $DoApply -HealCount $healCount -MaxHeals $MaxHealsPerRun -Thrash $ThrashBudget -Log $healLog
            switch ($res.bucket) {
                'healed'   { $healed.Add($res.msg); $healCount++; $c=0; if ($healLog.ContainsKey($res.target)) { $c=[int]$healLog[$res.target] }; $healLog[$res.target]=$c+1 }
                'failed'   { $failed.Add($res.msg); $escal.Add($res.msg) }
                'would'    { $would.Add($res.msg) }
                'escalate' { $escal.Add($res.msg) }
            }
        }
    }

    # --- persist heal-log + write report ------------------------------------
    try { ($healLog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3) | Set-Content -Path $healLogPath -Encoding UTF8 } catch { }
    $mode = if ($DoApply) { 'APPLY' } else { 'DRY-RUN' }
    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
    $reportPath = Join-Path $medicDir ("report-{0}.md" -f (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))
    $lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines.Add("# loop-medic -- $stamp  [$mode]")
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Healed -- $($healed.Count)")
    if ($healed.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $healed | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Would heal (dry / over-cap) -- $($would.Count)")
    if ($would.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $would | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add("## Escalate to human -- $($escal.Count)")
    if ($escal.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none') } else { $escal | ForEach-Object { $lines.Add("- $_") } }
    ($lines -join "`r`n") | Set-Content -Path $reportPath -Encoding UTF8

    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }

    if ($failed.Count -gt 0 -or $escal.Count -gt 0) {
        Send-MedicNote ("[$mode] healed $($healed.Count), would $($would.Count), ESCALATE $($escal.Count). See $reportPath")
    }
    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State GREEN
    Write-Output ("loop-medic [$mode] OK: healed=$($healed.Count) would=$($would.Count) escalate=$($escal.Count) report=$reportPath")
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    # Persist the failure so a fail-closed RED is diagnosable next session (webhook may be unset).
    try {
        $errDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$MedicId"
        if (Test-Path $errDir) {
            $errStamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')
            "$errStamp  $($_.Exception.GetType().Name): $msg`r`n$($_.ScriptStackTrace)" |
                Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $errDir 'last-error.txt') -Encoding UTF8
        }
    } catch { }
    if ($lockHeld) { try { & $lockScript -Release scheduled-tasks | Out-Null } catch { } }
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $MedicId -State RED } catch { }
    Send-MedicNote "RED: $msg"
    Write-Error "loop-medic FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}
