Traced it end-to-end (systematic-debugging): the failing run was **06-30 07:40** (action completed 08:46:59, `0x80070001`=exit 1), roll-up `files=TIMEOUT` (a *required* task). Root cause = it ran the **pre-`aeb8120`** orchestrator code that treated a required task's normal TIMEOUT (Files is an 11-min async scan) as a roll-up failure. Fix commit `aeb8120` "TIMEOUT on required task is not a roll-up failure" landed **06-30 18:50** (~10h later). Current code (HEAD, clean working copy) treats TIMEOUT as soft — **verified** by isolating the exact `$failed` predicate against the failing summary -> `exit 0`. So NO code change needed; the stale `0x1` clears on the next scheduled 07:00 run (fixed code), before the medic's 09:30 pass. LESSON: check recent git changes (Phase-1 step 3) BEFORE instrumenting — the "out-of-band exit" was a code-version mismatch, not a live bug; nearly added instrumentation for a non-problem.
54	## gbrain daemon hourly-restart — root-caused + FIXED (commit `1ab0685` in ~/tools)
55	The "latent issue found in passing" above turned out to be real and live. Systematic-debugging trace: `~/tools/gbrain-src/src/daemon-server.ts`'s `/health` handler called `engine.getHealth()`/`engine.getStats()`, both proxied through the daemon's single-writer `serialize()` chain (`serializingEngine`). `/sync` deliberately runs `performSync` as ONE giant `serialize()` slot for its whole duration (avoids a proxy re-entrant-transaction deadlock) -- so `/health` queues behind an in-flight sync and can't resolve until it finishes; a plain `/ingest` can trip the same thing if one embed step runs long. `JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` (every 5min, anchor `:01`) runs `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy`, whose probe (5-10s timeout) times out when queued this way; its OWN `ingest.running` safety check ALSO queues behind the same chain and times out, so it falls to "assume wedged" and `Stop-Process -Force`s a daemon that was alive and correctly busy.
56	**Evidence:** `~/.gbrain-sync/log/2026-06-30.log` shows "connection actively refused" on essentially every hourly vault-sync AND a mem-ingest, each aligned exactly to the watchdog's 5-min-past-`:01` tick. The aborted sync then reports `[OK] null` post-restart (fresh process, no `last_result`/`last_error`) -- masking the loss as success.
57	**Fix:** while `ingest.running`, `/health` answers entirely from in-memory state (`ingestStatus()`, pid, uptime, embed config) -- never touches `engine.getHealth()`/`getStats()` -- so a busy daemon reports honestly instead of looking wedged, and the watchdog's own safety check now succeeds fast and correctly refuses the kill.
58	**Verified:** `bun build` clean; `bun test` 776 pass, 0 new failures (108 pre-existing are bare-`bun`-not-on-bash-PATH/unrelated CLI-e2e artifacts, none touch `daemon-server.ts`). Restarted the daemon live (sanctioned `restart-brain-daemon.ps1`, under `service:gbrain-daemon` lock, 6 peers active) -- new pid, brain state intact (chunks=5501 embedded=5493). **Live reproduction, twice:** raced a real (non-dry-run) `/sync` against a concurrent burst of `/health` polls. Run 1: caught the busy window returning `busy:true,ingest.running:true` in single-digit ms across ~20 polls (one early 5s stall, likely a post-restart first-call warm-up artifact). Run 2 (clean re-run): **20/20 fast, 0 slow, 0 errors.** Daemon pid unchanged before/after both runs -- no kill, no restart. LESSON: don't stop at a plausible code-level fix -- a live before/after repro under the actual failure conditions (concurrent real sync + burst health polls) is what turns "should be fixed" into "verified fixed," and running it twice caught that the one anomaly wasn't the steady-state behavior.
59

Systematic-debugging trace: `~/tools/gbrain-src/src/daemon-server.ts`'s `/health` handler called `engine.getHealth()`/`engine.getStats()`, both proxied through the daemon's single-writer `serialize()` chain (`serializingEngine`). `/sync` deliberately runs `performSync` as ONE giant `serialize()` slot for its whole duration (avoids a proxy re-entrant-transaction deadlock) -- so `/health` queues behind an in-flight sync and can't resolve until it finishes; a plain `/ingest` can trip the same thing if one embed step runs long. `JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` (every 5min, anchor `:01`) runs `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy`, whose probe (5-10s timeout) times out when queued this way; its OWN `ingest.running` safety check ALSO queues behind the same chain and times out, so it falls to "assume wedged" and `Stop-Process -Force`s a daemon that was alive and correctly busy.
**Evidence:** `~/.gbrain-sync/log/2026-06-30.log` shows "connection actively refused" on essentially every hourly vault-sync AND a mem-ingest, each aligned exactly to the watchdog's 5-min-past-`:01` tick. The aborted sync then reports `[OK] null` post-restart (fresh process, no `last_result`/`last_error`) -- masking the loss as success.
**Fix:** while `ingest.running`, `/health` answers entirely from in-memory state (`ingestStatus()`, pid, uptime, embed config) -- never touches `engine.getHealth()`/`getStats()` -- so a busy daemon reports honestly instead of looking wedged, and the watchdog's own safety check now succeeds fast and correctly refuses the kill.
**Verified:** `bun build` clean; `bun test` 776 pass, 0 new failures (108 pre-existing are bare-`bun`-not-on-bash-PATH/unrelated CLI-e2e artifacts, none touch `daemon-server.ts`). Restarted the daemon live (sanctioned `restart-brain-daemon.ps1`, under `service:gbrain-daemon` lock, 6 peers active) -- new pid, brain state intact (chunks=5501 embedded=5493). **Live reproduction, twice:** raced a real (non-dry-run) `/sync` against a concurrent burst of `/health` polls. Run 1: caught the busy window returning `busy:true,ingest.running:true` in single-digit ms across ~20 polls (one early 5s stall, likely a post-restart first-call warm-up artifact). Run 2 (clean re-run): **20/20 fast, 0 slow, 0 errors.** Daemon pid unchanged before/after both runs -- no kill, no restart. LESSON: don't stop at a plausible code-level fix -- a live before/after repro under the actual failure conditions (concurrent real sync + burst health polls) is what turns "should be fixed" into "verified fixed," and running it twice caught that the one anomaly wasn't the steady-state behavior.

# Loop Fleet — Operator's Guide

How to *run* the self-healing loop fleet day-to-day. This is the operator runbook;
the design doctrine ("when is something a loop, what are the brakes") lives in
`~/.claude/rules/loop-engineering.md`. Read that once; keep this one handy.

Last updated 2026-07-01 (loop-medic armed live).

---

## 1. The mental model — four verbs, then walk away

| Verb | Tool | You run it… |
|---|---|---|
| **compile** | `/loopify <goal>` | when you have a new recurring goal |
| **observe** | `/loops` | when you want to see fleet state (~weekly, or after a ping) |
| **operate** | `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1` | rarely — to inspect/kill/restart a specific loop |
| **heal** | the `loop-medic` task (automatic) + `loopctl -Action Heal/Restart` (manual) | almost never — the medic does it for you |

**The whole point:** once a loop is compiled and deployed, it runs on its own
schedule, heals its own routine faults, and **pings you only when it needs a
human**. Steady state = you do nothing. If you're checking on it constantly,
something's wrong with the loop, not with your attention.

---

## 2. What you actually do (the 90% case)

1. **Nothing.** Loops fire on their schedules. The medic (09:30 daily) heals the
   safe faults. fleet-health (10:00 daily) posts a board.
2. **When a Discord ping arrives** (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` → your Discord): read it.
   A ping means either (a) a loop hit an **escalate-class** fault the medic won't
   touch, or (b) a heal **failed**, or (c) a loop hit its **stop condition / budget**.
   The ping names the loop and points at a report file.
3. **Occasionally run `/loops`** to eyeball the board — green/stale/red, one line each.

That's it. Everything below is for the 10% when you want to look closer or change something.

---

## 3. Reading the reports

Every scheduled loop writes a dated report you can read anytime:

- **Medic:** `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/report-YYYY-MM-DD.md`
  - Header shows `[APPLY]` (live) or `[DRY-RUN]`.
  - Three sections: **Healed** (what it fixed), **Would heal** (dry-run / over-cap),
    **Escalate to human** (what it refuses to auto-fix — *these are yours*).
- **Fleet-health:** `~/.claude/loops/fleet-health/report-*.md` — the board snapshot.
- **Any loop:** `~/.claude/loops/<id>/` holds its `run.ps1`, `report-*.md`,
  `.heartbeat`, and (on failure) `last-error.txt`.

**Standing escalation right now:** the medic escalates `Jarvis-VaultIngest-All
(worker-error)` — that's a known stale `0x1` that self-clears; ignore unless it
persists past a 07:00 run.

---

## 4. loopctl cheat-sheet (the operate verb)

```powershell
$lc = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'

& $lc -Action List                       # every registered loop + status + last heartbeat
& $lc -Action Status  -Id loop-medic      # one loop in detail
& $lc -Action Restart -Id loop-medic      # re-run a stalled/stale loop NOW (don't wait for schedule)
& $lc -Action Heal    -Id fleet-health    # PREVIEW what healing would do (dry-run, safe)
& $lc -Action Heal    -Id fleet-health -Apply   # actually run the remediation
& $lc -Action Heal    -Target Loopify-maint-sweep   # heal a raw task name (no registry entry needed)
& $lc -Action Remove  -Id <id> -Purge     # unregister AND delete the scheduled task
```

- **`Heal` without `-Apply` is always a safe dry-run.** Use it to see the medic's
  logic on demand for any loop, not just on its schedule.
- **`Restart`** is your "I don't want to wait until 09:30" button.

---

## 5. Adding a new loop

Just describe the goal:

```
/loopify keep the paper-shadow Sharpe report fresh and ping me if it crosses 0.5
```

The compiler classifies the archetype, picks the runner (local task vs in-session
vs Workflow), wires the six brakes, registers it, and — if it's **safe**
(read-only / report / in-repo) — auto-deploys it live. If its steady-state action
is destructive or outward-facing (trades, pushes, `.env`/secret writes, deletes,
prod restarts, third-party messages), it compiles but **stops at a human gate** in
report-only/dry-run mode and surfaces a `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker for you.

**Hard rule it enforces for you:** anything touching local disk / installed tooling /
IB / pm2 / the engine runs LOCAL (a scheduled task), never a cloud routine — the
cloud sandbox can't see `C:\Users\mattm\` and fails silently.

---

## 6. The safety model (what heals vs what escalates)

The medic **only** auto-heals three fault classes — all safe and idempotent:

| Auto-healed | Meaning | Remediation |
|---|---|---|
| `battery-gate` | task refused with `0x800710E0` because it fired on battery | clear the battery flags |
| `hung-runner` | an instance is wedged past its time limit | kill the hung instance so the schedule frees |
| `dead-loop` | a deployed loop stopped heartbeating (>26h stale) | re-run its task |

Everything else is **escalate-class** — the medic notifies you and does **not** act:
`night-wakefail`, `wake-fail`, `worker-error`, `unknown`. Plus guards:

- **Thrash budget (3):** a target healed 3× already gets escalated, not re-healed —
  a fault that won't stay fixed is a human problem.
- **Max heals per run (6)** and a **240s runtime cap** per fire.
- **Claims the `scheduled-tasks` lock** before any mutation (peer-session safe).
- **Fail-closed:** any error → RED heartbeat + ping + non-zero exit.

---

## 7. Gotchas / things that will bite you

- **`-DoApply` reverts on redeploy.** The medic is armed live via a direct edit of
  its scheduled-task action (`...run.ps1 -DoApply`). `loopctl -Action Deploy` (or a
  `/loopify` recompile of loop-medic) rebuilds that action **without** `-DoApply`,
  silently dropping it back to dry-run. If you ever redeploy it, re-arm with:
  ```powershell
  $t=Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName Loopify-loop-medic
  if($t.Actions[0].Arguments -notmatch '-DoApply'){
    Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName Loopify-loop-medic `
      -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $t.Actions[0].Execute `
      -Argument ($t.Actions[0].Arguments.TrimEnd()+' -DoApply')) }
  ```
  (Claim the `scheduled-tasks` lock first if peer Claude sessions are live.)
- **Don't schedule loops for 00:00–05:59.** The machine sleeps; the task fails with
  `0xFFFD0000`. `/loopify` picks 09:00–11:00 by default — keep new ones there.
- **The webhook is the nervous system.** `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` (User scope) is set →
  your Discord. If pings ever stop, check it's still set; an unset webhook makes the
  fleet silently non-notifying (loops still run, you just stop hearing about them).
- **Escalate-class items are yours.** The medic will *never* fix a `worker-error` or
  `wake-fail` for you — those need a human decision. If one keeps appearing in the
  medic report, that's your signal to dig in (or `/loopify` a fix).

---

## 8. Quick recall

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| See the whole fleet | `/loops` |
| See one loop in detail | `loopctl -Action Status -Id <id>` |
| Run a loop now, not on schedule | `loopctl -Action Restart -Id <id>` |
| Preview what healing would do | `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <id>` (no `-Apply`) |
| Actually heal now | `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <id> -Apply` |
| Add a recurring goal | `/loopify <goal>` |
| Retire a loop | `loopctl -Action Remove -Id <id> -Purge` |
| Know why I got pinged | read `~/.claude/loops/<id>/report-*.md` |

Doctrine: `~/.claude/rules/loop-engineering.md` · Control plane: `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1`
· Registry: `~/.claude/loops/registry.json` · Self-healing detail:
`~/.claude/projects/C--Users-mattm/memory/project_loop_self_healing_2026_07_01.md`

something's wrong with the loop, not with your attention.

---

## 2. What you actually do (the 90% case)

1. **Nothing.** Loops fire on their schedules. The medic (09:30 daily) heals the
   safe faults. fleet-health (10:00 daily) posts a board.
2. **When a Discord ping arrives** (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` → your Discord): read it.
   A ping means either (a) a loop hit an **escalate-class** fault the medic won't
   touch, or (b) a heal **failed**, or (c) a loop hit its **stop condition / budget**.
   The ping names the loop and points at a report file.
3. **Occasionally run `/loops`** to eyeball the board — green/stale/red, one line each.

That's it. Everything below is for the 10% when you want to look closer or change something.

---

## 3. Reading the reports

Every scheduled loop writes a dated report you can read anytime:

- **Medic:** `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/report-YYYY-MM-DD.md`
  - Header shows `[APPLY]` (live) or `[DRY-RUN]`.
  - Three sections: **Healed** (what it fixed), **Would heal** (dry-run / over-cap),
    **Escalate to human** (what it refuses to auto-fix — *these are yours*).
- **Fleet-health:** `~/.claude/loops/fleet-health/report-*.md` — the board snapshot.
- **Any loop:** `~/.claude/loops/<id>/` holds its `run.ps1`, `report-*.md`,
  `.heartbeat`, and (on failure) `last-error.txt`.

**Standing escalation right now:** the medic escalates `Jarvis-VaultIngest-All
(worker-error)` — that's a known stale `0x1` that self-clears; ignore unless it
persists past a 07:00 run.

---

## 4. loopctl cheat-sheet (the operate verb)

```powershell
$lc = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'

& $lc -Action List                       # every registered loop + status + last heartbeat
& $lc -Action Status  -Id loop-medic      # one loop in detail
& $lc -Action Restart -Id loop-medic      # re-run a stalled/stale loop NOW (don't wait for schedule)
& $lc -Action Heal    -Id fleet-health    # PREVIEW what healing would do (dry-run, safe)
& $lc -Action Heal    -Id fleet-health -Apply   # actually run the remediation
& $lc -Action Heal    -Target Loopify-maint-sweep   # heal a raw task name (no registry entry needed)
& $lc -Action Remove  -Id <id> -Purge     # unregister AND delete the scheduled task
```

- **`Heal` without `-Apply` is always a safe dry-run.** Use it to see the medic's
  logic on demand for any loop, not just on its schedule.
- **`Restart`** is your "I don't want to wait until 09:30" button.

---

## 5. Adding a new loop

Just describe the goal:

```
/loopify keep the paper-shadow Sharpe report fresh and ping me if it crosses 0.5
```

The compiler classifies the archetype, picks the runner (local task vs in-session
vs Workflow), wires the six brakes, registers it, and — if it's **safe**
(read-only / report / in-repo) — auto-deploys it live. If its steady-state action
is destructive or outward-facing (trades, pushes, `.env`/secret writes, deletes,
prod restarts, third-party messages), it compiles but **stops at a human gate** in
report-only/dry-run mode and surfaces a `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker for you.

**Hard rule it enforces for you:** anything touching local disk / installed tooling /
IB / pm2 / the engine runs LOCAL (a scheduled task), never a cloud routine — the
cloud sandbox can't see `C:\Users\mattm\` and fails silently.

---

## 6. The safety model (what heals vs what escalates)

The medic **only** auto-heals three fault classes — all safe and idempotent:

| Auto-healed | Meaning | Remediation |
|---|---|---|
| `battery-gate` | task refused with `0x800710E0` because it fired on battery | clear the battery flags |
| `hung-runner` | an instance is wedged past its time limit | kill the hung instance so the schedule frees |
| `dead-loop` | a deployed loop stopped heartbeating (>26h stale) | re-run its task |

Everything else is **escalate-class** — the medic notifies you and does **not** act:
`night-wakefail`, `wake-fail`, `worker-error`, `unknown`. Plus guards:

- **Thrash budget (3):** a target healed 3× already gets escalated, not re-healed —
  a fault that won't stay fixed is a human problem.
- **Max heals per run (6)** and a **240s runtime cap** per fire.
- **Claims the `scheduled-tasks` lock** before any mutation (peer-session safe).
- **Fail-closed:** any error → RED heartbeat + ping + non-zero exit.

---

## 7. Gotchas / things that will bite you

- **`-DoApply` reverts on redeploy.** The medic is armed live via a direct edit of
  its scheduled-task action (`...run.ps1 -DoApply`). `loopctl -Action Deploy` (or a
  `/loopify` recompile of loop-medic) rebuilds that action **without** `-DoApply`,
  silently dropping it back to dry-run. If you ever redeploy it, re-arm with:
  ```powershell
  $t=Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName Loopify-loop-medic
  if($t.Actions[0].Arguments -notmatch '-DoApply'){
    Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName Loopify-loop-medic `
      -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $t.Actions[0].Execute `
      -Argument ($t.Actions[0].Arguments.TrimEnd()+' -DoApply')) }
  ```
  (Claim the `scheduled-tasks` lock first if peer Claude sessions are live.)
- **Don't schedule loops for 00:00–05:59.** The machine sleeps; the task fails with
  `0xFFFD0000`. `/loopify` picks 09:00–11:00 by default — keep new ones there.
- **The webhook is the nervous system.** `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` (User scope) is set →
  your Discord. If pings ever stop, check it's still set; an unset webhook makes the
  fleet silently non-notifying (loops still run, you just stop hearing about them).
- **Escalate-class items are yours.** The medic will *never* fix a `worker-error` or
  `wake-fail` for you — those need a human decision. If one keeps appearing in the
  medic report, that's your signal to dig in (or `/loopify` a fix).

---

## 8. Quick recall

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| See the whole fleet | `/loops` |
| See one loop in detail | `loopctl -Action Status -Id <id>` |
| Run a loop now, not on schedule | `loopctl -Action Restart -Id <id>` |
| Preview what healing would do | `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <id>` (no `-Apply`) |
| Actually heal now | `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <id> -Apply` |
| Add a recurring goal | `/loopify <goal>` |
| Retire a loop | `loopctl -Action Remove -Id <id> -Purge` |
| Know why I got pinged | read `~/.claude/loops/<id>/report-*.md` |

Doctrine: `~/.claude/rules/loop-engineering.md` · Control plane: `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1`
· Registry: `~/.claude/loops/registry.json` · Self-healing detail:
`~/.claude/projects/C--Users-mattm/memory/project_loop_self_healing_2026_07_01.md`

# Loop Fleet — Operator's Guide

How to *run* the self-healing loop fleet day-to-day. This is the operator runbook;
the design doctrine ("when is something a loop, what are the brakes") lives in
`~/.claude/rules/loop-engineering.md`. Read that once; keep this one handy.

Last updated 2026-07-01 (loop-medic armed live).

---

## 1. The mental model — four verbs, then walk away

| Verb | Tool | You run it… |
|---|---|---|
| **compile** | `/loopify <goal>` | when you have a new recurring goal |
| **observe** | `/loops` | when you want to see fleet state (~weekly, or after a ping) |
| **operate** | `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1` | rarely — to inspect/kill/restart a specific loop |
| **heal** | the `loop-medic` task (automatic) + `loopctl -Action Heal/Restart` (manual) | almost never — the medic does it for you |

**The whole point:** once a loop is compiled and deployed, it runs on its own
schedule, heals its own routine faults, and **pings you only when it needs a
human**. Steady state = you do nothing. If you're checking on it constantly,
something's wrong with the loop, not with your attention.

---

## 2. What you actually do (the 90% case)

1. **Nothing.** Loops fire on their schedules. The medic (09:30 daily) heals the
   safe faults. fleet-health (10:00 daily) posts a board.
2. **When a Discord ping arrives** (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` → your Discord): read it.
   A ping means either (a) a loop hit an **escalate-class** fault the medic won't
   touch, or (b) a heal **failed**, or (c) a loop hit its **stop condition / budget**.
   The ping names the loop and points at a report file.
3. **Occasionally run `/loops`** to eyeball the board — green/stale/red, one line each.

That's it. Everything below is for the 10% when you want to look closer or change something.

---

## 3. Reading the reports

Every scheduled loop writes a dated report you can read anytime:

- **Medic:** `~/.claude/loops/loop-medic/report-YYYY-MM-DD.md`
  - Header shows `[APPLY]` (live) or `[DRY-RUN]`.
  - Three sections: **Healed** (what it fixed), **Would heal** (dry-run / over-cap),
    **Escalate to human** (what it refuses to auto-fix — *these are yours*).
- **Fleet-health:** `~/.claude/loops/fleet-health/report-*.md` — the board snapshot.
- **Any loop:** `~/.claude/loops/<id>/` holds its `run.ps1`, `report-*.md`,
  `.heartbeat`, and (on failure) `last-error.txt`.

**Standing escalation right now:** the medic escalates `Jarvis-VaultIngest-All
(worker-error)` — that's a known stale `0x1` that self-clears; ignore unless it
persists past a 07:00 run.

---

## 4. loopctl cheat-sheet (the operate verb)

```powershell
$lc = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'

& $lc -Action List                       # every registered loop + status + last heartbeat
& $lc -Action Status  -Id loop-medic      # one loop in detail
& $lc -Action Restart -Id loop-medic      # re-run a stalled/stale loop NOW (don't wait for schedule)
& $lc -Action Heal    -Id fleet-health    # PREVIEW what healing would do (dry-run, safe)
& $lc -Action Heal    -Id fleet-health -Apply   # actually run the remediation
& $lc -Action Heal    -Target Loopify-maint-sweep   # heal a raw task name (no registry entry needed)
& $lc -Action Remove  -Id <id> -Purge     # unregister AND delete the scheduled task
```

- **`Heal` without `-Apply` is always a safe dry-run.** Use it to see the medic's
  logic on demand for any loop, not just on its schedule.
- **`Restart`** is your "I don't want to wait until 09:30" button.

---

## 5. Adding a new loop

Just describe the goal:

```
/loopify keep the paper-shadow Sharpe report fresh and ping me if it crosses 0.5
```

The compiler classifies the archetype, picks the runner (local task vs in-session
vs Workflow), wires the six brakes, registers it, and — if it's **safe**
(read-only / report / in-repo) — auto-deploys it live. If its steady-state action
is destructive or outward-facing (trades, pushes, `.env`/secret writes, deletes,
prod restarts, third-party messages), it compiles but **stops at a human gate** in
report-only/dry-run mode and surfaces a `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker for you.

**Hard rule it enforces for you:** anything touching local disk / installed tooling /
IB / pm2 / the engine runs LOCAL (a scheduled task), never a cloud routine — the
cloud sandbox can't see `C:\Users\mattm\` and fails silently.

---

## 6. The safety model (what heals vs what escalates)

The medic **only** auto-heals three fault classes — all safe and idempotent:

| Auto-healed | Meaning | Remediation |
|---|---|---|
| `battery-gate` | task refused with `0x800710E0` because it fired on battery | clear the battery flags |
| `hung-runner` | an instance is wedged past its time limit | kill the hung instance so the schedule frees |
| `dead-loop` | a deployed loop stopped heartbeating (>26h stale) | re-run its task |

Everything else is **escalate-class** — the medic notifies you and does **not** act:
`night-wakefail`, `wake-fail`, `worker-error`, `unknown`. Plus guards:

- **Thrash budget (3):** a target healed 3× already gets escalated, not re-healed —
  a fault that won't stay fixed is a human problem.
- **Max heals per run (6)** and a **240s runtime cap** per fire.
- **Claims the `scheduled-tasks` lock** before any mutation (peer-session safe).
- **Fail-closed:** any error → RED heartbeat + ping + non-zero exit.

---

## 7. Gotchas / things that will bite you

- **`-DoApply` reverts on redeploy.** The medic is armed live via a direct edit of
  its scheduled-task action (`...run.ps1 -DoApply`). `loopctl -Action Deploy` (or a
  `/loopify` recompile of loop-medic) rebuilds that action **without** `-DoApply`,
  silently dropping it back to dry-run. If you ever redeploy it, re-arm with:
  ```powershell
  $t=Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName Loopify-loop-medic
  if($t.Actions[0].Arguments -notmatch '-DoApply'){
    Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName Loopify-loop-medic `
      -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $t.Actions[0].Execute `
      -Argument ($t.Actions[0].Arguments.TrimEnd()+' -DoApply')) }
  ```
  (Claim the `scheduled-tasks` lock first if peer Claude sessions are live.)
- **Don't schedule loops for 00:00–05:59.** The machine sleeps; the task fails with
  `0xFFFD0000`. `/loopify` picks 09:00–11:00 by default — keep new ones there.
- **The webhook is the nervous system.** `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` (User scope) is set →
  your Discord. If pings ever stop, check it's still set; an unset webhook makes the
  fleet silently non-notifying (loops still run, you just stop hearing about them).
- **Escalate-class items are yours.** The medic will *never* fix a `worker-error` or
  `wake-fail` for you — those need a human decision. If one keeps appearing in the
  medic report, that's your signal to dig in (or `/loopify` a fix).

---

## 8. Quick recall

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| See the whole fleet | `/loops` |
| See one loop in detail | `loopctl -Action Status -Id <id>` |
| Run a loop now, not on schedule | `loopctl -Action Restart -Id <id>` |
| Preview what healing would do | `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <id>` (no `-Apply`) |
| Actually heal now | `loopctl -Action Heal -Id <id> -Apply` |
| Add a recurring goal | `/loopify <goal>` |
| Retire a loop | `loopctl -Action Remove -Id <id> -Purge` |
| Know why I got pinged | read `~/.claude/loops/<id>/report-*.md` |

Doctrine: `~/.claude/rules/loop-engineering.md` · Control plane: `~/scripts/loopctl.ps1`
· Registry: `~/.claude/loops/registry.json` · Self-healing detail:
`~/.claude/projects/C--Users-mattm/memory/project_loop_self_healing_2026_07_01.md`

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\mattm\.claude\skills\loopify # Loopify — the prompt-to-loop compiler > A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes. > Loopify's job: take a goal Amo states once, and leave behind a **running loop** that pursues it — safely, observably, and killably. **Autonomy: FULL AUTO-DEPLOY** (Amo's standing choice, 2026-06-30). Safe loops register, deploy, and start themselves. The brakes below plus the machine's existing hooks (credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the safety net. Only genuinely destructive / outward-facing steady-state actions stop at a human gate (see §Safety). --- ## The one-screen model ``` GOAL (English) ──▶ [1 CLASSIFY] ──▶ [2 LEDGER] ──▶ [3 RUNNER] ──▶ [4 BRAKES] ──▶ [5 FEEDBACK] ──▶ [6 REGISTER+DEPLOY] ──▶ running loop what shape? what's "done" where runs? how it stops how it learns loopctl + verify + report ``` Every stage is mandatory. Create a todo per stage and work them in order. Do not skip to deploy. --- ## Control plane All loops share one registry and one CLI: **`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1`** → `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`. ```powershell loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id -Goal "" -Archetype -Runner [-RunnerPath

] [-Schedule ] [-StopCondition ] [-BudgetCap ] [-Deploy] loopctl.ps1 -Action Deploy -Id # (re)create the scheduled task for a local-scheduled loop loopctl.ps1 -Action List # fleet board loopctl.ps1 -Action Status [-Id ] # full JSON loopctl.ps1 -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR # runners call this every iteration loopctl.ps1 -Action Remove -Id [-Purge] # -Purge also deletes the scheduled task ``` `-Deploy` on a `local-scheduled` loop creates a `Loopify-` Windows task (shim pwsh, battery-gate cleared, LIMITED, daytime). For every other runner, deploy is done by *you* (the agent) with the right tool, then recorded via `-Action Register`. --- ## Stage 1 — CLASSIFY (what shape is this loop?) Walk the decision tree top-down; first match wins. | If the goal… | Archetype | Canonical runner | |---|---|---| | watches **external state** and acts when it changes (CI, a queue, a price, a file landing) | **dynamic** | in-session `/loop` + `ScheduleWakeup`, OR local-scheduled poller | | drains a **known, finite backlog** (a task list, a set of files) to empty | **backlog-drain** | in-session `/ralph` | | drains a backlog that **regenerates itself** — you must re-discover work each pass | **discovery-drain** | in-session `/jarvis-loop` | | must **push a quality metric to a bar** (score ≥ X, tests green, latency < Y) by generate→judge→improve | **evaluator-optimizer** | in-session loop or Workflow | | fires on a **clock** to read/compute/report (digest, audit, briefing) | **scheduled-cadence** | local-scheduled (fs/tooling) OR cloud routine (Gmail/Cal/pure-cognition) | | is **one big parallelizable pass** with a verify step (review N files, migrate N sites) | **fan-out-verify** | `Workflow` | | **proposes** a change, a second pass **checks** it, then commit | **maker-checker** | in-session loop or Workflow | Write down: `archetype = ` and one sentence why. If two fit, prefer the *simplest runner* that satisfies the stop condition. **Runner picker (hard constraints):** - Touches `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local fs → **local-scheduled** or **in-session**. NEVER a cloud routine (the sandbox can't see the local disk — it fails silently). - Pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar / Drive / web → **cloud routine** (`/schedule` or CCR `create_trigger`). - Needs many agents at once → **Workflow** (fan-out-verify). - Needs to run while no Claude session is open → **local-scheduled** or **cloud** (never in-session). --- ## Stage 2 — LEDGER (what is "done", and where does state live?) A loop without a written ledger is an infinite loop. Define both: 1. **Done predicate** — the exact, checkable condition that ends the loop or a run: - drain: `prd.json` all `passes:true` AND discovery finds 0 new (discovery-drain) / backlog empty (backlog-drain) - evaluator-optimizer: `metric >= threshold` OR `no improvement for K rounds` - scheduled-cadence: never "done" — it's a heartbeat; the run is done when the report is emitted - dynamic: the watched condition resolved (merge landed, queue empty) 2. **State store** — where the loop remembers across iterations: - drain → a `prd.json` / queue file (reuse the ralph/jarvis-loop layout) - evaluator-optimizer → a metrics JSONL (`~/.claude/loops//metrics.jsonl`), one row per round - scheduled-cadence → last-run marker + the report file under `~/.claude/loops//` - dynamic → the external state itself is the store; record last-seen in `~/.claude/loops//state.json` No state store you can point at → you have not finished Stage 2. --- ## Stage 3 — RUNNER (scaffold the execution substrate) Create `~/.claude/loops//` (or, for a repo-scoped loop, `/scripts/loops/`). Put the runner there. - **local-scheduled** → copy `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (next to this SKILL), fill the WORK block. It already wires preflight, heartbeat, fail-closed, notify, and the loopctl heartbeat call. ASCII-only (PS 5.1 will run it). Use `127.0.0.1`, shim paths, battery-safe (loopctl handles the last one at deploy). - **in-session** (`/loop`, `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`) → no script; the runner is the skill. Register the loop so it's on the board, and use `ScheduleWakeup`/the skill's own loop for iteration. - **cloud** → the runner is the routine prompt. Write it as a *complete standalone instruction* (fresh session each fire sees no history). - **workflow** → the runner is the Workflow script (pipeline/parallel + verify stage). - **evaluator-optimizer** (in-session or workflow) → copy `templates/evaluator-optimizer.md` — generate → *independent* judge panel → improve, with stop-at-bar / converge / cap / budget brakes already wired. --- ## Stage 4 — BRAKES (mandatory — no loop deploys without all six) Every deployed loop MUST carry all six. This is what makes it an *engineered* loop, not a runaway. 1. **Preflight gate** — verify dependencies before doing work; abort (no-op, exit 0) if a dep is down. (Don't trade if the engine's down; don't digest if the data source is unreachable.) 2. **Heartbeat** — call `loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR` every iteration. A dead loop stops stamping → the fleet board shows it stale. 3. **Fail-closed** — on any error: stamp RED, notify, exit **non-zero**. Never swallow an error into a green "success". (Anti-pattern: "no error in the log so it worked.") 4. **Stop condition** — the Stage-2 done predicate, checked every iteration. Even cadence loops need a max-runtime guard. 5. **Budget / iteration cap** — a hard ceiling (max iterations, max tokens, max wall-clock). The backstop when the stop condition never trips. 6. **Notification** — on RED / stop / budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` Discord, or Telegram). No-op silently if unset — never throw, never block. For PowerShell runners, brakes 1-3 and 6 come pre-wired in `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. For in-session/cloud/workflow, wire the equivalents (a Workflow gets brakes from `budget.total`, a stop-count loop, and a verify stage). --- ## Stage 5 — FEEDBACK (how the loop learns / self-corrects) Match the archetype: - **discovery-drain** → the discovery phase IS the feedback (re-scan signals each pass). - **evaluator-optimizer** → a judge/verify step scores each attempt; the next attempt reads the score. Use an *independent* judge (separate agent/criteria), not self-grading. - **maker-checker / fan-out-verify** → a second pass adversarially checks the first before commit. Default the checker to skeptical. - **scheduled-cadence** → the report's own deltas vs last run (flag regressions). - **dynamic** → re-read external state each wake; act only on genuine change. A loop with no feedback is a cron job. That's fine *if* the goal is truly stateless cadence — but say so explicitly. --- ## Stage 6 — REGISTER + DEPLOY + OBSERVE 1. **Register** via `loopctl -Action Register …` with the archetype, runner, stop condition, and budget cap filled in. 2. **Deploy** (full auto): - `local-scheduled` → add `-Deploy` (loopctl creates + battery-clears the task). Then **verify it exists**: `schtasks /Query /TN Loopify- /V /FO LIST` shows `Ready` + a plausible Next Run. - `cloud` → create the trigger with CCR `create_trigger` (fresh-session mode for standalone) or `/schedule`, then `Register` (record `task_name`=trigger id). - `in-session` → start the loop now (invoke `/ralph` / `/jarvis-loop` / `/loop`), Register it so it's on the board. - `workflow` → run the `Workflow`; Register a one-shot entry for the audit trail. 3. **Smoke-run once** if safe (a scheduled runner: `Start-ScheduledTask` then read the heartbeat / report). Confirm GREEN. Per verification.md — never claim it runs from the absence of an error; hit the actual heartbeat/report. 4. **Report to Amo** in the format below. ### Report format (always end a /loopify run with this) ``` LOOP COMPILED: goal : archetype : runner: ledger : done = state = brakes : preflight | cap | stop | notify deployed : status= observe : loopctl -Action List (and: ) kill : gated? : ``` --- ## Safety — what full auto-deploy does NOT cover Full auto-deploy means: read-only, report, local-fs-analysis, and in-repo maker-checker loops **deploy and start themselves**. It does **not** authorize a loop whose *steady-state action* is destructive or outward-facing. If the compiled loop would, on its own, repeatedly: - place **live** trades, or flip a paper/live flag - `git push` to a shared branch (main/master/develop/release/*), or force-push - mutate secrets / `.env` / 1Password - delete or mass-move files (always archive, never delete) - restart a prod service (engine, Hermes gateway) unguarded - send messages to **third parties** (email/DM to people who aren't Amo) then **do not auto-deploy it live**. Instead: compile it fully, register it with `status=blocked`, deploy it in **report-only / dry-run** mode (or gate the mutating step behind a flag defaulting OFF), and surface the gate to Amo with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The loop's dangerous step still hits the machine's PreToolUse hooks as a second line of defense — but the design-time gate is yours to hold. Everything else deploys. When in doubt between "useful cadence report" and "outward action", ship the report and let Amo pull the trigger on the action. --- ## Anti-patterns | Anti-pattern | Why it's wrong | Do instead | |---|---|---| | Deploy without a stop condition | infinite loop / runaway spend | Stage 2 done predicate is mandatory | | Green on error (swallow exceptions) | silent failure looks healthy | fail-closed: RED + notify + non-zero exit | | Cloud routine that reads `C:\Users\mattm\` | sandbox can't see local fs — fails silently | local-scheduled for anything local | | Self-grading evaluator loop | grades its own homework, never converges | independent judge / adversarial checker | | Night-time scheduled task (00:00-05:59) | machine asleep → 0xFFFD0000 | schedule 09:00-11:00 (Stage 6) | | One loop per file / per finding | fleet noise | group related work into one loop | | `git add -A` inside a runner | sweeps the 1,450-file backlog | stage per-file, pathspec commit | | Skipping Register | loop invisible + unkillable from the board | always Register, even in-session/workflow | --- ## Dogfood examples (shapes, not prescriptions) - "keep an eye on the self-healing scheduled tasks and ping me if one stays red" → **scheduled-cadence**, local-scheduled, daily 10:00, report-only, notify on red. Safe → auto-deploy. - "get the MES VWAP strategy's paper Sharpe above 0.5" → **evaluator-optimizer**, in-session/Workflow, metric ledger, independent gate-v2 judge, cap 20 rounds. Backtest-only → auto-deploy; any live wiring is Amo-gated. - "review every open PR for the exec-path stack and verify findings" → **fan-out-verify**, Workflow, adversarial verify stage. Read-only → auto-deploy. - "watch for the Vertex quota grant and flip the engine to Vertex-primary" → **dynamic**, poller; but the flip mutates engine config → deploy the *watch* live, **gate the flip** (notify Amo when granted). --- ## Cross-references - Brakes library + heartbeat: `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1` - Loop archetypes in the wild: `/ralph` (backlog), `/jarvis-loop` (discovery), `/loop` (dynamic) - Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `~/.claude/rules/windows-pitfalls.md` - Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `~/.claude/rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling - Verify-before-claiming: `~/.claude/rules/verification.md` - Destructive-op gate: `~/.claude/rules/destructive-op-gates.md` ARGUMENTS: Compile three read-only monitoring loops for JARVIS: (1) engine-health watchdog — poll http://127.0.0.1:8010/health on a cadence, ping JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK when status!=ok OR llm_path_healthy=false OR tradingview_mcp_healthy=false OR ibkr disconnected; (2) LLM burn monitor — read engine/data/llm_costs.db daily, ping if trailing-24h spend crosses a threshold; (3) PR-staleness sweep — list open PRs in mattamundson/jarvis-trader, ping-only digest of PRs open past N days. <#
  Loopify scheduled-runner template  -- ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
  Copy to ~/.claude/loops/<id>/run.ps1 and fill the two marked blocks.
  All six brakes are pre-wired: preflight gate, heartbeat, fail-closed,
  stop/runtime cap, budget cap, notify. Do not remove them.

  Deploy:  loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id <id> -Goal "..." -Archetype scheduled-cadence `
             -Runner local-scheduled -RunnerPath <this file> -Schedule "DAILY@10:00" -Deploy
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'CHANGE-ME',              # must match the registered loop id
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 600            # brake 4/5: hard wall-clock cap for one fire
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'   # self-healing layer (Stage A/B)
$FailBudget = 3                                       # consecutive REDs before escalating
if (Test-Path $loopHeal) { . $loopHeal }             # best-effort; template still works if absent
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    # Brake 6: best-effort notify. No-op if webhook unset. NEVER throws.
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

function Test-Preflight {
    # Brake 1: verify dependencies. Return $true to proceed, $false to abort clean (no-op).
    # ---- FILL: check whatever this loop depends on (engine /health, a file, a port). ----
    # Example:
    #   try { (Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:8010/health' -TimeoutSec 5).status -eq 'ok' }
    #   catch { $false }
    return $true
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Preflight)) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN     # dep down is not an error; abort clean
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: dependency not ready -- skipping this fire (no-op)."
        exit 0
    }

    # ================= WORK BLOCK (fill this) =================
    # Do the loop's actual work. Write any report to
    #   Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$Id\report-<date>.md"
    # Enforce the runtime cap inside any inner loop:
    #   if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded" }
    $result = "TODO: implement work"
    Write-Output $result
    # =========================================================

    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
    if (Get-Command Register-LoopResult -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State GREEN | Out-Null    # Stage B: reset the fail counter
    }
    exit 0
}
catch {
    # Brake 3: fail-closed. Stamp RED, notify, exit non-zero. Never green-on-error.
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State RED } catch { }
    # Stage B: escalation budget -- transient REDs retry on cadence; after $FailBudget
    # consecutive fails, escalate louder (a chronic fault a human must look at).
    $note = "RED: $msg"
    if (Get-Command Register-LoopResult -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $d = Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State RED -Fault 'runner-exception' -Budget $FailBudget
        if ($d.escalate) { $note = "ESCALATE ($($d.consecutive_fails)/$FailBudget consecutive REDs): $msg" }
    }
    Send-LoopNote $note
    Write-Error "LOOP FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

input.content:
<#
  engine-health-watch -- dynamic watchdog for the JARVIS engine.
  Polls http://127.0.0.1:8010/health each fire; pings JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK only on a
  STATE TRANSITION (healthy<->unhealthy), never every poll -- so a sustained outage
  is one ping, not one-per-hour. ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.

  Unhealthy = any of: status != ok | llm_path_healthy false | tradingview_mcp_healthy
  false | ibkr_connected false. (Single-leg LLM, primary_healthy=false, is NOT
  unhealthy -- llm_path_healthy stays true, so the current gpt-4o-mini leg won't alarm.)

  Six brakes: preflight (n/a -- the engine IS the subject; unreachable = the alert),
  heartbeat, fail-closed, stop/runtime cap, budget (single HTTP call), notify.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'engine-health-watch',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 60,
    [string] $HealthUrl = 'http://127.0.0.1:8010/health'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$dir     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$Id"
$statePath = Join-Path $dir 'state.json'

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null }

    # --- poll /health; unreachable IS the alert condition, not a preflight abort ---
    $problems = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $h = $null
    try { $h = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $HealthUrl -TimeoutSec 8 }

<#

  Reads engine/data/llm_costs.db, sums cost_usd over the trailing 24h, and pings
  JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK if it crosses -ThresholdUsd. Guards against a silent return to
  the expensive-Claude treadmill (~$30/day) or a runaway. ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.

  Six brakes: preflight (DB + venv python exist), heartbeat, fail-closed, runtime cap,
  budget (one query), notify. Reports every run to report-<date>.md; pings only over threshold.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'llm-burn-monitor',
    [double] $ThresholdUsd = 15.0,
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 120
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$repo    = 'C:\Users\mattm\ThinkorSwim\jarvis-trader'
$py      = Join-Path $repo 'engine\.venv\Scripts\python.exe'
$db      = Join-Path $repo 'engine\data\llm_costs.db'
$dir     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$Id"

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null }

    # --- preflight: deps present; if not, abort clean (GREEN no-op), don't false-RED ---
    if (-not (Test-Path $py) -or -not (Test-Path $db)) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: venv python or cost DB missing -- skipping (no-op)."
        exit 0
    }

    # --- query: trailing-24h cost + per-provider breakdown; cutoff computed in UTC ISO
    #     to match the stored '+00:00' timestamps exactly (robust lexical compare). ---
    $pyCode = @'
import sqlite3, datetime, json, sys
db = sys.argv[1]
cutoff = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(hours=24)).isoformat()
c = sqlite3.connect(db)
total, n = c.execute("select coalesce(sum(cost_usd),0), count(*) from llm_calls where timestamp >= ?", (cutoff,)).fetchone()
by = c.execute("select coalesce(model,'?'), round(coalesce(sum(cost_usd),0),4), count(*) from llm_calls where timestamp >= ? group by model order by 2 desc", (cutoff,)).fetchall()
print(json.dumps({"total": round(total,4), "calls": n, "by_model": by}))
'@
    $tmp = Join-Path $dir '_burnquery.py'
    Set-Content -Path $tmp -Value $pyCode -Encoding ASCII
    $raw = & $py $tmp $db 2>&1

    $data = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json

    $total = [double]$data.total
    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
    $over  = $total -gt $ThresholdUsd

    $lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines.Add("# llm-burn-monitor -- $stamp")
    $lines.Add("trailing-24h spend: `$$total  (threshold `$$ThresholdUsd)  calls=$($data.calls)")
    $lines.Add("status: $(if($over){'OVER THRESHOLD'}else{'ok'})")
    $lines.Add('')
    $lines.Add('## by model')
    foreach ($m in $data.by_model) { $lines.Add("- $($m[0]): `$$($m[1])  ($($m[2]) calls)") }
    ($lines -join "`r`n") | Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $dir ("report-{0}.md" -f (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))) -Encoding ASCII

    if ($over) {
        $top = if ($data.by_model.Count -gt 0) { " top: $($data.by_model[0][0]) `$$($data.by_model[0][1])" } else { '' }
        Send-LoopNote "BURN: trailing-24h LLM spend `$$total > threshold `$$ThresholdUsd.$top"
    }

    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
    Write-Output "llm-burn-monitor OK: 24h=`$$total threshold=`$$ThresholdUsd over=$over"
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State RED } catch { }
    Send-LoopNote "RED: $msg"
    Write-Error "llm-burn-monitor FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

input.content:
<#
  pr-staleness-sweep -- daily scheduled-cadence digest of stale open PRs in
  mattamundson/jarvis-trader. Ping-only; mutates nothing. Pings JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
  with a digest of PRs open longer than -StaleDays. ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.

  Uses the gh REST API (not GraphQL) to avoid the shared 5000/hr GraphQL cap.
  A gh failure (not installed / not auth'd / rate-limited) is treated as a transient
  dep-down -> abort clean (GREEN no-op), never a false RED on a low-priority digest.

  Six brakes: preflight (gh reachable), heartbeat, fail-closed, runtime cap,
  budget (one paginated REST call), notify.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'pr-staleness-sweep',
    [int]    $StaleDays = 7,
    [string] $Repo = 'mattamundson/jarvis-trader',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 120
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$dir     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".claude\loops\$Id"

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null }

    $gh = (Get-Command gh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    if (-not $gh) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: gh not installed -- skipping (no-op)."
        exit 0
    }

    # --- fetch open PRs via REST (soft-fail: gh error/rate-limit = clean no-op) ---
    $raw = & gh api "repos/$Repo/pulls?state=open&per_page=100" 2>&1
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: gh api unavailable (rate limit / auth) -- skipping (no-op): $($raw | Select-Object -First 1)"
        exit 0
    }
    $prs = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json

    $now = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime()
    $stale = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
    foreach ($p in @($prs)) {
        if ($null -eq $p) { continue }
        $created = $null
        try { $created = ([datetime]$p.created_at).ToUniversalTime() } catch { continue }
        $age = [int][math]::Floor(($now - $created).TotalDays)
        if ($age -ge $StaleDays) {
            $stale.Add([pscustomobject]@{ num = $p.number; age = $age; draft = [bool]$p.draft; title = "$($p.title)" })
        }
    }
    $sorted = @($stale | Sort-Object -Property age -Descending)

    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')
    $lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines.Add("# pr-staleness-sweep -- $stamp")
    $lines.Add("open PRs: $(@($prs).Count)  stale (>= $StaleDays d): $($sorted.Count)")
    $lines.Add('')
    if ($sorted.Count -eq 0) { $lines.Add('- none stale') }
    else { foreach ($s in $sorted) { $lines.Add("- #$($s.num) [$($s.age)d]$(if($s.draft){' (draft)'}else{''}) $($s.title)") } }
    ($lines -join "`r`n") | Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $dir ("report-{0}.md" -f (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))) -Encoding ASCII

    if ($sorted.Count -gt 0) {
        $top = @($sorted | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { "#$($_.num)($($_.age)d)" }) -join ' '
        Send-LoopNote "$($sorted.Count) PR(s) open >= $StaleDays d: $top$(if($sorted.Count -gt 5){' ...'}else{''})"
    }

    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
    Write-Output "pr-staleness-sweep OK: open=$(@($prs).Count) stale=$($sorted.Count)"
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State RED } catch { }
    Send-LoopNote "RED: $msg"
    Write-Error "pr-staleness-sweep FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

# Three JARVIS monitoring loops — compiled + deployed 2026-07-01

Amo asked (after the loop-medic live-arm + the durable `-DoApply` persistence fix) to
`/loopify` three read-only monitors. All are the **safe auto-deploy class** (read-only,
report, ping-only), all local-scheduled, all verified GREEN end-to-end (runner smoke-test +
scheduler-fired `LastTaskResult 0x0` + heartbeat stamped + report/state written).

## The three loops
| id | archetype | schedule | pings when | runner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine-health-watch` | dynamic (poller) | **HOURLY** | health-state **transition** to unhealthy, and on recovery | `~/.claude/loops/engine-health-watch/run.ps1` |
| `llm-burn-monitor` | scheduled-cadence | DAILY@10:45 | trailing-24h `cost_usd` > threshold | `~/.claude/loops/llm-burn-monitor/run.ps1` |
| `pr-staleness-sweep` | scheduled-cadence | DAILY@10:50 | any open PR older than N days | `~/.claude/loops/pr-staleness-sweep/run.ps1` |

## Design decisions / tuning knobs (the non-obvious bits)
- **engine-health-watch is TRANSITION-based, not every-poll.** It reads `state.json`
  (`{unhealthy,reasons,checked}`) and pings ONLY when the healthy<->unhealthy state flips —
  so a sustained outage is one "DOWN" ping + one "RECOVERED" ping, never one-per-hour.
  Unhealthy = `status!=ok` OR `llm_path_healthy=false` OR `tradingview_mcp_healthy=false`
  OR `ibkr_connected=false`. **Single-leg LLM does NOT alarm** (criterion is
  `llm_path_healthy`, which stays true on the gpt-4o-mini leg) — verified: smoke-test on the
  current single-leg engine returned healthy/no-ping. CAVEAT flagged to Amo: IBKR paper (4002)
  can be legitimately down outside trading hours, so it MAY produce a session-boundary
  ping-pair; if noisy, drop ibkr from the condition or add a market-hours gate. HOURLY cadence
  is tunable (loopctl's schedule parser only does HOURLY/DAILY/WEEKLY — for sub-hourly, patch
  the task's RepetitionInterval).
- **llm-burn-monitor threshold default = $15/day** (`-ThresholdUsd`). Current baseline at
  build time = **$4.36 trailing-24h** (2935 calls, all gpt-4o-mini — the cheap single leg), so
  $15 catches a ~3.5x spike (e.g. a return to expensive-Claude ~$30/day, or a runaway). Queries
  `engine/data/llm_costs.db` table `llm_calls` (cols: timestamp TEXT UTC-ISO, model, cost_usd
  REAL, provider, success). Cutoff computed in **Python UTC ISO** to lexically match the stored
  `+00:00` timestamps exactly (a naive SQLite `datetime('now','-1 day')` compare is off by the
  `T`-vs-space at the day boundary). Runs via the engine venv python (`engine/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`).
- **pr-staleness-sweep uses `gh api` REST, NOT GraphQL** — deliberately, to dodge the shared
  5000/hr GraphQL cap (which was exhausted during this very session). `StaleDays` default 7,
  `Repo` default `mattamundson/jarvis-trader`. A gh failure (not installed / not auth'd /
  rate-limited) is a **clean GREEN no-op**, never a false RED on a low-priority digest. Baseline
  at build: 14 open PRs, 0 stale (>=7d) — the repo merges fast, so 7d rarely trips (that's the point).

## Brakes (all six, per loop)
Preflight (deps present / dep-down = clean no-op) · heartbeat via `loopctl -Heartbeat` ·
fail-closed (RED + notify + exit 1 on runner exception) · stop/runtime cap · budget (1 call/query
per fire) · notify via `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` (confirmed set, User scope → Discord). Runners are
ASCII-only, parse-clean under pwsh 7 (the task runtime via the WindowsApps shim), default `$Id`
hardcoded to match the registered id (tasks invoke with no `-Id` arg).

## Operate
`loopctl -Action List` (board) · `-Action Status -Id <id>` · `-Action Restart -Id <id>` (run now)
· reports at `~/.claude/loops/<id>/report-*.md` · kill: `schtasks /Delete /F /TN Loopify-<id>`.
Operator guide: `~/.claude/loops/OPERATING_GUIDE.md`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine-health-watch` | dynamic (poller) | **HOURLY** | health-state **transition** to unhealthy, and on recovery | `~/.claude/loops/engine-health-watch/run.ps1` |
| `llm-burn-monitor` | scheduled-cadence | DAILY@10:45 | trailing-24h `cost_usd` > threshold | `~/.claude/loops/llm-burn-monitor/run.ps1` |
| `pr-staleness-sweep` | scheduled-cadence | DAILY@10:50 | any open PR older than N days | `~/.claude/loops/pr-staleness-sweep/run.ps1` |

## Design decisions / tuning knobs (the non-obvious bits)
- **engine-health-watch is TRANSITION-based, not every-poll.** It reads `state.json`
  (`{unhealthy,reasons,checked}`) and pings ONLY when the healthy<->unhealthy state flips —
  so a sustained outage is one "DOWN" ping + one "RECOVERED" ping, never one-per-hour.
  Unhealthy = `status!=ok` OR `llm_path_healthy=false` OR `tradingview_mcp_healthy=false`
  OR `ibkr_connected=false`. **Single-leg LLM does NOT alarm** (criterion is
  `llm_path_healthy`, which stays true on the gpt-4o-mini leg) — verified: smoke-test on the
  current single-leg engine returned healthy/no-ping. CAVEAT flagged to Amo: IBKR paper (4002)
  can be legitimately down outside trading hours, so it MAY produce a session-boundary
  ping-pair; if noisy, drop ibkr from the condition or add a market-hours gate. HOURLY cadence
  is tunable (loopctl's schedule parser only does HOURLY/DAILY/WEEKLY — for sub-hourly, patch
  the task's RepetitionInterval).
- **llm-burn-monitor threshold default = $15/day** (`-ThresholdUsd`). Current baseline at
  build time = **$4.36 trailing-24h** (2935 calls, all gpt-4o-mini — the cheap single leg), so
  $15 catches a ~3.5x spike (e.g. a return to expensive-Claude ~$30/day, or a runaway). Queries
  `engine/data/llm_costs.db` table `llm_calls` (cols: timestamp TEXT UTC-ISO, model, cost_usd
  REAL, provider, success). Cutoff computed in **Python UTC ISO** to lexically match the stored
  `+00:00` timestamps exactly (a naive SQLite `datetime('now','-1 day')` compare is off by the
  `T`-vs-space at the day boundary). Runs via the engine venv python (`engine/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`).
- **pr-staleness-sweep uses `gh api` REST, NOT GraphQL** — deliberately, to dodge the shared
  5000/hr GraphQL cap (which was exhausted during this very session). `StaleDays` default 7,
  `Repo` default `mattamundson/jarvis-trader`. A gh failure (not installed / not auth'd /
  rate-limited) is a **clean GREEN no-op**, never a false RED on a low-priority digest. Baseline
  at build: 14 open PRs, 0 stale (>=7d) — the repo merges fast, so 7d rarely trips (that's the point).

## Brakes (all six, per loop)
Preflight (deps present / dep-down = clean no-op) · heartbeat via `loopctl -Heartbeat` ·
fail-closed (RED + notify + exit 1 on runner exception) · stop/runtime cap · budget (1 call/query
per fire) · notify via `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` (confirmed set, User scope → Discord). Runners are
ASCII-only, parse-clean under pwsh 7 (the task runtime via the WindowsApps shim), default `$Id`
hardcoded to match the registered id (tasks invoke with no `-Id` arg).

## Operate
`loopctl -Action List` (board) · `-Action Status -Id <id>` · `-Action Restart -Id <id>` (run now)
· reports at `~/.claude/loops/<id>/report-*.md` · kill: `schtasks /Delete /F /TN Loopify-<id>`.

<#
  restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -- the SANCTIONED restart path for the single-writer gbrain brain daemon.

  Mirrors restart_engine.ps1: stop the current opener cleanly, wait for the lock/port to release, then
  relaunch DETACHED (session-independent, survives the shell that ran this). Use this instead of an
  ad-hoc Stop-Process -- the daemon owns the one PGlite connection, so an uncoordinated kill mid-ingest
  is the exact failure class this daemon exists to delete.

  Safe to kill when ingest is idle: PGlite transactions are atomic (a dropped connection rolls back,
  the heap stays intact). This script refuses to stop while an ingest is RUNNING unless -Force is given.

  -Force : stop even if an ingest is in progress (rolls back the in-flight embed batch; brain stays sound).

  -IfUnhealthy : no-op if the daemon already answers /health OK; otherwise stop + relaunch. This is the
  WATCHDOG entry point — a bare port check (start-brain-daemon's idempotency) can't tell a healthy
  daemon from a wedged one (port bound, /health dead), so the watchdog would never heal a wedge. With
  -IfUnhealthy the watchdog heals BOTH down and wedged daemons.

  Run it yourself (human-in-the-loop) when an agent's destructive-op guard blocks a raw kill:
    ! pwsh -NoProfile -File C:\Users\mattm\tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1
#>
param([int]$Port = 8077, [switch]$Force, [switch]$IfUnhealthy)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$launcher = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'

function Test-Port { Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $Port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue }

# Watchdog gate: if the daemon is already serving /health AND can spawn children, do nothing. A
# generous timeout avoids killing a healthy-but-busy daemon (/health serializes individually and stays
# responsive even mid-ingest). ?deep=1 adds a child-spawn probe: a spawn-dead daemon (its cwd was
# deleted -> Windows CreateProcess fails) answers /health ok but can't run /sync's git ops -- treat
# spawn.ok=false as unhealthy so the watchdog heals it too. ($null spawn = older daemon w/o the probe;
# fall back to ok alone for backward compat during the upgrade window.) Any failure -> stop + relaunch.
if ($IfUnhealthy) {
  $healthy = $false
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10
    $spawnOk = ($null -eq $h.spawn) -or [bool]$h.spawn.ok
    $healthy = ([bool]$h.ok) -and $spawnOk
    if (([bool]$h.ok) -and -not $spawnOk) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health ok but spawn DEAD ($($h.spawn.error)) - healing spawn-dead daemon."
    }
  } catch { $healthy = $false }
  if ($healthy) { Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health OK (pid=$($h.pid), spawn ok) - nothing to do."; exit 0 }
  Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] -IfUnhealthy: daemon down, wedged, or spawn-dead - healing."
}

# Refuse to yank the lock out from under a live embed unless forced.
if (Test-Port) {
  try {
    $st = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 5
    if ($st.ingest.running -and -not $Force) {
      Write-Error "daemon is mid-ingest (phase=$($st.ingest.phase)). Re-run with -Force to stop anyway, or wait for it to finish."
      exit 3
    }
  } catch { Write-Warning "port $Port up but /health unreachable; proceeding to stop." }
}

# Find and stop the daemon's bun process by command line (robust against pid drift).
$procs = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'" |
           Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*' }
foreach ($p in $procs) {
  Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] stopping bun pid $($p.ProcessId)"
  Stop-Process -Id $p.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

# Wait for the port (and thus the PGlite lock) to actually release.
$n = 0
while ((Test-Port) -and $n -lt 20) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500; $n++ }
if (Test-Port) { Write-Error "port $Port still held after stop; aborting relaunch."; exit 4 }
Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] port $Port released."

# Relaunch detached (the launcher's own port-check makes this a no-op if something already rebound).
& pwsh -NoProfile -File $launcher -Detached

# Verify the new daemon answers. A cold PGlite open of the ~135MB brain + Voyage key resolution can
# take well over 30s, so wait up to 90s before declaring failure (avoids a false "did not come up"
# that alarms the operator / could trigger spurious watchdog churn).
$n = 0
while ($n -lt 90) {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; $n++
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 3
    if ($h.ok) { Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] UP: pid=$($h.pid) model=$($h.embed.model)/$($h.embed.dim) chunks=$($h.stats.chunk_count) embedded=$($h.stats.embedded_count)"; exit 0 }
  } catch { }
}
Write-Error "daemon did not come up on $Port within 90s; check ~/.gbrain-trading/logs/daemon.err.log"

<#
  restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -- the SANCTIONED restart path for the single-writer gbrain brain daemon.

  Mirrors restart_engine.ps1: stop the current opener cleanly, wait for the lock/port to release, then
  relaunch DETACHED (session-independent, survives the shell that ran this). Use this instead of an
  ad-hoc Stop-Process -- the daemon owns the one PGlite connection, so an uncoordinated kill mid-ingest
  is the exact failure class this daemon exists to delete.

  Safe to kill when ingest is idle: PGlite transactions are atomic (a dropped connection rolls back,
  the heap stays intact). This script refuses to stop while an ingest is RUNNING unless -Force is given.

  -Force : stop even if an ingest is in progress (rolls back the in-flight embed batch; brain stays sound).

  -IfUnhealthy : no-op if the daemon already answers /health OK; otherwise stop + relaunch. This is the
  WATCHDOG entry point — a bare port check (start-brain-daemon's idempotency) can't tell a healthy
  daemon from a wedged one (port bound, /health dead), so the watchdog would never heal a wedge. With
  -IfUnhealthy the watchdog heals BOTH down and wedged daemons.

  Run it yourself (human-in-the-loop) when an agent's destructive-op guard blocks a raw kill:
    ! pwsh -NoProfile -File C:\Users\mattm\tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1
#>
param([int]$Port = 8077, [switch]$Force, [switch]$IfUnhealthy, [int]$StallMinutes = 15, [switch]$DetectOnly)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$launcher = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'

function Test-Port { Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $Port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue }

function Test-IngestWedged {
  # Wedge detector: the daemon claims ingest.running but is making NO progress -- PGlite unwritten
  # for > $StallMinutes AND the process CPU idle over a short sample. BOTH signals are required so a
  # slow-but-working ingest (still writing PGlite, or burning CPU) is never false-killed. Every
  # uncertain path returns $false (fail SAFE -- never kill a daemon we can't prove is wedged).
  # This closes the -IfUnhealthy blind spot: a wedged ingest answers /health ok:true forever.
  param($Health)
  if (-not $Health -or -not $Health.ingest -or -not $Health.ingest.running) { return $false }
  $pg = "$($Health.data_dir)"
  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($pg) -or -not (Test-Path $pg)) {
    $pg = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\brain.pglite'
  }
  if (-not (Test-Path $pg)) { return $false }
  $newest = Get-ChildItem $pg -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  if (-not $newest) { return $false }
  $stallMin = ((Get-Date) - $newest.LastWriteTime).TotalMinutes
  if ($stallMin -le $StallMinutes) { return $false }   # wrote PGlite recently => progressing => healthy
  $proc = Get-Process -Id ([int]$Health.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $proc) { return $false }
  $c1 = [double]$proc.CPU
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
  $proc2 = Get-Process -Id ([int]$Health.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $proc2) { return $false }
  $cpuDelta = [double]$proc2.CPU - $c1
  Write-Host ("[restart-brain-daemon] ingest.running but PGlite stale {0:N1} min (> {1}) and CPU delta {2:N3}s/5s" -f $stallMin, $StallMinutes, $cpuDelta)
  return ($cpuDelta -lt 0.3)   # CPU idle => hung, not working => wedged
}

# Watchdog gate: if the daemon is already serving /health AND can spawn children, do nothing. A
# generous timeout avoids killing a healthy-but-busy daemon (/health serializes individually and stays
# responsive even mid-ingest). ?deep=1 adds a child-spawn probe: a spawn-dead daemon (its cwd was
# deleted -> Windows CreateProcess fails) answers /health ok but can't run /sync's git ops -- treat
# spawn.ok=false as unhealthy so the watchdog heals it too. ($null spawn = older daemon w/o the probe;
# fall back to ok alone for backward compat during the upgrade window.) Any failure -> stop + relaunch.
# Read-only diagnostic: report whether the daemon is wedged, act on nothing. For testing the
# detector and for operator use (a zero-side-effect wedge check).
if ($DetectOnly) {
  try { $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10 }
  catch { Write-Host "DETECT: /health unreachable (daemon down or port unbound)."; exit 0 }
  $wedged = Test-IngestWedged -Health $h
  Write-Host ("DETECT: wedged={0}  ok={1}  ingest.running={2}  pid={3}" -f $wedged, $h.ok, $h.ingest.running, $h.pid)
  exit 0
}

if ($IfUnhealthy) {
  $healthy = $false
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10
    $spawnOk = ($null -eq $h.spawn) -or [bool]$h.spawn.ok
    $healthy = ([bool]$h.ok) -and $spawnOk
    if (([bool]$h.ok) -and -not $spawnOk) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health ok but spawn DEAD ($($h.spawn.error)) - healing spawn-dead daemon."
    }

    # -IfUnhealthy used to say "nothing to do" and never heal this class. Now: detect it and force-heal.
    if (Test-IngestWedged -Health $h) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] WEDGED ingest detected (no PGlite progress + CPU idle) - forcing heal."

`/health ok:true pid=28140`, `busy:true`, `ingest.running:true` phase `sync:second-brain` --

  check CPU + pglite mtime.

`JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` entry point) checks `/health.ok` + `spawn.ok` only -- NOT

answer" are blind to a wedged-but-responsive ingest. **Proposed fix (not yet built):** add an

no pglite write, treat as unhealthy and restart -Force.

content.text:
**#3 done — and it turned out there was a live wedge to prove it against.** Committed `d1d80cd` in `~/tools`.

What happened and what I built:
- **Confirmed a live wedge**: pid 34952 claimed `ingest.running` for 29 min but CPU was idle (0.016s/6s) and pglite hadn't been written in 65 min — recall was broken. A second sync had fired after the peer's restart and hung, exactly as they predicted.
- **Fixed both gaps** the peer documented as "not yet built":
  1. **Detection** — `Test-IngestWedged` wired into `-IfUnhealthy`: wedged = `ingest.running` AND pglite stale >15 min AND CPU idle over a 5s sample. Both signals required, every uncertain path fails safe, so a slow-but-working ingest is never false-killed.
  2. **Kill path** — PID fallback (from `/health.pid`, then `daemon-lock.json`) for when the `CommandLine` filter reads empty under the non-elevated watchdog — the bug that aborted the peer's heal with "port still held."
  - Plus a read-only `-DetectOnly` mode for testing/operator use.
- **Verified**: parse-clean/ASCII-pure; the `.vbs` confirms my code is on the watchdog path (`-IfUnhealthy`); true-negative confirmed (`DetectOnly` → `wedged=False` on the healthy daemon, no false-kill); true-positive validated against the real wedge's measured values. The wedge got healed to fresh pid 31412 and **recall is restored** (chunks 5501 intact). One honesty note: I can't 100%-attribute the live heal to my new code vs a peer restart around the same 06:31 watchdog fire — no watchdog stdout log exists — but the fix is correct and on-path.

**Recommended next step (the actual root cause):** my fix is a *backstop* — it detects and restarts a wedge, but doesn't prevent it. The wedge itself is a silent no-timeout hang, almost certainly a **Voyage embed HTTP call with no timeout** in `daemon-server.ts`. The durable cure is a per-request timeout on that embed call so the ingest fails-fast (and the sync retries) instead of hanging for hours. That's a `daemon-server.ts` change + `bun build` + a daemon restart to deploy (the restart is the one gated/peer-territory step).

Want me to build the embed-timeout root-cause fix? I'd write + build it, then gate the daemon restart on your OK (and coordinate via the `service:gbrain-daemon` lock).

name: feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart
description: "gbrain can wedge mid-ingest (busy:true forever, ok:true) — invisible to the watchdog; diagnose by CPU/pglite-write stall, fix with restart -Force"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

2026-07-01: recall.ps1 / `/vault` timed out. First wrong call: "gbrain daemon DOWN." It was
`/health ok:true pid=28140`, `busy:true`, `ingest.running:true` phase `sync:second-brain` --
looked like a normal busy ingest. But it was **wedged**, not working:

**How to tell wedged from busy-working (the discriminators that matter):**
- process CPU delta over 5s = **0.00** (idle, not embedding)
- pglite data dir (`~/.gbrain-trading/brain.pglite`) **last write ~2h old** (no ingest progress)
- `ingest.started_at` unchanged for the whole watch, `finished_at:null`, `last_error:null`
- daemon.err.log has only the connect line -> a **silent no-timeout hang** (likely a Voyage
  embed HTTP call with no timeout). Never conclude "down" OR "healthy-busy" from `/health` alone;
  check CPU + pglite mtime.

**THE WATCHDOG GAP (important):** `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy` (the
`JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` entry point) checks `/health.ok` + `spawn.ok` only -- NOT
ingest-progress. A daemon wedged mid-ingest answers `ok:true`, so `-IfUnhealthy` says "nothing
to do" and NEVER heals this class. `restart_engine`-style watchdogs that gate on "does /health
answer" are blind to a wedged-but-responsive ingest. **FIX BUILT 2026-07-01 (commit `d1d80cd`
in ~/tools):** `restart-brain-daemon.ps1` now has `Test-IngestWedged` wired into `-IfUnhealthy`
-- wedged = `ingest.running` AND pglite unwritten > `-StallMinutes` (15) AND process CPU idle over
a 5s sample; BOTH required so a slow-but-working ingest is never false-killed, every uncertain path
returns false (fail safe). On wedge it sets `-Force` and heals. ALSO fixed the kill path (part 2 of
the bug below): when the `CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*'` filter finds nothing (empty under
non-elevated watchdog), it now falls back to the authoritative PID from `/health.pid` then
`daemon-lock.json`. New `-DetectOnly` = read-only wedge check. Validated: true-positive against the
real wedge's measured values (pglite 65m stale, CPU 0.016s/6s -> flagged); true-negative via
`-DetectOnly` on the healthy daemon (wedged=False, no false-kill); parse-clean/ASCII. NOTE: a live
wedge (2nd sync, pid 34952) was present during the fix and got healed to fresh pid 31412 around the
06:31 watchdog fire -- can't 100%-attribute the heal to my new code vs a peer restart (no watchdog
stdout log; .vbs runs hidden), but the fix is correct + on the watchdog path (`.vbs` -> `-IfUnhealthy`).

**The fix that worked:**
1. `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -Force` is the sanctioned path (atomic PGlite rollback => force-kill
   mid-ingest is SAFE, brain stays sound). `-IfUnhealthy` alone will NOT act (sees ok:true).
2. BUT it aborted "port 8077 still held": its kill filter is `bun.exe` WHERE
   `CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*'`, and **CommandLine reads back EMPTY when not
   elevated**, so it matched nothing. Under a non-elevated agent, kill by **PID** instead
   (authoritative PID = `~/.gbrain-trading/daemon-lock.json` .pid == `/health.pid` == the 8077
   owner), then relaunch `~/tools/start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached`.
3. Result: old pid 28140 stopped, port released instantly, new pid 34952 up in 4s, came up
   IDLE (did not auto-re-trigger the wedged sync), `/search` 200 in 2.9s, chunks 5501/embedded
   5493 (99.9%, intact). Recall restored.

Root cause found, fixed, committed (`f2cb730`) — and notably **not** where we guessed:

**The embed-timeout theory was wrong.** `embedding.ts` already has a 60s per-request timeout + finite retries (your 2026-05-07 patch), and the wedge showed `last_error:null` — a timed-out embed would throw and set that.
