---
name: feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart
description: "gbrain can wedge mid-ingest (busy:true forever, ok:true) — invisible to the watchdog; diagnose by CPU/pglite-write stall, fix with restart -Force"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 0372b597-ccb7-40ca-8ea7-fc3dd0acdb53
---

2026-07-01: recall.ps1 / `/vault` timed out. First wrong call: "gbrain daemon DOWN." It was
`/health ok:true pid=28140`, `busy:true`, `ingest.running:true` phase `sync:second-brain` --
looked like a normal busy ingest. But it was **wedged**, not working:

**How to tell wedged from busy-working (the discriminators that matter):**
- process CPU delta over 5s = **0.00** (idle, not embedding)
- pglite data dir (`~/.gbrain-trading/brain.pglite`) **last write ~2h old** (no ingest progress)
- `ingest.started_at` unchanged for the whole watch, `finished_at:null`, `last_error:null`
- daemon.err.log has only the connect line -> a **silent no-timeout hang** (likely a Voyage
  embed HTTP call with no timeout). Never conclude "down" OR "healthy-busy" from `/health` alone;
  check CPU + pglite mtime.

**THE WATCHDOG GAP (important):** `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy` (the
`JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` entry point) checks `/health.ok` + `spawn.ok` only -- NOT
ingest-progress. A daemon wedged mid-ingest answers `ok:true`, so `-IfUnhealthy` says "nothing
to do" and NEVER heals this class. `restart_engine`-style watchdogs that gate on "does /health
answer" are blind to a wedged-but-responsive ingest. **FIX BUILT 2026-07-01 (commit `d1d80cd`
in ~/tools):** `restart-brain-daemon.ps1` now has `Test-IngestWedged` wired into `-IfUnhealthy`
-- wedged = `ingest.running` AND pglite unwritten > `-StallMinutes` (15) AND process CPU idle over
a 5s sample; BOTH required so a slow-but-working ingest is never false-killed, every uncertain path
returns false (fail safe). On wedge it sets `-Force` and heals. ALSO fixed the kill path (part 2 of
the bug below): when the `CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*'` filter finds nothing (empty under
non-elevated watchdog), it now falls back to the authoritative PID from `/health.pid` then
`daemon-lock.json`. New `-DetectOnly` = read-only wedge check. Validated: true-positive against the
real wedge's measured values (pglite 65m stale, CPU 0.016s/6s -> flagged); true-negative via
`-DetectOnly` on the healthy daemon (wedged=False, no false-kill); parse-clean/ASCII. NOTE: a live
wedge (2nd sync, pid 34952) was present during the fix and got healed to fresh pid 31412 around the
06:31 watchdog fire -- can't 100%-attribute the heal to my new code vs a peer restart (no watchdog
stdout log; .vbs runs hidden), but the fix is correct + on the watchdog path (`.vbs` -> `-IfUnhealthy`).

**The fix that worked:**
1. `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -Force` is the sanctioned path (atomic PGlite rollback => force-kill
   mid-ingest is SAFE, brain stays sound). `-IfUnhealthy` alone will NOT act (sees ok:true).
2. BUT it aborted "port 8077 still held": its kill filter is `bun.exe` WHERE
   `CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*'`, and **CommandLine reads back EMPTY when not
   elevated**, so it matched nothing. Under a non-elevated agent, kill by **PID** instead
   (authoritative PID = `~/.gbrain-trading/daemon-lock.json` .pid == `/health.pid` == the 8077
   owner), then relaunch `~/tools/start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached`.
3. Result: old pid 28140 stopped, port released instantly, new pid 34952 up in 4s, came up
   IDLE (did not auto-re-trigger the wedged sync), `/search` 200 in 2.9s, chunks 5501/embedded
   5493 (99.9%, intact). Recall restored.

Launcher/paths: daemon = `bun.exe` running `daemon-server.ts`, port 8077, data
`~/.gbrain-trading/brain.pglite`, embed voyage-finance-2/1024. Cockpit (zero-DB-touch):
`~/scripts/gbrain/gbrain-status.ps1`. Restart: `~/tools/restart-brain-daemon.ps1`. Launch:
`~/tools/start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached`. Periodic sync task: `Jarvis-VaultGbrainSync`.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (commit `f2cb730`, ~/tools): NOT the embed call -- `embedding.ts` ALREADY
has a 60s per-request timeout + finite retries (Amo's 2026-05-07 patch), and the wedge showed
`last_error:null` (a timed-out embed would throw and set last_error). The real hang is in
`sync.ts`'s `git()` helper: the Node fallback set `timeout:30000` but the **Bun.spawnSync path the
daemon actually uses had NO timeout**. `performSync`'s first step is `git pull --ff-only` (network) --
a hung remote / stale `index.lock` / interactive credential prompt blocks `Bun.spawnSync` forever ->
single-writer thread wedged (busy, CPU idle, no PGLite write, last_error:null). Fix: added
`timeout` (`GBRAIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`=30000) + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to the Bun git path so a hung/
prompting git fails fast (killed -> throw -> last_error -> retry next fire). Build clean, sync suite
32 pass/0 fail. **Deploy = daemon restart** (bun runs source directly; no dist) -- gated on Amo.
The watchdog change (`d1d80cd`) remains the backstop that heals a wedge if one still slips through.
LESSON (systematic-debugging): the "likely embed timeout" guess was WRONG -- the embed path was
already guarded; `last_error:null` + the timeout-guarded embed pointed at an un-timeout'd subprocess,
not the network embed. Check what's already handled before adding a redundant fix. [[project_obsidian_health_loop_2026_07_01]]
[[feedback_mcp_prompt_wedge_bash_bypass]]

<#
  restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -- the SANCTIONED restart path for the single-writer gbrain brain daemon.

  Mirrors restart_engine.ps1: stop the current opener cleanly, wait for the lock/port to release, then
  relaunch DETACHED (session-independent, survives the shell that ran this). Use this instead of an
  ad-hoc Stop-Process -- the daemon owns the one PGlite connection, so an uncoordinated kill mid-ingest
  is the exact failure class this daemon exists to delete.

  Safe to kill when ingest is idle: PGlite transactions are atomic (a dropped connection rolls back,
  the heap stays intact). This script refuses to stop while an ingest is RUNNING unless -Force is given.

  -Force : stop even if an ingest is in progress (rolls back the in-flight embed batch; brain stays sound).

  -IfUnhealthy : no-op if the daemon already answers /health OK; otherwise stop + relaunch. This is the
  WATCHDOG entry point -- a bare port check (start-brain-daemon's idempotency) can't tell a healthy
  daemon from a wedged one (port bound, /health dead), so the watchdog would never heal a wedge. With
  -IfUnhealthy the watchdog heals BOTH down and wedged daemons.

  Run it yourself (human-in-the-loop) when an agent's destructive-op guard blocks a raw kill:
    ! pwsh -NoProfile -File C:\Users\mattm\tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1
#>
param([int]$Port = 8077, [switch]$Force, [switch]$IfUnhealthy, [int]$StallMinutes = 15, [switch]$DetectOnly)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$launcher = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'

function Test-Port { Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $Port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue }

function Test-IngestWedged {
  # Wedge detector: the daemon claims ingest.running but is making NO progress -- PGlite unwritten
  # for > $StallMinutes AND the process CPU idle over a short sample. BOTH signals are required so a
  # slow-but-working ingest (still writing PGlite, or burning CPU) is never false-killed. Every
  # uncertain path returns $false (fail SAFE -- never kill a daemon we can't prove is wedged).
  # This closes the -IfUnhealthy blind spot: a wedged ingest answers /health ok:true forever.
  param($Health)
  if (-not $Health -or -not $Health.ingest -or -not $Health.ingest.running) { return $false }
  $pg = "$($Health.data_dir)"
  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($pg) -or -not (Test-Path $pg)) {
    $pg = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\brain.pglite'
  }
  if (-not (Test-Path $pg)) { return $false }
  $newest = Get-ChildItem $pg -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  if (-not $newest) { return $false }
  $stallMin = ((Get-Date) - $newest.LastWriteTime).TotalMinutes
  if ($stallMin -le $StallMinutes) { return $false }   # wrote PGlite recently => progressing => healthy
  $proc = Get-Process -Id ([int]$Health.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $proc) { return $false }
  $c1 = [double]$proc.CPU
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
  $proc2 = Get-Process -Id ([int]$Health.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $proc2) { return $false }
  $cpuDelta = [double]$proc2.CPU - $c1
  Write-Host ("[restart-brain-daemon] ingest.running but PGlite stale {0:N1} min (> {1}) and CPU delta {2:N3}s/5s" -f $stallMin, $StallMinutes, $cpuDelta)
  return ($cpuDelta -lt 0.3)   # CPU idle => hung, not working => wedged
}

# Watchdog gate: if the daemon is already serving /health AND can spawn children, do nothing. A
# generous timeout avoids killing a healthy-but-busy daemon (/health serializes individually and stays
# responsive even mid-ingest). ?deep=1 adds a child-spawn probe: a spawn-dead daemon (its cwd was
# deleted -> Windows CreateProcess fails) answers /health ok but can't run /sync's git ops -- treat
# spawn.ok=false as unhealthy so the watchdog heals it too. ($null spawn = older daemon w/o the probe;
# fall back to ok alone for backward compat during the upgrade window.) Any failure -> stop + relaunch.
# Read-only diagnostic: report whether the daemon is wedged, act on nothing. For testing the
# detector and for operator use (a zero-side-effect wedge check).
if ($DetectOnly) {
  try { $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10 }
  catch { Write-Host "DETECT: /health unreachable (daemon down or port unbound)."; exit 0 }
  $wedged = Test-IngestWedged -Health $h
  Write-Host ("DETECT: wedged={0}  ok={1}  ingest.running={2}  pid={3}" -f $wedged, $h.ok, $h.ingest.running, $h.pid)
  exit 0
}

if ($IfUnhealthy) {
  $healthy = $false
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10
    $spawnOk = ($null -eq $h.spawn) -or [bool]$h.spawn.ok
    $healthy = ([bool]$h.ok) -and $spawnOk
    if (([bool]$h.ok) -and -not $spawnOk) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health ok but spawn DEAD ($($h.spawn.error)) - healing spawn-dead daemon."
    }
  } catch { $healthy = $false }
  if ($healthy) {
    # NEW: a daemon that answers ok can still be WEDGED mid-ingest (busy:true forever, no progress).
    # -IfUnhealthy used to say "nothing to do" and never heal this class. Now: detect it and force-heal.
    if (Test-IngestWedged -Health $h) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] WEDGED ingest detected (no PGlite progress + CPU idle) - forcing heal."
      $Force = $true   # let the mid-ingest refuse-gate below through; force-kill is safe (atomic PGlite rollback)
    } else {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health OK (pid=$($h.pid), spawn ok) - nothing to do."; exit 0
    }
  } else {
    Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] -IfUnhealthy: daemon down, wedged, or spawn-dead - healing."
  }
}

# Refuse to yank the lock out from under a live embed unless forced.
if (Test-Port) {
  try {
    $st = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 5
    if ($st.ingest.running -and -not $Force) {
      Write-Error "daemon is mid-ingest (phase=$($st.ingest.phase)). Re-run with -Force to stop anyway, or wait for it to finish."
      exit 3
    }
  } catch { Write-Warning "port $Port up but /health unreachable; proceeding to stop." }
}

# Find and stop the daemon's bun process. Primary: CommandLine match (robust against pid drift).
# Fallback: authoritative PID from /health then the daemon lock file -- because
# Win32_Process.CommandLine reads back EMPTY for a NON-ELEVATED caller (the watchdog runs LIMITED),
# so the CommandLine filter matches nothing and a wedge would never get killed. (See
# feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart -- this exact bug aborted the heal with "port still held".)
$procs = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'" |
             Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*' })
if ($procs.Count -gt 0) {
  foreach ($p in $procs) {
    Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] stopping bun pid $($p.ProcessId)"
    Stop-Process -Id $p.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  }
} else {
  $pidCandidates = @()
  try { $pidCandidates += [int](Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 5).pid } catch { }
  $lockFile = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\daemon-lock.json'
  if (Test-Path $lockFile) { try { $pidCandidates += [int]((Get-Content $lockFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).pid) } catch { } }
  $pidCandidates = @($pidCandidates | Where-Object { $_ -gt 0 } | Select-Object -Unique)
  if ($pidCandidates.Count -eq 0) { Write-Warning "no bun proc via CommandLine and no PID from /health or lock file." }
  foreach ($pp in $pidCandidates) {
    $bp = Get-Process -Id $pp -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($bp -and $bp.ProcessName -eq 'bun') {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] stopping bun pid $pp (PID fallback -- CommandLine empty under non-elevated watchdog)"
      Stop-Process -Id $pp -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
  }
}

# Wait for the port (and thus the PGlite lock) to actually release.
$n = 0
while ((Test-Port) -and $n -lt 20) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500; $n++ }
if (Test-Port) { Write-Error "port $Port still held after stop; aborting relaunch."; exit 4 }
Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] port $Port released."

# Relaunch detached (the launcher's own port-check makes this a no-op if something already rebound).
& pwsh -NoProfile -File $launcher -Detached

# Verify the new daemon answers. A cold PGlite open of the ~135MB brain + Voyage key resolution can
# take well over 30s, so wait up to 90s before declaring failure (avoids a false "did not come up"
# that alarms the operator / could trigger spurious watchdog churn).
$n = 0
while ($n -lt 90) {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; $n++
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 3
    if ($h.ok) { Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] UP: pid=$($h.pid) model=$($h.embed.model)/$($h.embed.dim) chunks=$($h.stats.chunk_count) embedded=$($h.stats.embedded_count)"; exit 0 }
  } catch { }
}
Write-Error "daemon did not come up on $Port within 90s; check ~/.gbrain-trading/logs/daemon.err.log"
exit 5

# Three JARVIS monitoring loops — compiled + deployed 2026-07-01

Amo asked (after the loop-medic live-arm + the durable `-DoApply` persistence fix) to
`/loopify` three read-only monitors. All are the **safe auto-deploy class** (read-only,
report, ping-only), all local-scheduled, all verified GREEN end-to-end (runner smoke-test +
scheduler-fired `LastTaskResult 0x0` + heartbeat stamped + report/state written).

## The three loops
| id | archetype | schedule | pings when | runner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine-health-watch` | dynamic (poller) | **HOURLY** | health-state **transition** to unhealthy, and on recovery | `~/.claude/loops/engine-health-watch/run.ps1` |
| `llm-burn-monitor` | scheduled-cadence | DAILY@10:45 | trailing-24h `cost_usd` > threshold | `~/.claude/loops/llm-burn-monitor/run.ps1` |
| `pr-staleness-sweep` | scheduled-cadence | DAILY@10:50 | any open PR older than N days | `~/.claude/loops/pr-staleness-sweep/run.ps1` |

## Design decisions / tuning knobs (the non-obvious bits)
- **engine-health-watch is TRANSITION-based, not every-poll.** It reads `state.json`
  (`{unhealthy,reasons,checked}`) and pings ONLY when the healthy<->unhealthy state flips —
  so a sustained outage is one "DOWN" ping + one "RECOVERED" ping, never one-per-hour.
  Unhealthy = `status!=ok` OR `llm_path_healthy=false` OR `tradingview_mcp_healthy=false`
  OR `ibkr_connected=false`. **Single-leg LLM does NOT alarm** (criterion is
  `llm_path_healthy`, which stays true on the gpt-4o-mini leg) — verified: smoke-test on the
  current single-leg engine returned healthy/no-ping. CAVEAT flagged to Amo: IBKR paper (4002)
  can be legitimately down outside trading hours, so it MAY produce a session-boundary
  ping-pair; if noisy, drop ibkr from the condition or add a market-hours gate. HOURLY cadence
  is tunable (loopctl's schedule parser only does HOURLY/DAILY/WEEKLY — for sub-hourly, patch
  the task's RepetitionInterval).
- **llm-burn-monitor threshold default = $15/day** (`-ThresholdUsd`). Current baseline at
  build time = **$4.36 trailing-24h** (2935 calls, all gpt-4o-mini — the cheap single leg), so
  $15 catches a ~3.5x spike (e.g. a return to expensive-Claude ~$30/day, or a runaway). Queries
  `engine/data/llm_costs.db` table `llm_calls` (cols: timestamp TEXT UTC-ISO, model, cost_usd
  REAL, provider, success). Cutoff computed in **Python UTC ISO** to lexically match the stored
  `+00:00` timestamps exactly (a naive SQLite `datetime('now','-1 day')` compare is off by the
  `T`-vs-space at the day boundary). Runs via the engine venv python (`engine/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`).
- **pr-staleness-sweep uses `gh api` REST, NOT GraphQL** — deliberately, to dodge the shared
  5000/hr GraphQL cap (which was exhausted during this very session). `StaleDays` default 7,
  `Repo` default `mattamundson/jarvis-trader`. A gh failure (not installed / not auth'd /
  rate-limited) is a **clean GREEN no-op**, never a false RED on a low-priority digest. Baseline
  at build: 14 open PRs, 0 stale (>=7d) — the repo merges fast, so 7d rarely trips (that's the point).

## Brakes (all six, per loop)
Preflight (deps present / dep-down = clean no-op) · heartbeat via `loopctl -Heartbeat` ·
fail-closed (RED + notify + exit 1 on runner exception) · stop/runtime cap · budget (1 call/query
per fire) · notify via `JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` (confirmed set, User scope → Discord). Runners are
ASCII-only, parse-clean under pwsh 7 (the task runtime via the WindowsApps shim), default `$Id`
hardcoded to match the registered id (tasks invoke with no `-Id` arg).

## Operate
`loopctl -Action List` (board) · `-Action Status -Id <id>` · `-Action Restart -Id <id>` (run now)
· reports at `~/.claude/loops/<id>/report-*.md` · kill: `schtasks /Delete /F /TN Loopify-<id>`.
Operator guide: `~/.claude/loops/OPERATING_GUIDE.md`.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\mattm\.claude\skills\loopify # Loopify — the prompt-to-loop compiler > A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes. > Loopify's job: take a goal Amo states once, and leave behind a **running loop** that pursues it — safely, observably, and killably. **Autonomy: FULL AUTO-DEPLOY** (Amo's standing choice, 2026-06-30). Safe loops register, deploy, and start themselves. The brakes below plus the machine's existing hooks (credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the safety net. Only genuinely destructive / outward-facing steady-state actions stop at a human gate (see §Safety). --- ## The one-screen model ``` GOAL (English) ──▶ [1 CLASSIFY] ──▶ [2 LEDGER] ──▶ [3 RUNNER] ──▶ [4 BRAKES] ──▶ [5 FEEDBACK] ──▶ [6 REGISTER+DEPLOY] ──▶ running loop what shape? what's "done" where runs? how it stops how it learns loopctl + verify + report ``` Every stage is mandatory. Create a todo per stage and work them in order. Do not skip to deploy. --- ## Control plane All loops share one registry and one CLI: **`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1`** → `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`. ```powershell loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id -Goal "" -Archetype -Runner [-RunnerPath

] [-Schedule ] [-StopCondition ] [-BudgetCap ] [-Deploy] loopctl.ps1 -Action Deploy -Id # (re)create the scheduled task for a local-scheduled loop loopctl.ps1 -Action List # fleet board loopctl.ps1 -Action Status [-Id ] # full JSON loopctl.ps1 -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR # runners call this every iteration loopctl.ps1 -Action Remove -Id [-Purge] # -Purge also deletes the scheduled task ``` `-Deploy` on a `local-scheduled` loop creates a `Loopify-` Windows task (shim pwsh, battery-gate cleared, LIMITED, daytime). For every other runner, deploy is done by *you* (the agent) with the right tool, then recorded via `-Action Register`. --- ## Stage 1 — CLASSIFY (what shape is this loop?) Walk the decision tree top-down; first match wins. | If the goal… | Archetype | Canonical runner | |---|---|---| | watches **external state** and acts when it changes (CI, a queue, a price, a file landing) | **dynamic** | in-session `/loop` + `ScheduleWakeup`, OR local-scheduled poller | | drains a **known, finite backlog** (a task list, a set of files) to empty | **backlog-drain** | in-session `/ralph` | | drains a backlog that **regenerates itself** — you must re-discover work each pass | **discovery-drain** | in-session `/jarvis-loop` | | must **push a quality metric to a bar** (score ≥ X, tests green, latency < Y) by generate→judge→improve | **evaluator-optimizer** | in-session loop or Workflow | | fires on a **clock** to read/compute/report (digest, audit, briefing) | **scheduled-cadence** | local-scheduled (fs/tooling) OR cloud routine (Gmail/Cal/pure-cognition) | | is **one big parallelizable pass** with a verify step (review N files, migrate N sites) | **fan-out-verify** | `Workflow` | | **proposes** a change, a second pass **checks** it, then commit | **maker-checker** | in-session loop or Workflow | Write down: `archetype = ` and one sentence why. If two fit, prefer the *simplest runner* that satisfies the stop condition. **Runner picker (hard constraints):** - Touches `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local fs → **local-scheduled** or **in-session**. NEVER a cloud routine (the sandbox can't see the local disk — it fails silently). - Pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar / Drive / web → **cloud routine** (`/schedule` or CCR `create_trigger`). - Needs many agents at once → **Workflow** (fan-out-verify). - Needs to run while no Claude session is open → **local-scheduled** or **cloud** (never in-session). --- ## Stage 2 — LEDGER (what is "done", and where does state live?) A loop without a written ledger is an infinite loop. Define both: 1. **Done predicate** — the exact, checkable condition that ends the loop or a run: - drain: `prd.json` all `passes:true` AND discovery finds 0 new (discovery-drain) / backlog empty (backlog-drain) - evaluator-optimizer: `metric >= threshold` OR `no improvement for K rounds` - scheduled-cadence: never "done" — it's a heartbeat; the run is done when the report is emitted - dynamic: the watched condition resolved (merge landed, queue empty) 2. **State store** — where the loop remembers across iterations: - drain → a `prd.json` / queue file (reuse the ralph/jarvis-loop layout) - evaluator-optimizer → a metrics JSONL (`~/.claude/loops//metrics.jsonl`), one row per round - scheduled-cadence → last-run marker + the report file under `~/.claude/loops//` - dynamic → the external state itself is the store; record last-seen in `~/.claude/loops//state.json` No state store you can point at → you have not finished Stage 2. --- ## Stage 3 — RUNNER (scaffold the execution substrate) Create `~/.claude/loops//` (or, for a repo-scoped loop, `/scripts/loops/`). Put the runner there. - **local-scheduled** → copy `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (next to this SKILL), fill the WORK block. It already wires preflight, heartbeat, fail-closed, notify, and the loopctl heartbeat call. ASCII-only (PS 5.1 will run it). Use `127.0.0.1`, shim paths, battery-safe (loopctl handles the last one at deploy). - **in-session** (`/loop`, `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`) → no script; the runner is the skill. Register the loop so it's on the board, and use `ScheduleWakeup`/the skill's own loop for iteration. - **cloud** → the runner is the routine prompt. Write it as a *complete standalone instruction* (fresh session each fire sees no history). - **workflow** → the runner is the Workflow script (pipeline/parallel + verify stage). - **evaluator-optimizer** (in-session or workflow) → copy `templates/evaluator-optimizer.md` — generate → *independent* judge panel → improve, with stop-at-bar / converge / cap / budget brakes already wired. --- ## Stage 4 — BRAKES (mandatory — no loop deploys without all six) Every deployed loop MUST carry all six. This is what makes it an *engineered* loop, not a runaway. 1. **Preflight gate** — verify dependencies before doing work; abort (no-op, exit 0) if a dep is down. (Don't trade if the engine's down; don't digest if the data source is unreachable.) 2. **Heartbeat** — call `loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR` every iteration. A dead loop stops stamping → the fleet board shows it stale. 3. **Fail-closed** — on any error: stamp RED, notify, exit **non-zero**. Never swallow an error into a green "success". (Anti-pattern: "no error in the log so it worked.") 4. **Stop condition** — the Stage-2 done predicate, checked every iteration. Even cadence loops need a max-runtime guard. 5. **Budget / iteration cap** — a hard ceiling (max iterations, max tokens, max wall-clock). The backstop when the stop condition never trips. 6. **Notification** — on RED / stop / budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` Discord, or Telegram). No-op silently if unset — never throw, never block. For PowerShell runners, brakes 1-3 and 6 come pre-wired in `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. For in-session/cloud/workflow, wire the equivalents (a Workflow gets brakes from `budget.total`, a stop-count loop, and a verify stage). --- ## Stage 5 — FEEDBACK (how the loop learns / self-corrects) Match the archetype: - **discovery-drain** → the discovery phase IS the feedback (re-scan signals each pass). - **evaluator-optimizer** → a judge/verify step scores each attempt; the next attempt reads the score. Use an *independent* judge (separate agent/criteria), not self-grading. - **maker-checker / fan-out-verify** → a second pass adversarially checks the first before commit. Default the checker to skeptical. - **scheduled-cadence** → the report's own deltas vs last run (flag regressions). - **dynamic** → re-read external state each wake; act only on genuine change. A loop with no feedback is a cron job. That's fine *if* the goal is truly stateless cadence — but say so explicitly. --- ## Stage 6 — REGISTER + DEPLOY + OBSERVE 1. **Register** via `loopctl -Action Register …` with the archetype, runner, stop condition, and budget cap filled in. 2. **Deploy** (full auto): - `local-scheduled` → add `-Deploy` (loopctl creates + battery-clears the task). Then **verify it exists**: `schtasks /Query /TN Loopify- /V /FO LIST` shows `Ready` + a plausible Next Run. - `cloud` → create the trigger with CCR `create_trigger` (fresh-session mode for standalone) or `/schedule`, then `Register` (record `task_name`=trigger id). - `in-session` → start the loop now (invoke `/ralph` / `/jarvis-loop` / `/loop`), Register it so it's on the board. - `workflow` → run the `Workflow`; Register a one-shot entry for the audit trail. 3. **Smoke-run once** if safe (a scheduled runner: `Start-ScheduledTask` then read the heartbeat / report). Confirm GREEN. Per verification.md — never claim it runs from the absence of an error; hit the actual heartbeat/report. 4. **Report to Amo** in the format below. ### Report format (always end a /loopify run with this) ``` LOOP COMPILED: goal : archetype : runner: ledger : done = state = brakes : preflight | cap | stop | notify deployed : status= observe : loopctl -Action List (and: ) kill : gated? : ``` --- ## Safety — what full auto-deploy does NOT cover Full auto-deploy means: read-only, report, local-fs-analysis, and in-repo maker-checker loops **deploy and start themselves**. It does **not** authorize a loop whose *steady-state action* is destructive or outward-facing. If the compiled loop would, on its own, repeatedly: - place **live** trades, or flip a paper/live flag - `git push` to a shared branch (main/master/develop/release/*), or force-push - mutate secrets / `.env` / 1Password - delete or mass-move files (always archive, never delete) - restart a prod service (engine, Hermes gateway) unguarded - send messages to **third parties** (email/DM to people who aren't Amo) then **do not auto-deploy it live**. Instead: compile it fully, register it with `status=blocked`, deploy it in **report-only / dry-run** mode (or gate the mutating step behind a flag defaulting OFF), and surface the gate to Amo with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The loop's dangerous step still hits the machine's PreToolUse hooks as a second line of defense — but the design-time gate is yours to hold. Everything else deploys. When in doubt between "useful cadence report" and "outward action", ship the report and let Amo pull the trigger on the action. --- ## Anti-patterns | Anti-pattern | Why it's wrong | Do instead | |---|---|---| | Deploy without a stop condition | infinite loop / runaway spend | Stage 2 done predicate is mandatory | | Green on error (swallow exceptions) | silent failure looks healthy | fail-closed: RED + notify + non-zero exit | | Cloud routine that reads `C:\Users\mattm\` | sandbox can't see local fs — fails silently | local-scheduled for anything local | | Self-grading evaluator loop | grades its own homework, never converges | independent judge / adversarial checker | | Night-time scheduled task (00:00-05:59) | machine asleep → 0xFFFD0000 | schedule 09:00-11:00 (Stage 6) | | One loop per file / per finding | fleet noise | group related work into one loop | | `git add -A` inside a runner | sweeps the 1,450-file backlog | stage per-file, pathspec commit | | Skipping Register | loop invisible + unkillable from the board | always Register, even in-session/workflow | --- ## Dogfood examples (shapes, not prescriptions) - "keep an eye on the self-healing scheduled tasks and ping me if one stays red" → **scheduled-cadence**, local-scheduled, daily 10:00, report-only, notify on red. Safe → auto-deploy. - "get the MES VWAP strategy's paper Sharpe above 0.5" → **evaluator-optimizer**, in-session/Workflow, metric ledger, independent gate-v2 judge, cap 20 rounds. Backtest-only → auto-deploy; any live wiring is Amo-gated. - "review every open PR for the exec-path stack and verify findings" → **fan-out-verify**, Workflow, adversarial verify stage. Read-only → auto-deploy. - "watch for the Vertex quota grant and flip the engine to Vertex-primary" → **dynamic**, poller; but the flip mutates engine config → deploy the *watch* live, **gate the flip** (notify Amo when granted). --- ## Cross-references - Brakes library + heartbeat: `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1` - Loop archetypes in the wild: `/ralph` (backlog), `/jarvis-loop` (discovery), `/loop` (dynamic) - Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `~/.claude/rules/windows-pitfalls.md` - Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `~/.claude/rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling - Verify-before-claiming: `~/.claude/rules/verification.md` - Destructive-op gate: `~/.claude/rules/destructive-op-gates.md` ARGUMENTS: Compile three read-only monitoring loops for JARVIS: (1) engine-health watchdog — poll http://127.0.0.1:8010/health on a cadence, ping JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK when status!=ok OR llm_path_healthy=false OR tradingview_mcp_healthy=false OR ibkr disconnected; (2) LLM burn monitor — read engine/data/llm_costs.db daily, ping if trailing-24h spend crosses a threshold; (3) PR-staleness sweep — list open PRs in mattamundson/jarvis-trader, ping-only digest of PRs open past N days. All local scheduled tasks, 09:00–11:00 window, ASCII-only PS runners, six brakes each.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map, list_code_components, get_code_component_info)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

<#
  restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -- the SANCTIONED restart path for the single-writer gbrain brain daemon.

  Mirrors restart_engine.ps1: stop the current opener cleanly, wait for the lock/port to release, then
  relaunch DETACHED (session-independent, survives the shell that ran this). Use this instead of an
  ad-hoc Stop-Process -- the daemon owns the one PGlite connection, so an uncoordinated kill mid-ingest
  is the exact failure class this daemon exists to delete.

  Safe to kill when ingest is idle: PGlite transactions are atomic (a dropped connection rolls back,
  the heap stays intact). This script refuses to stop while an ingest is RUNNING unless -Force is given.

  -Force : stop even if an ingest is in progress (rolls back the in-flight embed batch; brain stays sound).

  -IfUnhealthy : no-op if the daemon already answers /health OK; otherwise stop + relaunch. This is the
  WATCHDOG entry point -- a bare port check (start-brain-daemon's idempotency) can't tell a healthy
  daemon from a wedged one (port bound, /health dead), so the watchdog would never heal a wedge. With
  -IfUnhealthy the watchdog heals BOTH down and wedged daemons.

  Run it yourself (human-in-the-loop) when an agent's destructive-op guard blocks a raw kill:
    ! pwsh -NoProfile -File C:\Users\mattm\tools\restart-brain-daemon.ps1
#>
param([int]$Port = 8077, [switch]$Force, [switch]$IfUnhealthy, [int]$StallMinutes = 15, [switch]$DetectOnly)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$launcher = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\start-brain-daemon.ps1'

function Test-Port { Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $Port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue }

function Test-IngestWedged {
  # Wedge detector: the daemon claims ingest.running but is making NO progress -- PGlite unwritten
  # for > $StallMinutes AND the process CPU idle over a short sample. BOTH signals are required so a
  # slow-but-working ingest (still writing PGlite, or burning CPU) is never false-killed. Every
  # uncertain path returns $false (fail SAFE -- never kill a daemon we can't prove is wedged).
  # This closes the -IfUnhealthy blind spot: a wedged ingest answers /health ok:true forever.
  param($Health)
  if (-not $Health -or -not $Health.ingest -or -not $Health.ingest.running) { return $false }
  $pg = "$($Health.data_dir)"
  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($pg) -or -not (Test-Path $pg)) {
    $pg = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\brain.pglite'
  }
  if (-not (Test-Path $pg)) { return $false }
  $newest = Get-ChildItem $pg -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  if (-not $newest) { return $false }
  $stallMin = ((Get-Date) - $newest.LastWriteTime).TotalMinutes
  if ($stallMin -le $StallMinutes) { return $false }   # wrote PGlite recently => progressing => healthy
  $proc = Get-Process -Id ([int]$Health.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $proc) { return $false }
  $c1 = [double]$proc.CPU
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
  $proc2 = Get-Process -Id ([int]$Health.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $proc2) { return $false }
  $cpuDelta = [double]$proc2.CPU - $c1
  Write-Host ("[restart-brain-daemon] ingest.running but PGlite stale {0:N1} min (> {1}) and CPU delta {2:N3}s/5s" -f $stallMin, $StallMinutes, $cpuDelta)

# responsive even mid-ingest). ?deep=1 adds a child-spawn probe: a spawn-dead daemon (its cwd was
# deleted -> Windows CreateProcess fails) answers /health ok but can't run /sync's git ops -- treat
# spawn.ok=false as unhealthy so the watchdog heals it too. ($null spawn = older daemon w/o the probe;
# fall back to ok alone for backward compat during the upgrade window.) Any failure -> stop + relaunch.
# Read-only diagnostic: report whether the daemon is wedged, act on nothing. For testing the
# detector and for operator use (a zero-side-effect wedge check).
if ($DetectOnly) {
  try { $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10 }
  catch { Write-Host "DETECT: /health unreachable (daemon down or port unbound)."; exit 0 }
  $wedged = Test-IngestWedged -Health $h
  Write-Host ("DETECT: wedged={0}  ok={1}  ingest.running={2}  pid={3}" -f $wedged, $h.ok, $h.ingest.running, $h.pid)
  exit 0
}

if ($IfUnhealthy) {
  $healthy = $false
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health?deep=1" -TimeoutSec 10
    $spawnOk = ($null -eq $h.spawn) -or [bool]$h.spawn.ok
    $healthy = ([bool]$h.ok) -and $spawnOk
    if (([bool]$h.ok) -and -not $spawnOk) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health ok but spawn DEAD ($($h.spawn.error)) - healing spawn-dead daemon."
    }
  } catch { $healthy = $false }
  if ($healthy) {
    # NEW: a daemon that answers ok can still be WEDGED mid-ingest (busy:true forever, no progress).
    # -IfUnhealthy used to say "nothing to do" and never heal this class. Now: detect it and force-heal.
    if (Test-IngestWedged -Health $h) {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] WEDGED ingest detected (no PGlite progress + CPU idle) - forcing heal."
      $Force = $true   # let the mid-ingest refuse-gate below through; force-kill is safe (atomic PGlite rollback)
    } else {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] /health OK (pid=$($h.pid), spawn ok) - nothing to do."; exit 0
    }
  } else {
    Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] -IfUnhealthy: daemon down, wedged, or spawn-dead - healing."
  }
}

# Refuse to yank the lock out from under a live embed unless forced.
if (Test-Port) {
  try {
    $st = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 5
    if ($st.ingest.running -and -not $Force) {
      Write-Error "daemon is mid-ingest (phase=$($st.ingest.phase)). Re-run with -Force to stop anyway, or wait for it to finish."
      exit 3
    }
  } catch { Write-Warning "port $Port up but /health unreachable; proceeding to stop." }
}

# Fallback: authoritative PID from /health then the daemon lock file -- because
# Win32_Process.CommandLine reads back EMPTY for a NON-ELEVATED caller (the watchdog runs LIMITED),
# so the CommandLine filter matches nothing and a wedge would never get killed. (See
# feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart -- this exact bug aborted the heal with "port still held".)
$procs = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'" |
             Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*' })
if ($procs.Count -gt 0) {
  foreach ($p in $procs) {
    Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] stopping bun pid $($p.ProcessId)"
    Stop-Process -Id $p.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  }
} else {
  $pidCandidates = @()
  try { $pidCandidates += [int](Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 5).pid } catch { }
  $lockFile = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\daemon-lock.json'
  if (Test-Path $lockFile) { try { $pidCandidates += [int]((Get-Content $lockFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).pid) } catch { } }
  $pidCandidates = @($pidCandidates | Where-Object { $_ -gt 0 } | Select-Object -Unique)
  if ($pidCandidates.Count -eq 0) { Write-Warning "no bun proc via CommandLine and no PID from /health or lock file." }
  foreach ($pp in $pidCandidates) {
    $bp = Get-Process -Id $pp -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($bp -and $bp.ProcessName -eq 'bun') {
      Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] stopping bun pid $pp (PID fallback -- CommandLine empty under non-elevated watchdog)"
      Stop-Process -Id $pp -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
  }
}

# Wait for the port (and thus the PGlite lock) to actually release.
$n = 0
while ((Test-Port) -and $n -lt 20) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500; $n++ }
if (Test-Port) { Write-Error "port $Port still held after stop; aborting relaunch."; exit 4 }
Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] port $Port released."

# Relaunch detached (the launcher's own port-check makes this a no-op if something already rebound).
& pwsh -NoProfile -File $launcher -Detached

# Verify the new daemon answers. A cold PGlite open of the ~135MB brain + Voyage key resolution can
# take well over 30s, so wait up to 90s before declaring failure (avoids a false "did not come up"
# that alarms the operator / could trigger spurious watchdog churn).
$n = 0
while ($n -lt 90) {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; $n++
  try {
    $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 3
    if ($h.ok) { Write-Host "[restart-brain-daemon] UP: pid=$($h.pid) model=$($h.embed.model)/$($h.embed.dim) chunks=$($h.stats.chunk_count) embedded=$($h.stats.embedded_count)"; exit 0 }
  } catch { }
}
Write-Error "daemon did not come up on $Port within 90s; check ~/.gbrain-trading/logs/daemon.err.log"
exit 5

While that validates in the background (~5–8 min, I'll be notified), here's where things stand.

## What was wrong

The gbrain vault-sync had silently stopped ingesting new content since ~08:25. Root cause, fully characterized:

- The daemon's `git rev-parse HEAD` was **failing in 52 ms** (not hanging 30 s — the old error message *said* "timed out after 30000ms / hung remote/lock/prompt / deleted cwd," and all three were wrong and cost real diagnosis time).
- It's a **Bun-on-Windows corruption specific to the long-lived daemon instance**: `Bun.spawnSync` with **piped stdio** spuriously fast-fails on repo-access git, while the health probe (`stdout:'ignore'`) survives the *same* process. I ruled it out across seven controlled fresh-process reproductions (WASM in-memory/file-backed, handle count, env-reconstruct, hidden/detached launch, timeout-poison) — none reproduce it; only the aged instance fails, and a restart clears it.
- **The watchdog was blind to it**: the failure has `ingest.running:false, phase:error`, so `Test-IngestWedged` (which needs `running:true`) said "healthy, nothing to do" across 3+ hours of fires.

## Fixes shipped (committed `a4e55be`, not pushed)

1. **`sync.ts` `git()` — structural fix.** Redirect git's stdout/stderr to temp **files** instead of a pipe (mirrors the probe's `ignore` path that provably survives the corruption), retry a fast signal-kill, and report honestly (only "timeout" when elapsed actually ≥ the limit). Sync suite: **32 pass / 0 fail**; file-redirect returns correct output.
2. **`restart-brain-daemon.ps1` — watchdog gap closed.** New `Test-SyncPersistentlyFailing` heals the spawn-instability class after ≥2 consecutive fires, storm-safe via a 30-min cooldown, and *only* that error class (never a legit `non-fast-forward`). Logic verified across 5 cases.

## Validating now

My new watchdog code is **already live** — the 11:21 fire ran it and stamped `consecutive:1`; the 11:26 fire will hit threshold → restart the daemon → redeploy the patched `sync.ts` → ingestion resumes. The background monitor will confirm the pid change and that a fresh sync succeeds (not `error`). I'll report the verified outcome when it lands — not claiming success until the sync comes back green.

## Remaining for the "gbrain isn't done" mandate

Once the heal is confirmed, the backlog I'd tackle next, in priority order: (a) a **stale-last-successful-sync** metric surfaced on `/health` so this class is *visible* not just auto-healed; (b) the 1,214 orphan pages (61% — likely the YAML-frontmatter parse failures flooding `daemon.err.log`); (c) the cosmetic `daemon-server.ts:106` probe (no Bun-path timeout); (d) recall/search quality validation. Want me to line those up as the next work items while the heal completes?

   fast|killed SIG|git timed out), never a legit non-fast-forward; fail-safe on any state-read error.

2026-07-01: recall.ps1 / `/vault` timed out. First wrong call: "gbrain daemon DOWN." It was
`/health ok:true pid=28140`, `busy:true`, `ingest.running:true` phase `sync:second-brain` --
looked like a normal busy ingest. But it was **wedged**, not working:

**How to tell wedged from busy-working (the discriminators that matter):**
- process CPU delta over 5s = **0.00** (idle, not embedding)
- pglite data dir (`~/.gbrain-trading/brain.pglite`) **last write ~2h old** (no ingest progress)
- `ingest.started_at` unchanged for the whole watch, `finished_at:null`, `last_error:null`
- daemon.err.log has only the connect line -> a **silent no-timeout hang** (likely a Voyage
  embed HTTP call with no timeout). Never conclude "down" OR "healthy-busy" from `/health` alone;
  check CPU + pglite mtime.

**THE WATCHDOG GAP (important):** `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -IfUnhealthy` (the
`JARVIS-BrainDaemon-Watchdog` entry point) checks `/health.ok` + `spawn.ok` only -- NOT
ingest-progress. A daemon wedged mid-ingest answers `ok:true`, so `-IfUnhealthy` says "nothing
to do" and NEVER heals this class. `restart_engine`-style watchdogs that gate on "does /health
answer" are blind to a wedged-but-responsive ingest. **FIX BUILT 2026-07-01 (commit `d1d80cd`
in ~/tools):** `restart-brain-daemon.ps1` now has `Test-IngestWedged` wired into `-IfUnhealthy`
-- wedged = `ingest.running` AND pglite unwritten > `-StallMinutes` (15) AND process CPU idle over
a 5s sample; BOTH required so a slow-but-working ingest is never false-killed, every uncertain path
returns false (fail safe). On wedge it sets `-Force` and heals. ALSO fixed the kill path (part 2 of
the bug below): when the `CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*'` filter finds nothing (empty under
non-elevated watchdog), it now falls back to the authoritative PID from `/health.pid` then
`daemon-lock.json`. New `-DetectOnly` = read-only wedge check. Validated: true-positive against the
real wedge's measured values (pglite 65m stale, CPU 0.016s/6s -> flagged); true-negative via
`-DetectOnly` on the healthy daemon (wedged=False, no false-kill); parse-clean/ASCII. NOTE: a live
wedge (2nd sync, pid 34952) was present during the fix and got healed to fresh pid 31412 around the
06:31 watchdog fire -- can't 100%-attribute the heal to my new code vs a peer restart (no watchdog
stdout log; .vbs runs hidden), but the fix is correct + on the watchdog path (`.vbs` -> `-IfUnhealthy`).

**The fix that worked:**
1. `restart-brain-daemon.ps1 -Force` is the sanctioned path (atomic PGlite rollback => force-kill
   mid-ingest is SAFE, brain stays sound). `-IfUnhealthy` alone will NOT act (sees ok:true).
2. BUT it aborted "port 8077 still held": its kill filter is `bun.exe` WHERE
   `CommandLine -like '*daemon-server.ts*'`, and **CommandLine reads back EMPTY when not
   elevated**, so it matched nothing. Under a non-elevated agent, kill by **PID** instead
   (authoritative PID = `~/.gbrain-trading/daemon-lock.json` .pid == `/health.pid` == the 8077
   owner), then relaunch `~/tools/start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached`.
3. Result: old pid 28140 stopped, port released instantly, new pid 34952 up in 4s, came up
   IDLE (did not auto-re-trigger the wedged sync), `/search` 200 in 2.9s, chunks 5501/embedded
   5493 (99.9%, intact). Recall restored.

Launcher/paths: daemon = `bun.exe` running `daemon-server.ts`, port 8077, data
`~/.gbrain-trading/brain.pglite`, embed voyage-finance-2/1024. Cockpit (zero-DB-touch):
`~/scripts/gbrain/gbrain-status.ps1`. Restart: `~/tools/restart-brain-daemon.ps1`. Launch:
`~/tools/start-brain-daemon.ps1 -Detached`. Periodic sync task: `Jarvis-VaultGbrainSync`.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (commit `f2cb730`, ~/tools): NOT the embed call -- `embedding.ts` ALREADY
has a 60s per-request timeout + finite retries (Amo's 2026-05-07 patch), and the wedge showed
`last_error:null` (a timed-out embed would throw and set last_error). The real hang is in
`sync.ts`'s `git()` helper: the Node fallback set `timeout:30000` but the **Bun.spawnSync path the
daemon actually uses had NO timeout**. `performSync`'s first step is `git pull --ff-only` (network) --
a hung remote / stale `index.lock` / interactive credential prompt blocks `Bun.spawnSync` forever ->
single-writer thread wedged (busy, CPU idle, no PGLite write, last_error:null). Fix: added
`timeout` (`GBRAIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`=30000) + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to the Bun git path so a hung/
prompting git fails fast (killed -> throw -> last_error -> retry next fire). Build clean, sync suite
32 pass/0 fail. **Deploy = daemon restart** (bun runs source directly; no dist) -- gated on Amo.
The watchdog change (`d1d80cd`) remains the backstop that heals a wedge if one still slips through.

`description:` frontmatter values. A JSON-style double-quoted string is a valid YAML scalar and
safely absorbs colons, em-dashes, backticks, `$`, and embedded quotes (escaped as `\"`). Cheap
insurance; the failure is silent (no error reaches the user, the file just disappears from recall).

name/description via `JSON.stringify(value)` (strip trailing `\r`), leaving the body byte-identical,
verifying each re-parses AND body-unchanged before writing. Then re-ingest:

recall hit.

kills this silent-recall-exclusion class regardless of frontmatter quality. Needs a daemon restart to
deploy (bun runs source). [[feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart]]

name: feedback_memory_frontmatter_quoting
description: "Unquoted memory-file frontmatter name/description values that contain a colon-space, em-dash, or a stray quote silently break gray-matter/js-yaml parsing, so gbrain SKIPS the whole file from ingest -- it vanishes from recall with no error surfaced to the user"
metadata:

2026-07-01: a gbrain validation pass (gray-matter over all 439 memory .md files, the SAME parser
`core/markdown.ts` uses) found **12 files (3%) failing frontmatter YAML parse** -- so the ingest
SKIPPED them entirely and they were **absent from recall**. Casualties included load-bearing files:
[[feedback_stop_stopping]], [[feedback_restart_engine_ps1_silent_noop]],
[[project_ci_broken_and_branch_salvage_2026_07_01]], and
[[project_vertex_quota_filed_llm_restored_2026_06_30]] -- i.e. the recall-first workflow could not
surface its own core rules or that day's work.

**Root cause:** unquoted YAML scalars in `name:` / `description:` containing:
- a `: ` colon-space (e.g. `...in scripts: budget cap`, `~17:26 CDT`) -> js-yaml reads a phantom
  nested mapping -> "incomplete explicit mapping pair".
- a leading-then-trailing quote (`name: "Stop stopping" -- don't...`) -> "a multiline key may not be
  an implicit key".
- em-dashes / arrows are fine *inside a quoted scalar* but combine with the above in practice.

**Rule going forward (when WRITING any memory file):** always DOUBLE-QUOTE the `name:` and
`description:` frontmatter values. A JSON-style double-quoted string is a valid YAML scalar and
safely absorbs colons, em-dashes, backticks, `$`, and embedded quotes (escaped as `\"`). Cheap
insurance; the failure is silent (no error reaches the user, the file just disappears from recall).

**How to audit + fix (repeatable):** run gray-matter over the corpus to list failures, then re-quote
name/description via `JSON.stringify(value)` (strip trailing `\r`), leaving the body byte-identical,
verifying each re-parses AND body-unchanged before writing. Then re-ingest:
`POST 127.0.0.1:8077/ingest {"raw_dir":"C:/Users/mattm/.claude/projects/C--Users-mattm/memory","embed":"stale"}`
(FORWARD slashes in JSON -- backslashes get mangled through the shell and the daemon rejects the body).
All 12 fixed + re-ingested 2026-07-01 (pages 1999->2004); both spot-checked files now return as the #1
recall hit.

**Deeper enhancement -- SHIPPED (commit `46b262e`, deployed pid 6628 2026-07-01):** `markdown.ts`
`parseMarkdown` is now RESILIENT -- on a frontmatter parse error it no longer throws/drops the file;
it logs a warning and ingests the body with empty + path-derived metadata (new
`stripLeadingFrontmatterFence` removes only the broken fence so raw YAML doesn't pollute recall).
Chunks come only from body (compiled_truth+timeline), never frontmatter, so nothing embeddable is
lost. This kills the silent-recall-exclusion class regardless of frontmatter quality -- so the
12-file bug CANNOT recur. Same commit added `/health` `stale_minutes` (age of last successful ingest
-- makes a "healthy but every-sync-failing" daemon visible) + a Bun-path timeout on the spawn probe.
Verified: malformed file no longer throws, body survives + recallable; well-formed unaffected;
markdown+sync suites 47 pass/0 fail. Still keep quoting frontmatter (resilience loses the structured
metadata fields even though recall survives). [[feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart]]

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\mattm\.claude\skills\loopify # Loopify — the prompt-to-loop compiler > A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes. > Loopify's job: take a goal Amo states once, and leave behind a **running loop** that pursues it — safely, observably, and killably. **Autonomy: FULL AUTO-DEPLOY** (Amo's standing choice, 2026-06-30). Safe loops register, deploy, and start themselves. The brakes below plus the machine's existing hooks (credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the safety net. Only genuinely destructive / outward-facing steady-state actions stop at a human gate (see §Safety). --- ## The one-screen model ``` GOAL (English) ──▶ [1 CLASSIFY] ──▶ [2 LEDGER] ──▶ [3 RUNNER] ──▶ [4 BRAKES] ──▶ [5 FEEDBACK] ──▶ [6 REGISTER+DEPLOY] ──▶ running loop what shape? what's "done" where runs? how it stops how it learns loopctl + verify + report ``` Every stage is mandatory. Create a todo per stage and work them in order. Do not skip to deploy. --- ## Control plane All loops share one registry and one CLI: **`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1`** → `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`. ```powershell loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id -Goal "" -Archetype -Runner [-RunnerPath

] [-Schedule ] [-StopCondition ] [-BudgetCap ] [-Deploy] loopctl.ps1 -Action Deploy -Id # (re)create the scheduled task for a local-scheduled loop loopctl.ps1 -Action List # fleet board loopctl.ps1 -Action Status [-Id ] # full JSON loopctl.ps1 -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR # runners call this every iteration loopctl.ps1 -Action Remove -Id [-Purge] # -Purge also deletes the scheduled task ``` `-Deploy` on a `local-scheduled` loop creates a `Loopify-` Windows task (shim pwsh, battery-gate cleared, LIMITED, daytime). For every other runner, deploy is done by *you* (the agent) with the right tool, then recorded via `-Action Register`. --- ## Stage 1 — CLASSIFY (what shape is this loop?) Walk the decision tree top-down; first match wins. | If the goal… | Archetype | Canonical runner | |---|---|---| | watches **external state** and acts when it changes (CI, a queue, a price, a file landing) | **dynamic** | in-session `/loop` + `ScheduleWakeup`, OR local-scheduled poller | | drains a **known, finite backlog** (a task list, a set of files) to empty | **backlog-drain** | in-session `/ralph` | | drains a backlog that **regenerates itself** — you must re-discover work each pass | **discovery-drain** | in-session `/jarvis-loop` | | must **push a quality metric to a bar** (score ≥ X, tests green, latency < Y) by generate→judge→improve | **evaluator-optimizer** | in-session loop or Workflow | | fires on a **clock** to read/compute/report (digest, audit, briefing) | **scheduled-cadence** | local-scheduled (fs/tooling) OR cloud routine (Gmail/Cal/pure-cognition) | | is **one big parallelizable pass** with a verify step (review N files, migrate N sites) | **fan-out-verify** | `Workflow` | | **proposes** a change, a second pass **checks** it, then commit | **maker-checker** | in-session loop or Workflow | Write down: `archetype = ` and one sentence why. If two fit, prefer the *simplest runner* that satisfies the stop condition. **Runner picker (hard constraints):** - Touches `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local fs → **local-scheduled** or **in-session**. NEVER a cloud routine (the sandbox can't see the local disk — it fails silently). - Pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar / Drive / web → **cloud routine** (`/schedule` or CCR `create_trigger`). - Needs many agents at once → **Workflow** (fan-out-verify). - Needs to run while no Claude session is open → **local-scheduled** or **cloud** (never in-session). --- ## Stage 2 — LEDGER (what is "done", and where does state live?) A loop without a written ledger is an infinite loop. Define both: 1. **Done predicate** — the exact, checkable condition that ends the loop or a run: - drain: `prd.json` all `passes:true` AND discovery finds 0 new (discovery-drain) / backlog empty (backlog-drain) - evaluator-optimizer: `metric >= threshold` OR `no improvement for K rounds` - scheduled-cadence: never "done" — it's a heartbeat; the run is done when the report is emitted - dynamic: the watched condition resolved (merge landed, queue empty) 2. **State store** — where the loop remembers across iterations: - drain → a `prd.json` / queue file (reuse the ralph/jarvis-loop layout) - evaluator-optimizer → a metrics JSONL (`~/.claude/loops//metrics.jsonl`), one row per round - scheduled-cadence → last-run marker + the report file under `~/.claude/loops//` - dynamic → the external state itself is the store; record last-seen in `~/.claude/loops//state.json` No state store you can point at → you have not finished Stage 2. --- ## Stage 3 — RUNNER (scaffold the execution substrate) Create `~/.claude/loops//` (or, for a repo-scoped loop, `/scripts/loops/`). Put the runner there. - **local-scheduled** → copy `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (next to this SKILL), fill the WORK block. It already wires preflight, heartbeat, fail-closed, notify, and the loopctl heartbeat call. ASCII-only (PS 5.1 will run it). Use `127.0.0.1`, shim paths, battery-safe (loopctl handles the last one at deploy). - **in-session** (`/loop`, `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`) → no script; the runner is the skill. Register the loop so it's on the board, and use `ScheduleWakeup`/the skill's own loop for iteration. - **cloud** → the runner is the routine prompt. Write it as a *complete standalone instruction* (fresh session each fire sees no history). - **workflow** → the runner is the Workflow script (pipeline/parallel + verify stage). - **evaluator-optimizer** (in-session or workflow) → copy `templates/evaluator-optimizer.md` — generate → *independent* judge panel → improve, with stop-at-bar / converge / cap / budget brakes already wired. --- ## Stage 4 — BRAKES (mandatory — no loop deploys without all six) Every deployed loop MUST carry all six. This is what makes it an *engineered* loop, not a runaway. 1. **Preflight gate** — verify dependencies before doing work; abort (no-op, exit 0) if a dep is down. (Don't trade if the engine's down; don't digest if the data source is unreachable.) 2. **Heartbeat** — call `loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR` every iteration. A dead loop stops stamping → the fleet board shows it stale. 3. **Fail-closed** — on any error: stamp RED, notify, exit **non-zero**. Never swallow an error into a green "success". (Anti-pattern: "no error in the log so it worked.") 4. **Stop condition** — the Stage-2 done predicate, checked every iteration. Even cadence loops need a max-runtime guard. 5. **Budget / iteration cap** — a hard ceiling (max iterations, max tokens, max wall-clock). The backstop when the stop condition never trips. 6. **Notification** — on RED / stop / budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` Discord, or Telegram). No-op silently if unset — never throw, never block. For PowerShell runners, brakes 1-3 and 6 come pre-wired in `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. For in-session/cloud/workflow, wire the equivalents (a Workflow gets brakes from `budget.total`, a stop-count loop, and a verify stage). --- ## Stage 5 — FEEDBACK (how the loop learns / self-corrects) Match the archetype: - **discovery-drain** → the discovery phase IS the feedback (re-scan signals each pass). - **evaluator-optimizer** → a judge/verify step scores each attempt; the next attempt reads the score. Use an *independent* judge (separate agent/criteria), not self-grading. - **maker-checker / fan-out-verify** → a second pass adversarially checks the first before commit. Default the checker to skeptical. - **scheduled-cadence** → the report's own deltas vs last run (flag regressions). - **dynamic** → re-read external state each wake; act only on genuine change. A loop with no feedback is a cron job. That's fine *if* the goal is truly stateless cadence — but say so explicitly. --- ## Stage 6 — REGISTER + DEPLOY + OBSERVE 1. **Register** via `loopctl -Action Register …` with the archetype, runner, stop condition, and budget cap filled in. 2. **Deploy** (full auto): - `local-scheduled` → add `-Deploy` (loopctl creates + battery-clears the task). Then **verify it exists**: `schtasks /Query /TN Loopify- /V /FO LIST` shows `Ready` + a plausible Next Run. - `cloud` → create the trigger with CCR `create_trigger` (fresh-session mode for standalone) or `/schedule`, then `Register` (record `task_name`=trigger id). - `in-session` → start the loop now (invoke `/ralph` / `/jarvis-loop` / `/loop`), Register it so it's on the board. - `workflow` → run the `Workflow`; Register a one-shot entry for the audit trail. 3. **Smoke-run once** if safe (a scheduled runner: `Start-ScheduledTask` then read the heartbeat / report). Confirm GREEN. Per verification.md — never claim it runs from the absence of an error; hit the actual heartbeat/report. 4. **Report to Amo** in the format below. ### Report format (always end a /loopify run with this) ``` LOOP COMPILED: goal : archetype : runner: ledger : done = state = brakes : preflight | cap | stop | notify deployed : status= observe : loopctl -Action List (and: ) kill : gated? : ``` --- ## Safety — what full auto-deploy does NOT cover Full auto-deploy means: read-only, report, local-fs-analysis, and in-repo maker-checker loops **deploy and start themselves**. It does **not** authorize a loop whose *steady-state action* is destructive or outward-facing. If the compiled loop would, on its own, repeatedly: - place **live** trades, or flip a paper/live flag - `git push` to a shared branch (main/master/develop/release/*), or force-push - mutate secrets / `.env` / 1Password - delete or mass-move files (always archive, never delete) - restart a prod service (engine, Hermes gateway) unguarded - send messages to **third parties** (email/DM to people who aren't Amo) then **do not auto-deploy it live**. Instead: compile it fully, register it with `status=blocked`, deploy it in **report-only / dry-run** mode (or gate the mutating step behind a flag defaulting OFF), and surface the gate to Amo with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The loop's dangerous step still hits the machine's PreToolUse hooks as a second line of defense — but the design-time gate is yours to hold. Everything else deploys. When in doubt between "useful cadence report" and "outward action", ship the report and let Amo pull the trigger on the action. --- ## Anti-patterns | Anti-pattern | Why it's wrong | Do instead | |---|---|---| | Deploy without a stop condition | infinite loop / runaway spend | Stage 2 done predicate is mandatory | | Green on error (swallow exceptions) | silent failure looks healthy | fail-closed: RED + notify + non-zero exit | | Cloud routine that reads `C:\Users\mattm\` | sandbox can't see local fs — fails silently | local-scheduled for anything local | | Self-grading evaluator loop | grades its own homework, never converges | independent judge / adversarial checker | | Night-time scheduled task (00:00-05:59) | machine asleep → 0xFFFD0000 | schedule 09:00-11:00 (Stage 6) | | One loop per file / per finding | fleet noise | group related work into one loop | | `git add -A` inside a runner | sweeps the 1,450-file backlog | stage per-file, pathspec commit | | Skipping Register | loop invisible + unkillable from the board | always Register, even in-session/workflow | --- ## Dogfood examples (shapes, not prescriptions) - "keep an eye on the self-healing scheduled tasks and ping me if one stays red" → **scheduled-cadence**, local-scheduled, daily 10:00, report-only, notify on red. Safe → auto-deploy. - "get the MES VWAP strategy's paper Sharpe above 0.5" → **evaluator-optimizer**, in-session/Workflow, metric ledger, independent gate-v2 judge, cap 20 rounds. Backtest-only → auto-deploy; any live wiring is Amo-gated. - "review every open PR for the exec-path stack and verify findings" → **fan-out-verify**, Workflow, adversarial verify stage. Read-only → auto-deploy. - "watch for the Vertex quota grant and flip the engine to Vertex-primary" → **dynamic**, poller; but the flip mutates engine config → deploy the *watch* live, **gate the flip** (notify Amo when granted). --- ## Cross-references - Brakes library + heartbeat: `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1` - Loop archetypes in the wild: `/ralph` (backlog), `/jarvis-loop` (discovery), `/loop` (dynamic) - Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `~/.claude/rules/windows-pitfalls.md` - Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `~/.claude/rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling - Verify-before-claiming: `~/.claude/rules/verification.md` - Destructive-op gate: `~/.claude/rules/destructive-op-gates.md` ARGUMENTS: Compile three read-only monitoring loops for JARVIS: (1) engine-health watchdog — poll http://127.0.0.1:8010/health on a cadence, ping JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK when status!=ok OR llm_path_healthy=false OR tradingview_mcp_healthy=false OR ibkr disconnected; (2) LLM burn monitor — read engine/data/llm_costs.db daily, ping if trailing-24h spend crosses a threshold; (3) PR-staleness sweep — list open PRs in mattamundson/jarvis-trader, ping-only digest of PRs open past N days. All local scheduled tasks, 09:00–11:00 window, ASCII-only PS runners, six brakes each.
