---
name: "project_gbrain_bookmark_enhancements_2026_07_01"
description: "Mining the last ~100 X bookmarks for gbrain-strengthening ideas surfaced 6 themes converging on Karpathy's LLM-Wiki 'value is in the edges not the nodes'; theme A (semantic auto-linking of ~61% orphan pages) shipped this session as a /auto-link daemon endpoint + the gbrain-recall-health loop gained stale_minutes alerting; themes B-F queued as ranked follow-ups"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b2ebcf3b-f06c-4765-b2ab-6fa1767d0291
---

2026-07-01: Amo asked to "search throughout the last 100 bookmarks to identify anything that can make
gbrain stronger." Mined the LOCAL harvested store (`master-jarvis/second-brain/raw/x-bookmarks/2026-W2[567].jsonl`
-- the live X API re-fetch was down: OAuth2 user token expired, needs `setup_oauth2`). 35 of the recent
bookmarks are gbrain-relevant. They converge hard on one idea and fan out into six themes.

**The dominant signal (and why it matched an earlier finding):** Karpathy's LLM-Wiki field note --
*"The value of the system is in the edges, not the nodes"* (@0xObssnnn, @MyWestLord, @polydao), and the
OMEGA build (@thelichhh: *"378 notes, 1816 edges, almost 5 links each. Nothing sits alone"*) plus
@humzaakhalid *"revived 5,000 dead notes with Claude in 20 mins."* This lines up with a validation finding
from earlier the same day: **gbrain is ~61% orphan pages** -- semantically recallable but with zero graph
edges, so `graph_recall` / `traverseGraph` (which walk the `links` table) can't traverse from them.

## The 6 themes (ranked)

- **A -- link-graph / edges>nodes  [SHIPPED this session]** -> semantic auto-linker (see below).
- **B -- episodic memory layer** (@0xCodez ex-Google "procedural + semantic + episodic"; @tom_doerr
  "dynamic memory with perception + forgetting cycles"). gbrain's `timeline_entry_count = 0` -- the
  dated-event/episodic third layer is entirely unused. Candidate: log session/decision events into the
  `timeline` half of pages (gbrain already splits compiled_truth vs timeline; the plumbing exists via
  `addTimelineEntry`). HIGH value, medium effort.
- **C -- self-maintenance loop  [SHIPPED 2026-07-01]** (@cyrilXBT "9 things my vault does while I sleep").
  `/loopify`'d `gbrain-maintenance` (Loopify-gbrain-maintenance, DAILY@10:30 -- daytime, machine asleep at
  night; battery-gate cleared; six brakes). Each run: preflight `/health` (skip if down/mid-ingest) ->
  POST `/auto-link` apply -> poll async to completion (600s cap) -> report (corpus/orphans/edges/stale +
  delta vs last run) -> GREEN/RED heartbeat + notify-on-RED. DB-only + reversible so it auto-deployed under
  the loopify envelope. Smoke-run GREEN: 0 new edges / 966 orphans (correct -- the one-shot already linked
  all >=0.78; proves idempotent incremental behaviour). v1 re-scans the 966 sub-threshold orphans each run
  (~2min daemon-busy); a since-last-run/skip-unlinkable filter is the next optimization. Future: fold in a
  duplicate/stub pruner + forgotten-note resurfacer.
- **D -- RAG quality / eval harness** (@ConsciousRide "chunking strategies, embeddings, reranking";
  @tom_doerr "hands-on notebooks for LLM and RAG evaluation"). Candidate: a golden-query set ->
  measure recall hit-rate, to regression-guard recall quality across re-embeds. Guards against silent
  recall decay. Medium value, medium effort.
- **E -- context engineering** (@ArchiveExplorer "builders moved on from prompts to context engineering";
  @sairahul1 Anthropic context-engineering template). Candidate: tighten what the auto-recall hook
  (`inject_knowledge.py`) injects -- it already gates at score>=0.55, top-3; revisit budget + dedup.
  Low effort, incremental.
- **F -- reference implementations to study** (Graphify @undefinedKi "one command turns any folder into a
  Claude Code second brain"; myKG @adnan_hashmi; Cabinet @HilaShmuel Obsidian+agents; @tom_doerr
  MCP-for-Obsidian). Comparison notes only -- gbrain already has the daemon+PGlite+voyage-finance
  embeddings these are reaching for. Lowest priority.

## Theme A -- what shipped (semantic auto-linker)

New daemon endpoint `POST /auto-link` in `C:\Users\mattm\tools\gbrain-src\src\daemon-server.ts`
(functions `runAutoLink` + `pickEmbedding`). For each **orphan** page (no outgoing links), take its
representative chunk embedding (prefers a compiled_truth chunk) and run the daemon's OWN
`searchVector` (cosine `<=>`), then `addLink(orphan, target, "auto:semantic score=<s>", "semantic")`
for the top K=5 distinct targets scoring >= 0.78. Reuses `listPages` / `getLinks` / `getChunks` /
`getEmbeddingsByChunkIds` / `searchVector` / `addLink` -- **no new similarity code**.

- **DB-only + reversible:** writes ONLY the `links` table with `link_type='semantic'` (never touches
  vault `.md` files). Entire pass reverses with `DELETE FROM links WHERE link_type='semantic'`.
  `addLink` is `ON CONFLICT (from,to) DO UPDATE` so re-runs are idempotent.
- **Runs server-side** because `searchVector` takes a `Float32Array` (daemon-owned; not
  JSON-round-trippable over `/rpc`). Each engine call self-serializes via the daemon proxy, so `/search`
  interleaves -- it does NOT hold the single writer for the whole pass.
- **Safe by default:** `dry_run` defaults TRUE; refuses while an ingest/sync holds the writer (409).
- **Async single-flight + event-loop yield (hardening found during rollout):** a synchronous full-corpus
  run FROZE the daemon within ~12s and the watchdog reaped it. Root cause: `searchVector` is a full-scan
  cosine over every chunk embedding in single-threaded WASM PGlite; `/search` does one per request, but this
  pass does one per orphan (hundreds-to-thousands) back-to-back, monopolizing the one JS thread so even
  in-memory `/health` can't answer -> watchdog force-kills. Fixed two ways: (1) run it single-flight through
  the same `ingest` busy-state as `/ingest`+`/sync` (POST returns 202, poll `GET /auto-link`), so `/health`
  fast-paths; (2) `await`-yield the event loop between orphans so liveness probes interleave. With both, a
  full pass stays reachable the whole time.
- **RESULT (applied 2026-07-01, daemon pid 4180):** corpus `totalPages=2007`, orphan rate ~66% (1375).
  Two passes applied **692 semantic edges across 409 pages** (batch: 92 edges/55 pages; full: 600 edges/354
  pages). Edges are high-precision (0.82-0.96): ERP/OneNote pages cluster to true siblings
  (`paradigm-erp-order-lifecycle -> creating-an-order-in-paradigm` 0.964). ~966 orphans remain with NO
  neighbor >= 0.78 (genuinely isolated at that bar; a lower-threshold pass would link more at lower precision).
  VERIFIED: `getLinks`/`traverseGraph`/`getBacklinks` all now walk formerly-orphan pages (e.g.
  `best-version-with-all-calculations -> hover-roofing-report`; `paradigm-procurement` has 4 semantic
  backlinks) -> gbrain `graph_recall` can traverse them. Fixed a `listPages` default `LIMIT 100` (was capping
  the sweep to 100 pages) -> `listPages({ limit: 1_000_000 })`. Reverse with `DELETE FROM links WHERE
  link_type='semantic'` (692 rows). Daemon-server.ts changes are LIVE (deployed via restart) but UNCOMMITTED.

**Deferred (documented, NOT built):** (1) writing a `## Related [[wikilink]]` block back into vault `.md`
for Obsidian graph visibility -- that's a mass file-edit, gate + archive-before-edit; (2) wiring the pass
into a nightly `/loopify` loop (theme C) once the one-shot edge-growth curve is seen.

## Also shipped: stale_minutes alerting (the earlier ask)

`gbrain-recall-health` loop (`run.ps1`) now reads `/health` `ingest.stale_minutes` (added 46b262e) and
throws RED when it exceeds `$StaleMinutesThreshold` (default 120 -- vault sync is hourly so a healthy
value sawtooths 0->~60; 120 = ~2 missed syncs = a real "up but every-sync-failing" wedge). Fail-closed
routes through the existing Send-LoopNote + Register-LoopResult path. Defensive null-guard: absent/null
stale_minutes (fresh daemon, pre-first-success) is skipped -> no false RED.

## Connectivity mesh (the "all connected" ask) -- 3/4 live

- Claude Code <-> gbrain: OK (native MCP `node Code/gbrain-mcp/index.mjs` -> 127.0.0.1:8077; recall verified).
- Claude Code <-> Obsidian: OK (MCP `obsidian-mcp-wrapper.ps1`, vault `master-jarvis\second-brain`).
- gbrain <-> Obsidian: OK (gbrain ingests the SAME `master-jarvis\second-brain` dir; hourly Jarvis-VaultGbrainSync).
- Hermes <-> gbrain: GATED -- `~/.hermes/config.yaml` has the staged `gbrain` entry (launcher
  `gbrain-wsl-launch.sh`, endpoint via portproxy 172.28.96.1:8077, GBRAIN_DISABLE_GRAPH=1 GBRAIN_READONLY=1).
  Loads only on a gateway restart, which is peer-gated + forbidden from a debug flow. Amo runs
  `bash /root/.hermes/bin/hermes-safe-restart.sh` (NO --force) when peers <=1, then `hermes mcp list | grep gbrain`.

## Operational note discovered this session

The BrainDaemon watchdog took ~20 min to heal a mid-sync wedge (pid 38740, idle CPU + no pglite progress),
because the busy fast-path `/health` answers `ok:true busy:true` from in-memory state and `-IfUnhealthy`
can't distinguish wedged-busy from progressing-busy. It DID eventually restart (pid 44192 at ~5:16). The
new stale_minutes alert + the recall-health loop's own /search-timeout brake both catch this class faster
than the watchdog. [[feedback_gbrain_ingest_wedge_restart]] [[project_gbrain_recall_health_loop_2026_07_01]]

<#
  Loopify runner: gbrain-maintenance  -- ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
  Daily self-maintenance for the gbrain brain: incrementally attach semantic edges to orphan
  pages so the graph stays navigable (graph_recall/traverseGraph can walk from new pages).

  Archetype: scheduled-cadence. LOCAL only. Writes ONLY semantic edges into the pglite links
  table (link_type='semantic') -- DB-only, reversible (DELETE ... WHERE link_type='semantic'),
  idempotent (addLink ON CONFLICT). Never touches vault .md files, never restarts the daemon.

  All six brakes: preflight (daemon up + not mid-ingest), heartbeat, fail-closed, runtime cap,
  single-run budget, notify-on-RED. Notifies only on RED/transition, not steady GREEN.

  v1 LIMITATION: a full pass re-scans every orphan (incl. the ~966 with no neighbour >= threshold),
  a few minutes of daemon-busy in the maintenance window. A since-last-run / skip-unlinkable filter
  is a future enhancement.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'gbrain-maintenance',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 600,          # brake 4/5: hard wall-clock cap for one fire
    [double] $Threshold = 0.78,             # min cosine to attach a semantic edge
    [int]    $K = 5                          # max edges per orphan
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl  = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'
$FailBudget = 3
$Endpoint = 'http://127.0.0.1:8077'
# loop-heal.ps1 has its own param() block; dot-sourcing re-runs it and clobbers $Id. Save + restore.
$__Id = $Id
if (Test-Path $loopHeal) { . $loopHeal }
$Id = $__Id
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

$LoopDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops\gbrain-maintenance'
if (-not (Test-Path $LoopDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $LoopDir -Force | Out-Null }

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

function Test-Preflight {
    # Brake 1: daemon reachable, healthy, and NOT mid-ingest (auto-link 409s during a sync).
    try {
        $h = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/health" -Method Get -TimeoutSec 8
        if (-not $h.ok) { $script:PreWhy = 'daemon /health not ok'; return $false }
        if ($h.ingest -and $h.ingest.running) { $script:PreWhy = "ingest/sync running (phase=$($h.ingest.phase))"; return $false }
        return $true
    } catch { $script:PreWhy = "daemon unreachable: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return $false }
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Preflight)) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN     # dep down / busy is not an error; abort clean
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: $script:PreWhy -- skipping this fire (no-op)."
        exit 0
    }

    # ================= WORK: incremental semantic auto-link =================
    $prevFile = Join-Path $LoopDir 'last-result.json'
    $prev = $null
    if (Test-Path $prevFile) { try { $prev = Get-Content $prevFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json } catch {} }

    $headers = @{ 'Content-Type' = 'application/json' }
    $reqBody = @{ dry_run = $false; threshold = $Threshold; k = $K } | ConvertTo-Json
    $post = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/auto-link" -Method Post -Headers $headers -Body $reqBody -TimeoutSec 15
    if (-not $post.accepted) { throw "auto-link not accepted: $($post.error)" }

    # Poll async completion, bounded by the runtime cap (the daemon stays alive via its event-loop yield).
    $st = $null
    do {
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
        if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded while polling auto-link" }
        $st = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/auto-link" -Method Get -TimeoutSec 10
    } while ($st.running)
    if ($st.last_error) { throw "auto-link reported error: $($st.last_error)" }
    $last = $st.last
    if (-not $last) { throw "auto-link completed but returned no result summary" }

    # Freshness (Task-1 metric) for the report.
    $stale = $null
    try { $h2 = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/health" -Method Get -TimeoutSec 8; if ($h2.ingest) { $stale = $h2.ingest.stale_minutes } } catch {}

    # Feedback: delta vs previous run.
    $dEdges = ''; $dOrph = ''
    if ($prev) {
        if ($null -ne $prev.edgesApplied) { $dEdges = " (prev $($prev.edgesApplied))" }
        if ($null -ne $prev.orphans)      { $dOrph  = " (prev $($prev.orphans))" }
    }

    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ')
    $rep = @()
    $rep += "# gbrain-maintenance run $stamp"
    $rep += ""
    $rep += "corpus_pages : $($last.totalPages)"
    $rep += "orphans      : $($last.orphans)$dOrph"
    $rep += "pages_linked : $($last.pagesLinked)"
    $rep += "edges_applied: $($last.edgesApplied)$dEdges"
    $rep += "embed_missing: $($last.orphansEmbedMissing)"
    $rep += "stale_minutes: $stale"
    $rep += "params       : threshold=$($last.threshold) k=$($last.k)"
    $rep -join "`n" | Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $LoopDir 'report-latest.md') -Encoding UTF8
    $last | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content -Path $prevFile -Encoding UTF8
    # =========================================================

    & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN
    if (Get-Command Register-LoopResult -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State GREEN | Out-Null }
    Write-Output "GREEN: gbrain-maintenance edges_applied=$($last.edgesApplied) orphans=$($last.orphans)/$($last.totalPages) stale_min=$stale"
    exit 0
}
catch {
    $msg = $_.Exception.Message
    try { & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State RED } catch { }
    $note = "RED: $msg"
    if (Get-Command Register-LoopResult -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $d = Register-LoopResult -Id $Id -State RED -Fault 'gbrain-maintenance' -Budget $FailBudget
        if ($d -and $d.escalate) { $note = "ESCALATE ($($d.consecutive_fails)/$FailBudget consecutive REDs): $msg" }
    }
    Send-LoopNote $note
    Write-Error "LOOP FAILED: $msg"
    exit 1
}

# Plan: gbrain stale-alerting + semantic auto-linking + full connectivity mesh

## Context

Three asks from Amo, in one thread:

1. **Wire `stale_minutes` alerting into the existing `gbrain-recall-health` loop.** Commit `46b262e` already
   added `/health` → `ingest.stale_minutes` / `last_success_at` (age of the last *successful* ingest). The
   loop reads `ok`/`busy`/`running`/`pid` but **not** these two fields — so a daemon that is up-and-answering
   yet **silently failing every sync** (the exact 2026-07-01 wedge class) still stamps GREEN. Close that gap.

2. **Strengthen gbrain from the X bookmarks.** Mining the local harvested store (35 gbrain-relevant recent
   bookmarks → 6 themes) surfaced one dominant, actionable signal that also matches an earlier validation
   finding: **"the value is in the edges, not the nodes"** (Karpathy LLM-Wiki; OMEGA "378 notes, 1816 edges,
   ~5 links each, nothing sits alone"; "revived 5,000 dead notes with Claude"). gbrain is **~61% orphan pages**
   (semantically recallable, but zero graph edges → `graph_recall` and the MCP `graph_recall` tool can't
   traverse from them). Amo scoped this to the **top pick: build the auto-linking / orphan-revival pass**;
   themes B–F are documented as a proposal, not built.

3. **Ensure gbrain, Obsidian, Hermes, and Claude Code are all connected.** 3 of 4 links are already live; the
   Hermes↔gbrain link is staged but needs a peer-gated gateway restart — which Amo will run himself (his
   "document as your step" choice).

**Intended outcome:** the health loop catches a sync-wedge the hour it starts; gbrain's orphan pages get
driven toward ~5 semantic edges each using gbrain's *own* vector engine (reversible, DB-only); the 4-way
mesh is verified and the one gated step is handed to Amo as a copy-paste command.

---

## Task 1 — `stale_minutes` alerting in the health loop

**File:** `C:\Users\mattm\.claude\loops\gbrain-recall-health\run.ps1` (ASCII-only; PS 5.1 runs it).

The loop already wires `Send-LoopNote`, transition-based alerting (`last-state.txt`), and
`Register-LoopResult` (FailBudget=3). Only two additions:

1. **Add a param** near the top param block:
   ```powershell
   [int] $StaleMinutesThreshold = 120
   ```
   Rationale for **120, not 30**: vault sync is hourly, so a *healthy* `stale_minutes` sawtooths 0→~60
   between syncs. 30 would false-alarm every cycle; 120 fires only after ~2 consecutive missed syncs =
   a real wedge. (Threshold is a param so Amo can tune via registry `runner_args` without editing code.)

2. **After the `/health` parse block (~line 152, right after the HEALTH report line, before the `/search`
   test)**, read the new fields defensively (they are `null` until the first successful ingest, and absent
   on an older daemon build) and fail-closed if stale:
   ```powershell
   $staleMin = $null; $lastSuccessAt = $null
   if ($health -and $health.ingest) {
     if ($health.ingest.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'stale_minutes')   { $staleMin = $health.ingest.stale_minutes }
     if ($health.ingest.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'last_success_at')  { $lastSuccessAt = $health.ingest.last_success_at }
   }
   if ($null -ne $staleMin -and $staleMin -gt $StaleMinutesThreshold) {
     $report.Add("INGEST-STALE: stale_minutes=$staleMin last_success=$lastSuccessAt (threshold=$StaleMinutesThreshold)")
     throw "gbrain ingest stalled: $staleMin min since last successful sync (> $StaleMinutesThreshold)"
   }
   ```
   The `throw` routes through the loop's existing fail-closed path → RED heartbeat + `Send-LoopNote` +
   `Register-LoopResult` (escalation budget) + non-zero exit. No new notification plumbing.

3. **(Optional) registry:** if Amo wants a non-default threshold, set it in
   `C:\Users\mattm\.claude\loops\registry.json` → `gbrain-recall-health.runner_args`
   (e.g. `-StaleMinutesThreshold 90`) and `loopctl -Action Deploy -Id gbrain-recall-health` to re-emit the
   task. Default 120 needs no registry change.

**Reuses:** `Send-LoopNote`, transition alerting, `Register-LoopResult`, `$report` — all already in the file.
**No** new daemon work (the `/health` fields already ship in `46b262e`, deployed pid 6628).

---

## Task 2 — Build the semantic auto-linking / orphan-revival pass

### Design (reuses gbrain's own vector engine — no new similarity code)

Building blocks that already exist in `C:\Users\mattm\tools\gbrain-src\src\core\pglite-engine.ts`:
- `searchVector(embedding, opts)` — cosine nearest-neighbour over chunk embeddings (`embedding <=> $1::vector`,
  score = `1 - distance`). **This is the auto-linker's candidate finder** — no new ANN code.
- `addLink(from, to, context?, linkType?)` — inserts into the `links` table (`from_page_id`, `to_page_id`,
  `link_type DEFAULT ''`, `context`). Indexes `idx_links_from` / `idx_links_to` already exist.
- `getLinks(slug)` / `getBacklinks(slug)` — to detect orphans and skip existing edges.

**The pass** (new command `src/commands/auto-link.ts`, following the `backlinks.ts` / `extract.ts` pattern,
+ a daemon `/rpc` method `auto-link` so it can run without the CLI):

1. Enumerate **orphan pages** = pages with `getLinks(slug).length === 0` (no *outgoing* edges).
2. For each orphan: take its representative chunk embedding (already stored — no re-embed), call
   `searchVector(embedding, { limit: K+guard })`.
3. Keep the top **K = 5** distinct target pages where `score >= 0.78` (param), excluding self and any edge
   already present. Call `addLink(orphan, target, "auto:semantic score=<s>", "semantic")`.
4. **`link_type = 'semantic'`** — distinct from the `''` wikilink edges the existing backfill produces. This
   is the reversibility guarantee: the entire pass is undone with `DELETE FROM links WHERE link_type='semantic'`.
5. **Idempotent:** skip a `(from,to)` that already exists (check `getLinks` set); re-running only fills gaps.

**Safety / scope boundaries (why this is safe to build now):**
- **DB-only.** Writes edges into `brain.pglite`; it does **not** mutate any vault `.md` file. Fully reversible
  (`DELETE ... WHERE link_type='semantic'`), so no archive-never-delete concern and no mass file-edit.
- Powers gbrain `graph_recall` + the native MCP `graph_recall` tool immediately (they read the `links` table).
- **Dry-run first:** the command takes `--dry-run` (default) → prints candidate edges + a
  per-page/-corpus histogram (orphans before, avg edges/page after) and writes nothing. Only `--apply`
  mutates the DB. I run dry-run, eyeball the edges for quality, then `--apply`.

**Deferred to a documented follow-up (NOT built here), because each is a heavier/mutating step:**
- Writing a `## Related` `[[wikilink]]` block back into vault `.md` files for **Obsidian graph visibility**
  (this is a mass file-edit → gate it, archive-before-edit, run behind a flag).
- Wiring the pass into a **nightly maintenance loop** via `/loopify` (theme C). Auto-linking on a cadence is
  DB-only + reversible so it *could* auto-deploy, but I'll ship the one-shot first and register the loop as a
  separate, explicit step so Amo sees the edge-growth curve before it runs unattended.

### Proposal doc for themes B–F (documented, not built)

Write `C:\Users\mattm\.claude\projects\C--Users-mattm\memory\project_gbrain_bookmark_enhancements_2026_07_01.md`
(frontmatter `name`/`description` **double-quoted** per `feedback_memory_frontmatter_quoting`) capturing the
35-bookmark mining and the 6 themes, with A marked SHIPPED and B–F as ranked candidates:
- **A — link-graph / edges>nodes** → *shipped this plan* (semantic auto-linker).
- **B — episodic memory layer** — gbrain `timeline_entry_count = 0`; the procedural/semantic/**episodic**
  taxonomy (@0xCodez, @tom_doerr "perception + forgetting cycles") says dated-event capture is the missing
  third layer. Candidate: log session/decision events into the `timeline` half of pages.
- **C — nightly self-maintenance** (@cyrilXBT "9 things my vault does while I sleep": auto-tag, surface
  forgotten notes via backlinks, flag duplicate notes, weekly review) → a `/loopify` scheduled-cadence loop.
- **D — RAG quality / eval** (@ConsciousRide chunking+reranking, @tom_doerr LLM/RAG eval notebooks) → a small
  recall-eval harness (golden query set → measure hit-rate) to regression-guard recall quality.
- **E — context engineering** (@ArchiveExplorer, @sairahul1 Anthropic template) → tighten what the auto-recall
  hook injects (already score≥0.55, top-3).
- **F — reference implementations** (Graphify, myKG, Cabinet, MCP-for-Obsidian) → comparison notes only.

**Reuses:** `searchVector`, `addLink`, `getLinks`, `getBacklinks`, the `links` schema, the `backlinks.ts`
command scaffold + the daemon `/rpc` dispatcher — all existing.

---

## Task 3 — Verify the 4-way connectivity mesh

**Verify (read-only) the 3 live links:**
- **Claude Code ↔ gbrain:** `claude mcp list` shows `gbrain` ✔ Connected (native MCP at
  `~/Code/gbrain-mcp/index.mjs`); auto-recall hook `inject_knowledge.py` now reads `prompt` (fixed);
  `Jarvis-GbrainKeepWarm` task Ready.
- **Claude Code ↔ Obsidian:** `claude mcp list` shows `obsidian` ✔ Connected.
- **gbrain ↔ Obsidian:** the vault dir is gbrain's ingest `raw_dir` (hourly sync); confirm `/health`
  `stale_minutes` is small (proves the sync path is live).

**Document (do NOT execute) the one gated link — Hermes ↔ gbrain:**
`~/.hermes/config.yaml` already has the staged `gbrain` entry (launcher `gbrain-wsl-launch.sh`,
`GBRAIN_ENDPOINT` via portproxy `172.28.96.1:8077`, `GBRAIN_DISABLE_GRAPH=1`, `GBRAIN_READONLY=1`). It loads
only on a gateway restart, which is **peer-gated and forbidden from a debug flow**. Per Amo's choice, the plan
**hands him the exact command** to run when peers ≤ 1 (via the safe-restart helper, never `--force`, never a
raw restart):
```
PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP: Hermes gateway restart to load the staged gbrain MCP entry.
Amo runs this himself when session_manifest shows peers <= 1:
  bash /root/.hermes/bin/hermes-safe-restart.sh      # NO --force; coordinated, drains DMs safely
Then verify inside WSL: hermes mcp list | grep gbrain   (expect: gbrain connected, read-only)
```

---

## Verification

- **Task 1:** run `Loopify-gbrain-recall-health` once (`Start-ScheduledTask`), read the heartbeat + report —
  GREEN on a healthy daemon. Then simulate stale by invoking `run.ps1 -StaleMinutesThreshold 0` → confirm it

  After `--apply`: re-query orphan count (expect a large drop) and `graph_recall` from a

  reverses in a scratch copy. Run gbrain's markdown+sync test suites (expect 47 pass / 0 fail, unchanged).
- **Task 3:** `claude mcp list` → gbrain + obsidian ✔ Connected; `/health` `stale_minutes` small; the Hermes
  step remains a documented Amo-run command (unexecuted).

## Files

- **Edit:** `C:\Users\mattm\.claude\loops\gbrain-recall-health\run.ps1` (param + stale check)
- **New:** `C:\Users\mattm\tools\gbrain-src\src\commands\auto-link.ts` + `/rpc` `auto-link` method in
  `daemon-server.ts` (reuses `searchVector`/`addLink`/`getLinks`)

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\mattm\.claude\skills\loopify # Loopify — the prompt-to-loop compiler > A prompt is a single turn. A loop is a prompt plus a memory, a stop condition, and a set of brakes. > Loopify's job: take a goal Amo states once, and leave behind a **running loop** that pursues it — safely, observably, and killably. **Autonomy: FULL AUTO-DEPLOY** (Amo's standing choice, 2026-06-30). Safe loops register, deploy, and start themselves. The brakes below plus the machine's existing hooks (credential-guard, destructive-op-gate, shared-resource-guard) are the safety net. Only genuinely destructive / outward-facing steady-state actions stop at a human gate (see §Safety). --- ## The one-screen model ``` GOAL (English) ──▶ [1 CLASSIFY] ──▶ [2 LEDGER] ──▶ [3 RUNNER] ──▶ [4 BRAKES] ──▶ [5 FEEDBACK] ──▶ [6 REGISTER+DEPLOY] ──▶ running loop what shape? what's "done" where runs? how it stops how it learns loopctl + verify + report ``` Every stage is mandatory. Create a todo per stage and work them in order. Do not skip to deploy. --- ## Control plane All loops share one registry and one CLI: **`C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1`** → `~/.claude/loops/registry.json`. ```powershell loopctl.ps1 -Action Register -Id -Goal "" -Archetype -Runner [-RunnerPath

] [-Schedule ] [-StopCondition ] [-BudgetCap ] [-Deploy] loopctl.ps1 -Action Deploy -Id # (re)create the scheduled task for a local-scheduled loop loopctl.ps1 -Action List # fleet board loopctl.ps1 -Action Status [-Id ] # full JSON loopctl.ps1 -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR # runners call this every iteration loopctl.ps1 -Action Remove -Id [-Purge] # -Purge also deletes the scheduled task ``` `-Deploy` on a `local-scheduled` loop creates a `Loopify-` Windows task (shim pwsh, battery-gate cleared, LIMITED, daytime). For every other runner, deploy is done by *you* (the agent) with the right tool, then recorded via `-Action Register`. --- ## Stage 1 — CLASSIFY (what shape is this loop?) Walk the decision tree top-down; first match wins. | If the goal… | Archetype | Canonical runner | |---|---|---| | watches **external state** and acts when it changes (CI, a queue, a price, a file landing) | **dynamic** | in-session `/loop` + `ScheduleWakeup`, OR local-scheduled poller | | drains a **known, finite backlog** (a task list, a set of files) to empty | **backlog-drain** | in-session `/ralph` | | drains a backlog that **regenerates itself** — you must re-discover work each pass | **discovery-drain** | in-session `/jarvis-loop` | | must **push a quality metric to a bar** (score ≥ X, tests green, latency < Y) by generate→judge→improve | **evaluator-optimizer** | in-session loop or Workflow | | fires on a **clock** to read/compute/report (digest, audit, briefing) | **scheduled-cadence** | local-scheduled (fs/tooling) OR cloud routine (Gmail/Cal/pure-cognition) | | is **one big parallelizable pass** with a verify step (review N files, migrate N sites) | **fan-out-verify** | `Workflow` | | **proposes** a change, a second pass **checks** it, then commit | **maker-checker** | in-session loop or Workflow | Write down: `archetype = ` and one sentence why. If two fit, prefer the *simplest runner* that satisfies the stop condition. **Runner picker (hard constraints):** - Touches `C:\Users\mattm\`, installed tooling, IB, pm2, the engine, or any local fs → **local-scheduled** or **in-session**. NEVER a cloud routine (the sandbox can't see the local disk — it fails silently). - Pure cognition over Gmail / Calendar / Drive / web → **cloud routine** (`/schedule` or CCR `create_trigger`). - Needs many agents at once → **Workflow** (fan-out-verify). - Needs to run while no Claude session is open → **local-scheduled** or **cloud** (never in-session). --- ## Stage 2 — LEDGER (what is "done", and where does state live?) A loop without a written ledger is an infinite loop. Define both: 1. **Done predicate** — the exact, checkable condition that ends the loop or a run: - drain: `prd.json` all `passes:true` AND discovery finds 0 new (discovery-drain) / backlog empty (backlog-drain) - evaluator-optimizer: `metric >= threshold` OR `no improvement for K rounds` - scheduled-cadence: never "done" — it's a heartbeat; the run is done when the report is emitted - dynamic: the watched condition resolved (merge landed, queue empty) 2. **State store** — where the loop remembers across iterations: - drain → a `prd.json` / queue file (reuse the ralph/jarvis-loop layout) - evaluator-optimizer → a metrics JSONL (`~/.claude/loops//metrics.jsonl`), one row per round - scheduled-cadence → last-run marker + the report file under `~/.claude/loops//` - dynamic → the external state itself is the store; record last-seen in `~/.claude/loops//state.json` No state store you can point at → you have not finished Stage 2. --- ## Stage 3 — RUNNER (scaffold the execution substrate) Create `~/.claude/loops//` (or, for a repo-scoped loop, `/scripts/loops/`). Put the runner there. - **local-scheduled** → copy `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` (next to this SKILL), fill the WORK block. It already wires preflight, heartbeat, fail-closed, notify, and the loopctl heartbeat call. ASCII-only (PS 5.1 will run it). Use `127.0.0.1`, shim paths, battery-safe (loopctl handles the last one at deploy). - **in-session** (`/loop`, `/ralph`, `/jarvis-loop`) → no script; the runner is the skill. Register the loop so it's on the board, and use `ScheduleWakeup`/the skill's own loop for iteration. - **cloud** → the runner is the routine prompt. Write it as a *complete standalone instruction* (fresh session each fire sees no history). - **workflow** → the runner is the Workflow script (pipeline/parallel + verify stage). - **evaluator-optimizer** (in-session or workflow) → copy `templates/evaluator-optimizer.md` — generate → *independent* judge panel → improve, with stop-at-bar / converge / cap / budget brakes already wired. --- ## Stage 4 — BRAKES (mandatory — no loop deploys without all six) Every deployed loop MUST carry all six. This is what makes it an *engineered* loop, not a runaway. 1. **Preflight gate** — verify dependencies before doing work; abort (no-op, exit 0) if a dep is down. (Don't trade if the engine's down; don't digest if the data source is unreachable.) 2. **Heartbeat** — call `loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id -State GREEN|RED|ERROR` every iteration. A dead loop stops stamping → the fleet board shows it stale. 3. **Fail-closed** — on any error: stamp RED, notify, exit **non-zero**. Never swallow an error into a green "success". (Anti-pattern: "no error in the log so it worked.") 4. **Stop condition** — the Stage-2 done predicate, checked every iteration. Even cadence loops need a max-runtime guard. 5. **Budget / iteration cap** — a hard ceiling (max iterations, max tokens, max wall-clock). The backstop when the stop condition never trips. 6. **Notification** — on RED / stop / budget-exhaustion, tell Amo (`JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK` Discord, or Telegram). No-op silently if unset — never throw, never block. For PowerShell runners, brakes 1-3 and 6 come pre-wired in `templates/scheduled-runner.ps1` and `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1`. For in-session/cloud/workflow, wire the equivalents (a Workflow gets brakes from `budget.total`, a stop-count loop, and a verify stage). --- ## Stage 5 — FEEDBACK (how the loop learns / self-corrects) Match the archetype: - **discovery-drain** → the discovery phase IS the feedback (re-scan signals each pass). - **evaluator-optimizer** → a judge/verify step scores each attempt; the next attempt reads the score. Use an *independent* judge (separate agent/criteria), not self-grading. - **maker-checker / fan-out-verify** → a second pass adversarially checks the first before commit. Default the checker to skeptical. - **scheduled-cadence** → the report's own deltas vs last run (flag regressions). - **dynamic** → re-read external state each wake; act only on genuine change. A loop with no feedback is a cron job. That's fine *if* the goal is truly stateless cadence — but say so explicitly. --- ## Stage 6 — REGISTER + DEPLOY + OBSERVE 1. **Register** via `loopctl -Action Register …` with the archetype, runner, stop condition, and budget cap filled in. 2. **Deploy** (full auto): - `local-scheduled` → add `-Deploy` (loopctl creates + battery-clears the task). Then **verify it exists**: `schtasks /Query /TN Loopify- /V /FO LIST` shows `Ready` + a plausible Next Run. - `cloud` → create the trigger with CCR `create_trigger` (fresh-session mode for standalone) or `/schedule`, then `Register` (record `task_name`=trigger id). - `in-session` → start the loop now (invoke `/ralph` / `/jarvis-loop` / `/loop`), Register it so it's on the board. - `workflow` → run the `Workflow`; Register a one-shot entry for the audit trail. 3. **Smoke-run once** if safe (a scheduled runner: `Start-ScheduledTask` then read the heartbeat / report). Confirm GREEN. Per verification.md — never claim it runs from the absence of an error; hit the actual heartbeat/report. 4. **Report to Amo** in the format below. ### Report format (always end a /loopify run with this) ``` LOOP COMPILED: goal : archetype : runner: ledger : done = state = brakes : preflight | cap | stop | notify deployed : status= observe : loopctl -Action List (and: ) kill : gated? : ``` --- ## Safety — what full auto-deploy does NOT cover Full auto-deploy means: read-only, report, local-fs-analysis, and in-repo maker-checker loops **deploy and start themselves**. It does **not** authorize a loop whose *steady-state action* is destructive or outward-facing. If the compiled loop would, on its own, repeatedly: - place **live** trades, or flip a paper/live flag - `git push` to a shared branch (main/master/develop/release/*), or force-push - mutate secrets / `.env` / 1Password - delete or mass-move files (always archive, never delete) - restart a prod service (engine, Hermes gateway) unguarded - send messages to **third parties** (email/DM to people who aren't Amo) then **do not auto-deploy it live**. Instead: compile it fully, register it with `status=blocked`, deploy it in **report-only / dry-run** mode (or gate the mutating step behind a flag defaulting OFF), and surface the gate to Amo with the `PROPOSING_DESTRUCTIVE_OP` marker. The loop's dangerous step still hits the machine's PreToolUse hooks as a second line of defense — but the design-time gate is yours to hold. Everything else deploys. When in doubt between "useful cadence report" and "outward action", ship the report and let Amo pull the trigger on the action. --- ## Anti-patterns | Anti-pattern | Why it's wrong | Do instead | |---|---|---| | Deploy without a stop condition | infinite loop / runaway spend | Stage 2 done predicate is mandatory | | Green on error (swallow exceptions) | silent failure looks healthy | fail-closed: RED + notify + non-zero exit | | Cloud routine that reads `C:\Users\mattm\` | sandbox can't see local fs — fails silently | local-scheduled for anything local | | Self-grading evaluator loop | grades its own homework, never converges | independent judge / adversarial checker | | Night-time scheduled task (00:00-05:59) | machine asleep → 0xFFFD0000 | schedule 09:00-11:00 (Stage 6) | | One loop per file / per finding | fleet noise | group related work into one loop | | `git add -A` inside a runner | sweeps the 1,450-file backlog | stage per-file, pathspec commit | | Skipping Register | loop invisible + unkillable from the board | always Register, even in-session/workflow | --- ## Dogfood examples (shapes, not prescriptions) - "keep an eye on the self-healing scheduled tasks and ping me if one stays red" → **scheduled-cadence**, local-scheduled, daily 10:00, report-only, notify on red. Safe → auto-deploy. - "get the MES VWAP strategy's paper Sharpe above 0.5" → **evaluator-optimizer**, in-session/Workflow, metric ledger, independent gate-v2 judge, cap 20 rounds. Backtest-only → auto-deploy; any live wiring is Amo-gated. - "review every open PR for the exec-path stack and verify findings" → **fan-out-verify**, Workflow, adversarial verify stage. Read-only → auto-deploy. - "watch for the Vertex quota grant and flip the engine to Vertex-primary" → **dynamic**, poller; but the flip mutates engine config → deploy the *watch* live, **gate the flip** (notify Amo when granted). --- ## Cross-references - Brakes library + heartbeat: `jarvis-trader/scripts/loops/loop-lib.ps1` - Loop archetypes in the wild: `/ralph` (backlog), `/jarvis-loop` (discovery), `/loop` (dynamic) - Runner pitfalls (shim paths, battery gate, ASCII, localhost): `~/.claude/rules/windows-pitfalls.md` - Scheduling triage (local vs cloud): `~/.claude/rules/workflow.md` § Scheduling - Verify-before-claiming: `~/.claude/rules/verification.md` - Destructive-op gate: `~/.claude/rules/destructive-op-gates.md` ARGUMENTS: Compile a daily gbrain self-maintenance loop. Local scheduled task, 09:00-11:00 window (machine asleep at night per windows-pitfalls), ASCII-only PS 5.1 runner, all six brakes. Each run works against the gbrain daemon at http://127.0.0.1:8077: (1) PREFLIGHT: GET /health; abort clean (no-op exit 0) if the daemon is down or an ingest/sync is already running. (2) WORK: POST /auto-link {dry_run:false} to incrementally attach semantic edges to any orphan pages (DB-only, reversible via DELETE WHERE link_type='semantic', idempotent via ON CONFLICT); it returns 202, so poll GET /auto-link until running=false (bounded by a max-runtime cap), then read the result summary (orphans, edgesApplied, pagesLinked, totalPages). (3) REPORT: write a report with corpus size, orphan count, edges added this run, and the stale_minutes freshness; heartbeat GREEN/RED via loopctl. (4) FEEDBACK: compare edgesApplied + orphan count vs the previous run's report (delta). Fail-closed: any error or auto-link last_error => RED + Send-LoopNote to JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK + non-zero exit. Notify only on RED/transition, not steady GREEN. This is DB-only + reversible so it fits the auto-deploy safety envelope. Id suggestion: gbrain-nightly-maintenance. Reuse the loop-lib/scheduled-runner brakes. Note as a known v1 limitation that a full pass re-scans the ~966 sub-threshold orphans each run (a few minutes of daemon-busy in the maintenance window); a since-last-run / skip-unlinkable optimization is a future enhancement.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map, list_code_components, get_code_component_info)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

<#
  start-brain-daemon.ps1 -- launch the single-writer gbrain brain daemon (M1 read + M3 write).

  Owns the ONE PGlite connection for the trading brain and the embed key (Voyage), resolved from the
  durable DPAPI secret store -- no 1Password app at runtime. Everything else talks to it over HTTP.

  Idempotent: if a daemon already holds the port it is a no-op success, so the at-logon task AND the
  watchdog (install-brain-daemon-task.ps1) can both re-run it without ever spawning a second opener
  -- the lock-collision this whole daemon exists to delete.

  -Detached : start the daemon hidden + return immediately (used by the scheduled tasks; logs ->
              ~/.gbrain-trading/logs). Without it, runs in the foreground; Ctrl-C releases the lock
              cleanly (daemon traps SIGINT/SIGTERM -> engine.disconnect()).
#>
param([switch]$Detached)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$bun         = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.bun\bin\bun.exe'
$daemon      = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\gbrain-src\src\daemon-server.ts'
$secretStore = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'tools\secret-store.ps1'
$logDir      = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\logs'

$env:GBRAIN_DATABASE_PATH    = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gbrain-trading\brain.pglite'
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_BASE_URL   = 'https://api.voyageai.com/v1'
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_MODEL      = 'voyage-finance-2'
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_DIMENSIONS = '1024'
if (-not $env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT) { $env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT = '8077' }

# Idempotent guard: if the port is already served, another daemon owns the lock -> do nothing.
$port = [int]$env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT
if (Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port $port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue) {
  Write-Host "[start-brain-daemon] daemon already listening on $port - nothing to do."
  exit 0
}

# Resolve the Voyage key from the durable DPAPI store (no 1Password app dependency at runtime).
$key = & pwsh -NoProfile -File $secretStore -Get VOYAGE_API_KEY 2>$null
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($key)) {
  Write-Error "VOYAGE_API_KEY not in secret store. Seed it once: pwsh $secretStore -Import VOYAGE_API_KEY -FromFile <one-line-key.txt>"
  exit 2
}
$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_API_KEY = $key

Write-Host "[start-brain-daemon] port=$env:GBRAIN_DAEMON_PORT  brain=$env:GBRAIN_DATABASE_PATH  model=$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_MODEL/$env:GBRAIN_EMBED_DIMENSIONS  detached=$Detached"

if ($Detached) {
  if (-not (Test-Path $logDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logDir -Force | Out-Null }
  $out = Join-Path $logDir 'daemon.out.log'
  $err = Join-Path $logDir 'daemon.err.log'
  # bun.exe is a native exe (not a .cmd shim), so Start-Process -FilePath works. The detached child
  # inherits the GBRAIN_* env set above and survives this launcher exiting (that is the point).
  # PIN the working directory to a durable dir: WITHOUT this the daemon inherits the launcher's cwd
  # (often a temp/worktree). If that dir is later deleted, the daemon stays up + /health green, but
  # execFileSync('git', ...) in /sync can no longer spawn (Windows CreateProcess can't resolve a dead
  # cwd) -- every git op then fails and is mis-reported as "No commits in repo" (observed 2026-05-30,
  # daemon pid 48728). $USERPROFILE never vanishes, so this deletes that failure class.
  Start-Process -FilePath $bun -ArgumentList @('run', "`"$daemon`"") -WindowStyle Hidden `
    -WorkingDirectory $env:USERPROFILE `
    -RedirectStandardOutput $out -RedirectStandardError $err
  Write-Host "[start-brain-daemon] launched detached; logs -> $logDir"
  exit 0
}
& $bun run $daemon

## Theme A -- what shipped (semantic auto-linker)

New daemon endpoint `POST /auto-link` in `C:\Users\mattm\tools\gbrain-src\src\daemon-server.ts`
(functions `runAutoLink` + `pickEmbedding`). For each **orphan** page (no outgoing links), take its
representative chunk embedding (prefers a compiled_truth chunk) and run the daemon's OWN
`searchVector` (cosine `<=>`), then `addLink(orphan, target, "auto:semantic score=<s>", "semantic")`
for the top K=5 distinct targets scoring >= 0.78. Reuses `listPages` / `getLinks` / `getChunks` /
`getEmbeddingsByChunkIds` / `searchVector` / `addLink` -- **no new similarity code**.

- **DB-only + reversible:** writes ONLY the `links` table with `link_type='semantic'` (never touches
  vault `.md` files). Entire pass reverses with `DELETE FROM links WHERE link_type='semantic'`.
  `addLink` is `ON CONFLICT (from,to) DO UPDATE` so re-runs are idempotent.

  JSON-round-trippable over `/rpc`). Each engine call self-serializes via the daemon proxy, so `/search`

  cosine over every chunk embedding in single-threaded WASM PGlite; `/search` does one per request, but this

  the same `ingest` busy-state as `/ingest`+`/sync` (POST returns 202, poll `GET /auto-link`), so `/health`
  fast-paths; (2) `await`-yield the event loop between orphans so liveness probes interleave. With both, a
  full pass stays reachable the whole time.

<#
  Loopify runner: gbrain-maintenance  -- ASCII-only, PS 5.1-safe.
  Daily self-maintenance for the gbrain brain: incrementally attach semantic edges to orphan
  pages so the graph stays navigable (graph_recall/traverseGraph can walk from new pages).

  Archetype: scheduled-cadence. LOCAL only. Writes ONLY semantic edges into the pglite links
  table (link_type='semantic') -- DB-only, reversible (DELETE ... WHERE link_type='semantic'),
  idempotent (addLink ON CONFLICT). Never touches vault .md files, never restarts the daemon.

  All six brakes: preflight (daemon up + not mid-ingest), heartbeat, fail-closed, runtime cap,
  single-run budget, notify-on-RED. Notifies only on RED/transition, not steady GREEN.

  v1 LIMITATION: a full pass re-scans every orphan (incl. the ~966 with no neighbour >= threshold),
  a few minutes of daemon-busy in the maintenance window. A since-last-run / skip-unlinkable filter
  is a future enhancement.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Id = 'gbrain-maintenance',
    [int]    $MaxRuntimeSec = 600,          # brake 4/5: hard wall-clock cap for one fire
    [double] $Threshold = 0.78,             # min cosine to attach a semantic edge
    [int]    $K = 5                          # max edges per orphan
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$loopctl  = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loopctl.ps1'
$loopHeal = 'C:\Users\mattm\scripts\loop-heal.ps1'
$FailBudget = 3
$Endpoint = 'http://127.0.0.1:8077'
# loop-heal.ps1 has its own param() block; dot-sourcing re-runs it and clobbers $Id. Save + restore.
$__Id = $Id
if (Test-Path $loopHeal) { . $loopHeal }
$Id = $__Id
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

$LoopDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\loops\gbrain-maintenance'
if (-not (Test-Path $LoopDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $LoopDir -Force | Out-Null }

function Send-LoopNote {
    param([string] $Text)
    $hook = $env:JARVIS_LOOP_WEBHOOK
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($hook)) { return }
    try {
        $body = @{ content = "[$Id] $Text" } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $hook -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null
    } catch { }
}

function Test-Preflight {
    # Brake 1: daemon reachable, healthy, and NOT mid-ingest (auto-link 409s during a sync).
    try {
        $h = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/health" -Method Get -TimeoutSec 8
        if (-not $h.ok) { $script:PreWhy = 'daemon /health not ok'; return $false }
        if ($h.ingest -and $h.ingest.running) { $script:PreWhy = "ingest/sync running (phase=$($h.ingest.phase))"; return $false }
        return $true
    } catch { $script:PreWhy = "daemon unreachable: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return $false }
}

try {
    if (-not (Test-Preflight)) {
        & $loopctl -Action Heartbeat -Id $Id -State GREEN     # dep down / busy is not an error; abort clean
        Write-Output "PREFLIGHT: $script:PreWhy -- skipping this fire (no-op)."
        exit 0
    }

    # ================= WORK: incremental semantic auto-link =================
    $prevFile = Join-Path $LoopDir 'last-result.json'
    $prev = $null
    if (Test-Path $prevFile) { try { $prev = Get-Content $prevFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json } catch {} }

    $headers = @{ 'Content-Type' = 'application/json' }
    $reqBody = @{ dry_run = $false; threshold = $Threshold; k = $K } | ConvertTo-Json
    $post = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/auto-link" -Method Post -Headers $headers -Body $reqBody -TimeoutSec 15
    if (-not $post.accepted) { throw "auto-link not accepted: $($post.error)" }

    # Poll async completion, bounded by the runtime cap (the daemon stays alive via its event-loop yield).
    $st = $null
    do {
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
        if ($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt $MaxRuntimeSec) { throw "runtime cap $MaxRuntimeSec s exceeded while polling auto-link" }
        $st = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/auto-link" -Method Get -TimeoutSec 10
    } while ($st.running)
    if ($st.last_error) { throw "auto-link reported error: $($st.last_error)" }
    $last = $st.last
    if (-not $last) { throw "auto-link completed but returned no result summary" }

    # Freshness (Task-1 metric) for the report.
    $stale = $null
    try { $h2 = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$Endpoint/health" -Method Get -TimeoutSec 8; if ($h2.ingest) { $stale = $h2.ingest.stale_minutes } } catch {}

    # Feedback: delta vs previous run.
    $dEdges = ''; $dOrph = ''
    if ($prev) {
        if ($null -ne $prev.edgesApplied) { $dEdges = " (prev $($prev.edgesApplied))" }

## Theme B -- what shipped (episodic memory layer)  [#2 of the 1-4 ladder]

gbrain's third memory layer (semantic pages + graph links + **episodic timeline**) shipped fully wired
but empty: `timeline_entry_count = 0`. The stock `extract timeline` producer only matches two markdown
patterns (`- **YYYY-MM-DD** | src -- summary` and `### YYYY-MM-DD -- title`) the corpus doesn't use --
measured **1 entry from 444 memory files**. So the layer needed a **corpus-aware producer**.

New producer `C:\Users\mattm\tools\gbrain-episodic-backfill.ts` (bun; talks to the daemon's existing
`/rpc` -- **no daemon change, no restart**). For each dated memory file (`*_YYYY_MM_DD.md`, the date is
in the filename and the file is already a page), it writes one timeline entry to a single canonical
synthetic page **`jarvis-session-journal`**, so the brain gains a queryable cross-topic **chronology**
via `getTimeline(after,before)`. `summary` = the file's frontmatter `description` (fallback: first
heading / humanized slug); `source = memory:<slug>` keeps provenance.

- **RESULT (applied 2026-07-01):** **309 dated events**, range **2026-03-04 .. 2026-07-01**;
  `timeline_entry_count` 0 -> 309. `getTimeline('jarvis-session-journal',{after,before})` returns the
  correct date-ordered slice with source slugs (verified for the 06-28..07-01 window).
- **Idempotent:** dedup on `date::summary`. FIRST cut had a bug -- `getTimeline` returns `date` as a full
  ISO string (`2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z`) but planned keys are `YYYY-MM-DD`, so the re-run key never

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UserPromptSubmit hook: auto-inject relevant knowledge from the gbrain daemon.

On every user prompt (all sessions, global registration in ~/.claude/settings.json),
query the gbrain knowledge daemon (127.0.0.1:8077) with the prompt text and inject the
top score-gated hits into Claude's context as `additionalContext`. This is how Claude
"continuously learns" from everything Amo has bookmarked/saved -- relevant knowledge
becomes ambient context automatically, with no manual recall.

Whole-brain (not bookmarks-only): the corpus is the full embedded vault + X/Discord
bookmarks. A relevance floor (GBRAIN_INJECT_MIN_SCORE) keeps only genuinely-relevant hits.

FAIL-OPEN: any error (daemon down, timeout, malformed) -> print nothing, exit 0. The hook
must never block or delay a prompt because the brain is unavailable.

stdlib only (runs under system Python 3.14 like check_alerts.py). No third-party deps.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime

DAEMON_URL = os.environ.get("GBRAIN_INJECT_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8077").rstrip("/")
TIMEOUT_S = float(os.environ.get("GBRAIN_INJECT_TIMEOUT", "4"))
MIN_SCORE = float(os.environ.get("GBRAIN_INJECT_MIN_SCORE", "0.55"))
TOP_N = int(os.environ.get("GBRAIN_INJECT_TOP", "3"))
SEARCH_LIMIT = int(os.environ.get("GBRAIN_INJECT_LIMIT", "8"))
LOG_PATH = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/hooks/inject_knowledge.log")

HEADER = (
    "From your knowledge brain (auto-recalled -- use only if relevant to the request):"
)

# Bare control words / affirmations that carry no recall signal.
SKIP_WORDS = {
    "yes",
    "no",
    "ok",
    "okay",
    "y",
    "n",
    "yep",
    "yeah",
    "sure",
    "go",
    "do it",
    "proceed",
    "continue",
    "thanks",
    "thank you",
    "ty",
    "stop",
    "wait",
    "next",
    "more",
    "again",
    "retry",
    "redo",
    "undo",
    "skip",
    "done",
    "good",
    "great",
    "nice",
    "perfect",
    "cool",
    "hmm",
    "k",
    "kk",
}


def should_skip(prompt: str) -> bool:
    p = (prompt or "").strip()
    if len(p) < 16:
        return True
    if p[0] in ("/", "!"):
        return True
    if p.lower() in SKIP_WORDS:
        return True
    # Recursion guard: don't re-search on our own injected block.
    if HEADER[:32] in p:
        return True
    return False


def search(prompt: str):
    payload = json.dumps({"query": prompt, "opts": {"limit": SEARCH_LIMIT}}).encode(
        "utf-8"
    )
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{DAEMON_URL}/search",
        data=payload,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT_S) as r:
        data = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    return data.get("results") or []


def label_for(hit: dict) -> str:
    """Per-tweet cards have weak titles ('Handle <tweet-id>') -> prefer a snippet."""
    title = (hit.get("title") or "").strip()
    weak = (not title) or len(title) < 6 or title[-1:].isdigit()
    if weak:
        snippet = " ".join((hit.get("chunk_text") or "").split())[:140]
        if snippet:
            return snippet
    return title or "(untitled)"


def select(results):
    """Score-gate, dedup by slug, take top N. Whole-brain (no slug filter)."""
    seen = set()
    picked = []
    for hit in results:
        score = hit.get("score")
        if not isinstance(score, (int, float)) or score < MIN_SCORE:
            continue
        slug = hit.get("slug") or ""
        if slug in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(slug)
        picked.append(hit)
        if len(picked) >= TOP_N:
            break
    return picked


def render(picked) -> str:
    lines = [HEADER]
    for hit in picked:
        score = hit.get("score") or 0.0
        slug = hit.get("slug") or ""
        tag = " [bookmark]" if "bookmark" in slug else ""
        lines.append(f"  [{score:.2f}]{tag} {label_for(hit)}\n    ({slug})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def log(session_id, prompt, picked):
    try:
        sid = (session_id or "?")[:8]
        slugs = [h.get("slug") for h in picked]
        line = (
            f'{datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")} {sid} '
            f'q="{(prompt or "")[:60]}" injected={len(picked)} slugs={slugs}\n'
        )
        with open(LOG_PATH, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(line)
    except Exception:
        pass


def main():
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.read()
        event = json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}
    except Exception:
        return  # no parsable input -> fail open
    # Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit event uses "prompt"; older/other schemas used
    # "user_prompt". Read both so the hook actually fires (it was silently dead --
    # reading only "user_prompt" meant real prompts arrived empty -> skipped).
    prompt = event.get("prompt") or event.get("user_prompt") or ""
    session_id = event.get("session_id", "")
    if should_skip(prompt):
        return
    try:
        results = search(prompt)
    except Exception:
        return  # daemon down / timeout -> fail open, never block the prompt
    picked = select(results)
    if not picked:
        log(session_id, prompt, picked)
        return
    out = {
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit",
            "additionalContext": render(picked),
        }
    }
    log(session_id, prompt, picked)
    print(json.dumps(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text: The log confirms two distinct precision problems (though it doesn't record scores — itself a tuning gap I'll fix): (1) **low-signal prompts still trigger recall** — `<task-notification>` XML and "proceed with recommended next steps" pulled in a GMS roll-forming ERP page; (2) the **0.55 floor is too low**. To pick the floor empirically I need the actual score distribution of relevant vs tangential hits. Probing representative queries with scores:

\$b='http://127.0.0.1:8077'

  \$r=Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \$b/search -Method Post -Body \$body -ContentType 'application/json' -TimeoutSec 30

"""RAG-eval harness for the auto-recall hook (inject_knowledge.py).

Runs the golden set (gbrain_recall_golden.json) against the live gbrain daemon and reports, per
score-floor, the metrics that actually matter for auto-recall:

  - recall  : fraction of POSITIVE queries whose expected slug appears in the injected top-N
  - clean   : fraction of NEGATIVE queries that correctly inject NOTHING (precision on the
              ERP-leak false-positive class -- higher is better)
  - injected: how many hits a query would inject (for eyeballing)

It imports inject_knowledge's OWN should_skip/select so the eval matches production exactly. Sweep the
floor to pick it empirically; run before/after a hook change to prove the change helps and to
regression-guard recall quality across re-embeds.

Usage:
  python gbrain_recall_eval.py                 # sweep floors 0.45..0.65, table
  python gbrain_recall_eval.py --floor 0.55    # single floor, verbose per-query
  python gbrain_recall_eval.py --json          # machine-readable

stdlib only (system Python 3.14, like the hook).
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import importlib.util

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
GOLDEN = os.path.join(HERE, "gbrain_recall_golden.json")

# Import the production hook module so we reuse its exact should_skip / search / select logic.
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("inject_knowledge", os.path.join(HERE, "inject_knowledge.py"))
hook = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(hook)


def select_at(results, floor, top_n):
    """Mirror hook.select but with an explicit floor/top_n (so we can sweep without env mutation)."""
    seen, picked = set(), []
    for hit in results:
        score = hit.get("score")
        if not isinstance(score, (int, float)) or score < floor:
            continue
        slug = hit.get("slug") or ""
        if slug in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(slug)
        picked.append(hit)
        if len(picked) >= top_n:
            break
    return picked


def evaluate(golden, floor, top_n, verbose=False):
    pos = golden.get("positives", [])
    neg = golden.get("negatives", [])
    recall_hits = 0
    clean = 0
    rows = []
    for case in pos:
        q, want = case["query"], case["expect_slug_substr"]
        skipped = hook.should_skip(q)
        picked = [] if skipped else select_at(hook.search(q), floor, top_n)
        slugs = [h.get("slug", "") for h in picked]
        hit = any(want in s for s in slugs)
        recall_hits += 1 if hit else 0
        rows.append(("POS", "HIT" if hit else ("SKIP" if skipped else "MISS"), q[:44], slugs))
    for case in neg:
        q = case["query"]
        skipped = hook.should_skip(q)
        picked = [] if skipped else select_at(hook.search(q), floor, top_n)
        slugs = [h.get("slug", "") for h in picked]
        is_clean = len(picked) == 0
        clean += 1 if is_clean else 0
        rows.append(("NEG", "CLEAN" if is_clean else "LEAK", q[:44], slugs))
    if verbose:
        for kind, verdict, q, slugs in rows:
            print(f"  {kind} {verdict:5} | {q:44} -> {slugs}")
    return {
        "floor": round(floor, 3),
        "recall": f"{recall_hits}/{len(pos)}",
        "recall_pct": round(100 * recall_hits / max(1, len(pos))),
        "clean_neg": f"{clean}/{len(neg)}",
        "clean_pct": round(100 * clean / max(1, len(neg))),
    }


def main():
    with open(GOLDEN, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        golden = json.load(f)
    top_n = int(os.environ.get("GBRAIN_INJECT_TOP", "3"))
    json_mode = "--json" in sys.argv
    if "--floor" in sys.argv:
        floor = float(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--floor") + 1])
        res = evaluate(golden, floor, top_n, verbose=not json_mode)
        print(json.dumps(res, indent=2) if json_mode else f"\nfloor={res['floor']}  recall={res['recall']} ({res['recall_pct']}%)  clean_neg={res['clean_neg']} ({res['clean_pct']}%)")
        return
    sweep = [0.45, 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65]
    results = [evaluate(golden, fl, top_n) for fl in sweep]
    if json_mode:
        print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
        return
    print(f"\ngbrain auto-recall eval  (top_n={top_n}, golden={len(golden.get('positives',[]))} pos / {len(golden.get('negatives',[]))} neg)")
    print(f"  {'floor':<7}{'recall':<14}{'clean_neg (precision)':<24}")
    for r in results:
        print(f"  {r['floor']:<7}{r['recall']+' ('+str(r['recall_pct'])+'%)':<14}{r['clean_neg']+' ('+str(r['clean_pct'])+'%)':<24}")
    print("\n  recall = expected slug surfaced in top-N; clean_neg = low-signal query injected NOTHING (higher=better).")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""RAG-eval harness for the auto-recall hook (inject_knowledge.py).

Runs the golden set (gbrain_recall_golden.json) against the live gbrain daemon and reports, per
score-floor, the metrics that actually matter for auto-recall:

  - recall  : fraction of POSITIVE queries whose expected slug appears in the injected top-N
  - clean   : fraction of NEGATIVE queries that correctly inject NOTHING (precision on the
              ERP-leak false-positive class -- higher is better)
  - injected: how many hits a query would inject (for eyeballing)

It imports inject_knowledge's OWN should_skip/select so the eval matches production exactly. Sweep the
floor to pick it empirically; run before/after a hook change to prove the change helps and to
regression-guard recall quality across re-embeds.

Usage:
  python gbrain_recall_eval.py                 # sweep floors 0.45..0.65, table
  python gbrain_recall_eval.py --floor 0.55    # single floor, verbose per-query
  python gbrain_recall_eval.py --json          # machine-readable

stdlib only (system Python 3.14, like the hook).
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import importlib.util

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
GOLDEN = os.path.join(HERE, "gbrain_recall_golden.json")

# Import the production hook module so we reuse its exact should_skip / search / select logic.
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "inject_knowledge", os.path.join(HERE, "inject_knowledge.py")
)
hook = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(hook)


def select_at(results, floor, top_n):
    """Mirror hook.select but with an explicit floor/top_n (so we can sweep without env mutation)."""
    seen, picked = set(), []
    for hit in results:
        score = hit.get("score")
        if not isinstance(score, (int, float)) or score < floor:
            continue
        slug = hit.get("slug") or ""
        if slug in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(slug)
        picked.append(hit)
        if len(picked) >= top_n:
            break
    return picked


def evaluate(golden, floor, top_n, verbose=False):
    pos = golden.get("positives", [])
    neg = golden.get("negatives", [])
    recall_hits = 0
    clean = 0
    rows = []
    for case in pos:
        q, want = case["query"], case["expect_slug_substr"]
        skipped = hook.should_skip(q)
        picked = [] if skipped else select_at(hook.search(q), floor, top_n)
        slugs = [h.get("slug", "") for h in picked]
        hit = any(want in s for s in slugs)
        recall_hits += 1 if hit else 0
        rows.append(
            ("POS", "HIT" if hit else ("SKIP" if skipped else "MISS"), q[:44], slugs)
        )
    for case in neg:
        q = case["query"]
        skipped = hook.should_skip(q)
        picked = [] if skipped else select_at(hook.search(q), floor, top_n)
        slugs = [h.get("slug", "") for h in picked]
        is_clean = len(picked) == 0
        clean += 1 if is_clean else 0
        rows.append(("NEG", "CLEAN" if is_clean else "LEAK", q[:44], slugs))
    if verbose:
        for kind, verdict, q, slugs in rows:
            print(f"  {kind} {verdict:5} | {q:44} -> {slugs}")

        "floor": round(floor, 3),
        "recall": f"{recall_hits}/{len(pos)}",

        "clean_neg": f"{clean}/{len(neg)}",
        "clean_pct": round(100 * clean / max(1, len(neg))),
    }

        )

        "\n  recall = expected slug surfaced in top-N; clean_neg = low-signal query injected NOTHING (higher=better)."
    )
